items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 世（せ）＋界（かい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Generations (世) bounded (界): the whole world.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The people of one <kanji>generation</kanji>, sealed together inside a single <kanji>boundary</kanji> of years, all live in one <vocabulary>world</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 世界で一番高い山はどこですか。
example_sentences.english: Where is the tallest mountain in the world?
example_sentences.furigana: 世[せ]界[かい]で一[いち]番[ばん]高[たか]い山[やま]はどこですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は船で世界を旅行しました。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather traveled around the world by ship.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は船[ふね]で世[せ]界[かい]を旅[りょ]行[こう]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は地図を見ながら、世界の海の名前を覚えています。
example_sentences.english: My daughter is memorizing the names of the world's oceans while looking at a map.
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]は地[ち]図[ず]を見[み]ながら、世[せ]界[かい]の海[うみ]の名[な]前[まえ]を覚[おぼ]えています。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 政（せい）＋治（じ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Governing (政) and ordering (治): politics.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <vocabulary>Politics</vocabulary> is the whole endless job of trying to <kanji>govern</kanji> a country full of shouting people and somehow get them to <kanji>calm down</kanji>.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父は政治の話が好きなので、晩ご飯が長くなります。
example_sentences.english: My uncle loves talking politics, so dinner always runs long.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔父[おじ]は政[せい]治[じ]の話[はなし]が好[す]きなので、晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]が長[なが]くなります。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は政治のことがあまり分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I don't really understand much about politics.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は政[せい]治[じ]のことがあまり分[わ]かりません。

example_sentences.japanese: 大学で政治を勉強したいと思っています。
example_sentences.english: I'm thinking I'd like to study politics at university.
example_sentences.furigana: 大[だい]学[がく]で政[せい]治[じ]を勉[べん]強[きょう]したいと思[おも]っています。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 意（い）＋見（けん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A meaning (意) that you see (見): your opinion.
items.meaning_mnemonic: An <kanji>idea</kanji> stuck on loop in your heart only turns into an <vocabulary>opinion</vocabulary> once you make other people <kanji>see</kanji> it too.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議で自分の意見を言うのは難しいです。
example_sentences.english: It's hard to give your own opinion in a meeting.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]で自[じ]分[ぶん]の意[い]見[けん]を言[い]うのは難[むずか]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生はみんなの意見を聞いてから、答えを教えてくれました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher heard everyone's opinions first, then told us the answer.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]はみんなの意[い]見[けん]を聞[き]いてから、答[こた]えを教[おし]えてくれました。

example_sentences.japanese: 姉に電話して、意見を聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I called my older sister and asked for her opinion.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]に電[でん]話[わ]して、意[い]見[けん]を聞[き]きました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 文（ぶん）＋化（か）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Writing (文) that transforms (化) a people: culture.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The slow <kanji>change</kanji> that a people's <kanji>style</kanji> of dress, food and speech goes through over centuries is their <vocabulary>culture</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国人の友達に日本の文化を紹介しました。
example_sentences.english: I introduced Japanese culture to a friend from abroad.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]人[じん]の友[とも]達[だち]に日本[にほん]の文[ぶん]化[か]を紹[しょう]介[かい]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 外国の文化を知るために、よく映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I often watch movies to learn about other cultures.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]の文[ぶん]化[か]を知[し]るために、よく映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: この町には古い文化が残っています。
example_sentences.english: This town still keeps its old culture.
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]には古[ふる]い文[ぶん]化[か]が残[のこ]っています。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 伝（でん）＋統（とう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Passed down (伝) and unified (統): tradition.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When one <kanji>overall</kanji> way of doing things is <kanji>transmit</kanji>ted from each parent to each child for ten generations without a gap, that unbroken handoff is <vocabulary>tradition</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎年、祖母と伝統の料理を作ります。
example_sentences.english: Every year I make traditional dishes with my grandmother.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]年[ねん]、祖[そ]母[ぼ]と伝[でん]統[とう]の料[りょう]理[り]を作[つく]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: この店には百年の伝統があります。
example_sentences.english: This shop has a hundred years of tradition.
example_sentences.furigana: この店[みせ]には百[ひゃく]年[ねん]の伝[でん]統[とう]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 若い人は、あまり伝統の服を着なくなりました。
example_sentences.english: Young people don't wear traditional clothes much anymore.
example_sentences.furigana: 若[わか]い人[ひと]は、あまり伝[でん]統[とう]の服[ふく]を着[き]なくなりました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 社（しゃ）＋会（かい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A shrine (社) gathering (会) of people: society.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every <kanji>company</kanji> and shrine keeps its gates open, and the crowds who <kanji>meet</kanji> and mingle between them are what we call a <vocabulary>society</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は春から社会に出ます。
example_sentences.english: My son goes out into the working world this spring.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]は春[はる]から社[しゃ]会[かい]に出[で]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 社会はだんだん便利になりました。
example_sentences.english: Society has gradually become more convenient.
example_sentences.furigana: 社[しゃ]会[かい]はだんだん便[べん]利[り]になりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 社会のために働く人になりたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to become someone who works for the good of society.
example_sentences.furigana: 社[しゃ]会[かい]のために働[はたら]く人[ひと]になりたいです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 国（こく）＋際（さい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Countries (国) meeting at the border (際): international.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Anything that happens right on the <kanji>edge</kanji> where one <kanji>country</kanji>'s wall butts against the next one's is, by definition, <vocabulary>international</vocabulary>.
items.description: Almost always used stuck in front of another noun, the way a label is, rather than standing on its own as a full noun.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は国際会議で英語を話しました。
example_sentences.english: She spoke English at an international conference.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は国[こく]際[さい]会[かい]議[ぎ]で英[えい]語[ご]を話[はな]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は国際問題の本をたくさん読んでいます。
example_sentences.english: My older brother reads lots of books on international issues.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は国[こく]際[さい]問[もん]題[だい]の本[ほん]をたくさん読[よ]んでいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 国際社会の中で、日本は何ができるでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: What can Japan do within the international community?
example_sentences.furigana: 国[こく]際[さい]社[しゃ]会[かい]の中[なか]で、日本[にほん]は何[なに]ができるでしょうか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 政（せい）＋府（ふ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Governance's (政) storehouse (府): the government.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pile every <kanji>government office</kanji> in the country into one enormous building, and whoever ends up running that building is the <vocabulary>government</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 政府は町に新しい病院を作ります。
example_sentences.english: The government is going to build a new hospital in the town.
example_sentences.furigana: 政[せい]府[ふ]は町[まち]に新[あたら]しい病[びょう]院[いん]を作[つく]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母は政府の仕事をしています。
example_sentences.english: My aunt works for the government.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔母[おば]は政[せい]府[ふ]の仕[し]事[ごと]をしています。

example_sentences.japanese: 政府の意見に反対する人も多いです。
example_sentences.english: Plenty of people disagree with the government's view.
example_sentences.furigana: 政[せい]府[ふ]の意[い]見[けん]に反[はん]対[たい]する人[ひと]も多[おお]いです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 法（ほう）＋律（りつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A rule (法) set in rhythm (律): the law.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every rule the whole country has agreed to write down and back with courts, police and prisons, instead of leaving it to a friendly handshake, is <vocabulary>law</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 法律で、ここに車を止めてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: By law, you can't park your car here.
example_sentences.furigana: 法[ほう]律[りつ]で、ここに車[くるま]を止[と]めてはいけません。

example_sentences.japanese: 法律の本は、言葉がとても難しいです。
example_sentences.english: The words in law books are really difficult.
example_sentences.furigana: 法[ほう]律[りつ]の本[ほん]は、言[こと]葉[ば]がとても難[むずか]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 来月から法律が変わるので、会社は準備しています。
example_sentences.english: The law changes next month, so the company is getting ready.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]月[げつ]から法[ほう]律[りつ]が変[か]わるので、会[かい]社[しゃ]は準[じゅん]備[び]しています。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 権（けん）＋利（り）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Authority (権) that benefits (利): a right.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>benefit</kanji> the law guarantees you from birth, one that no ruler or vote is allowed to strip away, is a <vocabulary>right (entitlement)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供にも遊ぶ権利があります。
example_sentences.english: Children have the right to play, too.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]にも遊[あそ]ぶ権[けん]利[り]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 働く人には休む権利があります。
example_sentences.english: Working people have the right to rest.
example_sentences.furigana: 働[はたら]く人[ひと]には休[やす]む権[けん]利[り]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: お金を払ったので、私たちにはこの席に座る権利があります。
example_sentences.english: We paid, so we have every right to sit in these seats.
example_sentences.furigana: お金[かね]を払[はら]ったので、私[わたし]たちにはこの席[せき]に座[すわ]る権[けん]利[り]があります。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 義（ぎ）＋務（む）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Righteousness (義) that must be worked (務): a duty.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When plain <kanji>morality</kanji>, not your boss, is what hands you a <kanji>task</kanji>, that unpaid assignment is a <vocabulary>duty / obligation</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校を掃除するのは学生の義務です。
example_sentences.english: Cleaning the school is the students' duty.
example_sentences.furigana: 学[がっ]校[こう]を掃[そう]除[じ]するのは学[がく]生[せい]の義[ぎ]務[む]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は家族を手伝う義務があります。
example_sentences.english: The son has a duty to help his family.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]は家[か]族[ぞく]を手伝[てつだ]う義[ぎ]務[む]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 義務を忘れる人もいます。
example_sentences.english: There are also people who forget their duties.
example_sentences.furigana: 義[ぎ]務[む]を忘[わす]れる人[ひと]もいます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 新（しん）＋聞（ぶん）＋社（しゃ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The newspaper (新聞) company (社).
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>company</kanji> whose one job is to <kanji>hear</kanji> what happened overnight and rush it into print while the news is still <kanji>new</kanji> is a <vocabulary>newspaper company</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は新聞社で働いています。
example_sentences.english: My older brother works at a newspaper company.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は新[しん]聞[ぶん]社[しゃ]で働[はたら]いています。

example_sentences.japanese: 姉はその新聞社で働きたいです。
example_sentences.english: My older sister wants to work at that newspaper company.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]はその新[しん]聞[ぶん]社[しゃ]で働[はたら]きたいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 新聞社の人が学校に来ました。
example_sentences.english: Someone from the newspaper company came to the school.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[しん]聞[ぶん]社[しゃ]の人[ひと]が学[がっ]校[こう]に来[き]ました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 企（き）＋業（ぎょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Planning (企) an occupation (業): a company.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A tree-stump <kanji>business</kanji> that someone <kanji>scheme</kanji>s up into offices, payroll and a logo has grown into an <vocabulary>enterprise / business</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: あの企業はとても有名です。
example_sentences.english: That enterprise is very famous.
example_sentences.furigana: あの企[き]業[ぎょう]はとても有[ゆう]名[めい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はその企業に入りたいです。
example_sentences.english: He wants to join that enterprise.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]はその企[き]業[ぎょう]に入[はい]りたいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい企業が駅の近くにできました。
example_sentences.english: A new enterprise was built near the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい企[き]業[ぎょう]が駅[えき]の近[ちか]くにできました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 貿（ぼう）＋易（えき）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Goods traded (貿) for a change (易): commerce.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Once two countries make it <kanji>easy</kanji> to swap whatever each of them has stacked up in surplus, that steady back-and-forth swapping is <vocabulary>trade (commerce)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は外国と貿易をしています。
example_sentences.english: Japan trades with foreign countries.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]は外[がい]国[こく]と貿[ぼう]易[えき]をしています。

example_sentences.japanese: 貿易の仕事はおもしろいです。
example_sentences.english: Trade work is interesting.
example_sentences.furigana: 貿[ぼう]易[えき]の仕[し]事[ごと]はおもしろいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は貿易の会社で働いています。
example_sentences.english: My father works at a trading company.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は貿[ぼう]易[えき]の会[かい]社[しゃ]で働[はたら]いています。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 輸（ゆ）＋出（しゅつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Transport (輸) that exits (出): to export.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Goods you <kanji>transport</kanji> to the country's <kanji>exit</kanji> and push out across the border are an <vocabulary>export</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社は野菜を輸出しています。
example_sentences.english: This company exports vegetables.
example_sentences.furigana: この会[かい]社[しゃ]は野[や]菜[さい]を輸[ゆ]出[しゅつ]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は車をたくさん輸出します。
example_sentences.english: Japan exports a lot of cars.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]は車[くるま]をたくさん輸[ゆ]出[しゅつ]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 貿易には輸出も輸入もあります。
example_sentences.english: Trade includes both exports and imports.
example_sentences.furigana: 貿[ぼう]易[えき]には輸[ゆ]出[しゅつ]も輸[ゆ]入[にゅう]もあります。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 輸（ゆ）＋入（にゅう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Transport (輸) that enters (入): to import.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When a cargo ship <kanji>send</kanji>s foreign goods across the sea and they <kanji>enter</kanji> your shops, what just landed is an <vocabulary>import</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は米をあまり輸入しません。
example_sentences.english: Japan doesn't import much rice.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]は米[こめ]をあまり輸[ゆ]入[にゅう]しません。

example_sentences.japanese: この店ではコーヒーを輸入しています。
example_sentences.english: This shop imports coffee.
example_sentences.furigana: この店[みせ]ではコーヒーを輸[ゆ]入[にゅう]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 輸入の服は高いです。
example_sentences.english: Imported clothes are expensive.
example_sentences.furigana: 輸[ゆ]入[にゅう]の服[ふく]は高[たか]いです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 税（ぜい）＋金（きん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Money (金) taken as tax (税): a tax.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The slice of everyone's <kanji>money</kanji> that the government quietly rakes off every year to pay for roads, schools and soldiers is <vocabulary>tax</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 税金を払うのは私たちの義務です。
example_sentences.english: Paying taxes is our duty.
example_sentences.furigana: 税[ぜい]金[きん]を払[はら]うのは私[わたし]たちの義[ぎ]務[む]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 税金を忘れると大変です。
example_sentences.english: If you forget about taxes, it becomes a big problem.
example_sentences.furigana: 税[ぜい]金[きん]を忘[わす]れると大[たい]変[へん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 税金が高すぎて困っています。
example_sentences.english: The taxes are too high, and it's a problem for me.
example_sentences.furigana: 税[ぜい]金[きん]が高[たか]すぎて困[こま]っています。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 価（か）＋格（かく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Value (価) given a fixed frame (格): the price.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every shop <kanji>rank</kanji>s its goods with a number on a little tag, and that number, the one every customer pays, is the <vocabulary>price</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 店で価格を見てからかばんを選びました。
example_sentences.english: I looked at the price at the store, then chose a bag.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[みせ]で価[か]格[かく]を見[み]てからかばんを選[えら]びました。

example_sentences.japanese: 店員が新しい価格を教えてくれました。
example_sentences.english: The shop clerk told me the new price.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]が新[あたら]しい価[か]格[かく]を教[おし]えてくれました。

example_sentences.japanese: このコートの価格はいくらですか。
example_sentences.english: How much is the price of this coat?
example_sentences.furigana: このコートの価[か]格[かく]はいくらですか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 市（し）＋場（じょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The city's (市) open place (場): a market.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Hand the awning-covered <kanji>market</kanji> one permanent <kanji>place</kanji> to set up, the same square every single day, and that fixed trading ground is a <vocabulary>market</vocabulary>.
items.description: Read this way, the word means an abstract market — a stock market, an export market, the whole arena of buyers and sellers. It is not a physical hall of stalls; that sense is a different reading of the same two characters.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は魚を市場に売りに行きます。
example_sentences.english: I go to the market to sell fish.
example_sentences.furigana: 僕[ぼく]は魚[さかな]を市[し]場[じょう]に売[う]りに行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: この市場は野菜が安いです。
example_sentences.english: Vegetables are cheap at this market.
example_sentences.furigana: この市[し]場[じょう]は野[や]菜[さい]が安[やす]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい市場が町にできました。
example_sentences.english: A new market was built in the town.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい市[し]場[じょう]が町[まち]にできました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 工（こう）＋場（じょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Construction's (工) open place (場): a factory.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Wall off a flat <kanji>place</kanji>, pack it with machines doing heavy <kanji>craft</kanji> all day, and the shed you built is a <vocabulary>factory</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この工場では車を作っています。
example_sentences.english: This factory makes cars.
example_sentences.furigana: この工[こう]場[じょう]では車[くるま]を作[つく]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 工場の近くに大きい川があります。
example_sentences.english: There is a big river near the factory.
example_sentences.furigana: 工[こう]場[じょう]の近[ちか]くに大[おお]きい川[かわ]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達はその工場を見に行きました。
example_sentences.english: My friend went to see that factory.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]はその工[こう]場[じょう]を見[み]に行[い]きました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 農（のう）＋家（か）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Farming's (農) household (家): a farmer's home.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>house</kanji> standing alone out in the crop fields, pig still under its roof, worked from dawn to dusk by whoever lives there, is a <vocabulary>farmhouse / farmer</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は農家で働いています。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather works on a farm.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は農[のう]家[か]で働[はたら]いています。

example_sentences.japanese: あの農家は野菜をたくさん売っています。
example_sentences.english: That farmhouse sells a lot of vegetables.
example_sentences.furigana: あの農[のう]家[か]は野[や]菜[さい]をたくさん売[う]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 農家の子供たちは毎朝早く起きます。
example_sentences.english: The farmer's children wake up early every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 農[のう]家[か]の子[こ]供[ども]たちは毎[まい]朝[あさ]早[はや]く起[お]きます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 漁（ぎょ）＋業（ぎょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Fishing (漁) as an occupation (業).
items.meaning_mnemonic: Scale that odd little tree-stump <kanji>business</kanji> up until a whole coast of boats is hauling nets of fish to market, and you have the <vocabulary>fishing industry</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この町は漁業で有名です。
example_sentences.english: This town is famous for its fishing industry.
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]は漁[ぎょ]業[ぎょう]で有[ゆう]名[めい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の家族は漁業をしています。
example_sentences.english: His family works in the fishing industry.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]の家[か]族[ぞく]は漁[ぎょ]業[ぎょう]をしています。

example_sentences.japanese: 漁業の仕事はとても大変です。
example_sentences.english: Fishing industry work is very hard.
example_sentences.furigana: 漁[ぎょ]業[ぎょう]の仕[し]事[ごと]はとても大[たい]変[へん]です。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 資（し）＋源（げん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Capital's (資) source (源): natural resources.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The underground <kanji>source</kanji> a country pulls its ore, timber, oil and fresh water from is the whole of its <vocabulary>resources</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 資源はあまり多くないです。
example_sentences.english: There aren't very many resources.
example_sentences.furigana: 資[し]源[げん]はあまり多[おお]くないです。

example_sentences.japanese: 資源を使いすぎないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don't use resources excessively.
example_sentences.furigana: 資[し]源[げん]を使[つか]いすぎないでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 資源はみんなのものです。
example_sentences.english: Resources belong to everyone.
example_sentences.furigana: 資[し]源[げん]はみんなのものです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 環（かん）＋境（きょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A ring (環) around the border (境): the environment.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Draw a <kanji>ring</kanji> around yourself and walk it out to the <kanji>boundary</kanji> where your surroundings stop; everything caught inside is your <vocabulary>environment</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社の環境はいいです。
example_sentences.english: This company's environment is good.
example_sentences.furigana: この会[かい]社[しゃ]の環[かん]境[きょう]はいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 静かな環境で勉強したいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to study in a quiet environment.
example_sentences.furigana: 静[しず]かな環[かん]境[きょう]で勉[べん]強[きょう]したいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 環境が新しくなりました。
example_sentences.english: The environment was renewed.
example_sentences.furigana: 環[かん]境[きょう]が新[あたら]しくなりました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 問（もん）＋題（だい）＋点（てん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The point (点) of a problem (問題).
items.meaning_mnemonic: Out of a whole report, the single <kanji>topic</kanji> every <kanji>question</kanji> keeps snagging on is the <vocabulary>problem point</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この問題点を説明してください。
example_sentences.english: Please explain this problem.
example_sentences.furigana: この問[もん]題[だい]点[てん]を説[せつ]明[めい]してください。

example_sentences.japanese: 問題点はまだ分かっていません。
example_sentences.english: The problem hasn't been figured out yet.
example_sentences.furigana: 問[もん]題[だい]点[てん]はまだ分[わ]かっていません。

example_sentences.japanese: この問題点は難しいですね。
example_sentences.english: This problem is difficult, isn't it?
example_sentences.furigana: この問[もん]題[だい]点[てん]は難[むずか]しいですね。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 原（げん）＋因（いん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The origin's (原) reason (因): a cause.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>original</kanji> thing that set an accident moving, traced back through every step, is its <vocabulary>cause</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の病気の原因は分かりません。
example_sentences.english: The cause of his illness is unknown.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]の病[びょう]気[き]の原[げん]因[いん]は分[わ]かりません。

example_sentences.japanese: 食べ過ぎは病気の原因になります。
example_sentences.english: Overeating becomes a cause of illness.
example_sentences.furigana: 食[た]べ過[す]ぎは病[びょう]気[き]の原[げん]因[いん]になります。

example_sentences.japanese: 原因が分かったので、うれしいです。
example_sentences.english: Since the cause was found, I'm glad.
example_sentences.furigana: 原[げん]因[いん]が分[わ]かったので、うれしいです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 結（けっ）＋果（か）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 結 けつ → けっ.
items.mnemonic_text: Tying together (結) a fruit (果): the result.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Tie</kanji> off the last knot of a long job and cut open whatever <kanji>fruit</kanji> it grew; that payoff is the <vocabulary>result</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 試験の結果を心配しています。
example_sentences.english: I'm worried about the exam results.
example_sentences.furigana: 試[し]験[けん]の結[けっ]果[か]を心[しん]配[ぱい]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 結果はまだ分かりません。
example_sentences.english: The results aren't known yet.
example_sentences.furigana: 結[けっ]果[か]はまだ分[わ]かりません。

example_sentences.japanese: いい結果がほしいです。
example_sentences.english: I want a good result.
example_sentences.furigana: いい結[けっ]果[か]がほしいです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 夫（ふう）＋婦（ふ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Husband (夫) and wife (婦): a couple.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Put a <kanji>husband</kanji> and a <kanji>wife</kanji> under one roof, rings on, and the pair of them together make a <vocabulary>married couple</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣に住んでいる夫婦はとても親切です。
example_sentences.english: The couple living next door is very kind.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]に住[す]んでいる夫[ふう]婦[ふ]はとても親[しん]切[せつ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: あの夫婦は公園で散歩しています。
example_sentences.english: That couple is taking a walk in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: あの夫[ふう]婦[ふ]は公[こう]園[えん]で散[さん]歩[ぽ]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちは去年結婚して、夫婦になりました。
example_sentences.english: We got married last year and became a couple.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]たちは去[きょ]年[ねん]結[けっ]婚[こん]して、夫[ふう]婦[ふ]になりました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 男（だん）＋性（せい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Man's (男) nature (性): male.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>man</kanji> straight from the rice field, ticked into one column of the <kanji>gender</kanji> box on the form, is <vocabulary>male (gender)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: あの男性は先生です。
example_sentences.english: That man is a teacher.
example_sentences.furigana: あの男[だん]性[せい]は先[せん]生[せい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 男性も女性も忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: Both men and women are busy.
example_sentences.furigana: 男[だん]性[せい]も女[じょ]性[せい]も忙[いそが]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: あの男性は電車の切符をなくしました。
example_sentences.english: That man lost his train ticket.
example_sentences.furigana: あの男[だん]性[せい]は電[でん]車[しゃ]の切[きっ]符[ぷ]をなくしました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 女（じょ）＋性（せい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Woman's (女) nature (性): female.
items.meaning_mnemonic: In biology class the <kanji>woman</kanji> is the worked example of the other <kanji>gender</kanji>, the one marked <vocabulary>female (gender)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: その女性はとても親切でした。
example_sentences.english: That woman was very kind.
example_sentences.furigana: その女[じょ]性[せい]はとても親[しん]切[せつ]でした。

example_sentences.japanese: この会社には女性が多いです。
example_sentences.english: This company has many women.
example_sentences.furigana: この会[かい]社[しゃ]には女[じょ]性[せい]が多[おお]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は女性の医者になりたいと言いました。
example_sentences.english: She said she wants to become a female doctor.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は女[じょ]性[せい]の医[い]者[しゃ]になりたいと言[い]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 青（せい）＋年（ねん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Blue-green (青) years (年): a young man.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A man in a <kanji>blue</kanji> shirt who has lived only twenty <kanji>year</kanji>s is a <vocabulary>youth (young man)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 公園で青年が犬と一緒に走っています。
example_sentences.english: A young man is running with his dog in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]で青[せい]年[ねん]が犬[いぬ]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に走[はし]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅で青年が荷物を運んでくれました。
example_sentences.english: At the station, a young man carried my luggage for me.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]で青[せい]年[ねん]が荷[に]物[もつ]を運[はこ]んでくれました。

example_sentences.japanese: その青年は毎朝六時に店を開けます。
example_sentences.english: That young man opens the shop at six every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: その青[せい]年[ねん]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]六[ろく]時[じ]に店[みせ]を開[あ]けます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 少（しょう）＋年（ねん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Few (少) years (年): a boy.
items.meaning_mnemonic: With only a <kanji>few</kanji> <kanji>year</kanji>s behind him, still losing his baby teeth, he is a <vocabulary>boy</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 川で少年が魚を三匹取りました。
example_sentences.english: A boy caught three fish in the river.
example_sentences.furigana: 川[かわ]で少[しょう]年[ねん]が魚[さかな]を三[さん]匹[ひき]取[と]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 少年のとき、祖父は海でよく泳いだそうです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently my grandfather often swam in the sea when he was a boy.
example_sentences.furigana: 少[しょう]年[ねん]のとき、祖[そ]父[ふ]は海[うみ]でよく泳[およ]いだそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 自転車に乗った少年が角を曲がりました。
example_sentences.english: A boy on a bicycle turned the corner.
example_sentences.furigana: 自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]に乗[の]った少[しょう]年[ねん]が角[かど]を曲[ま]がりました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 少（しょう）＋女（じょ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Few (少) years, a woman (女): a girl.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>woman</kanji> with only a <kanji>little</kanji> of her growing behind her, still barely elbow-high, is a <vocabulary>girl</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 窓の外で少女が雪を見ています。
example_sentences.english: A girl is outside the window, watching the snow.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]の外[そと]で少[しょう]女[じょ]が雪[ゆき]を見[み]ています。

example_sentences.japanese: 少女は赤い帽子を探していました。
example_sentences.english: The girl was looking for her red hat.
example_sentences.furigana: 少[しょう]女[じょ]は赤[あか]い帽[ぼう]子[し]を探[さが]していました。

example_sentences.japanese: この本は十歳の少女が書きました。
example_sentences.english: A ten-year-old girl wrote this book.
example_sentences.furigana: この本[ほん]は十[じゅっ]歳[さい]の少[しょう]女[じょ]が書[か]きました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 恋（こい）＋人（びと）. Rendaku: 人 ひと → びと.
items.mnemonic_text: A person (人) of love (恋): a lover.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The single <kanji>person</kanji> your heart keeps circling back to, the one you actually picked, is your <vocabulary>lover / partner</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 恋人に手紙を書いたのに、まだ送っていません。
example_sentences.english: I wrote a letter to my partner, but I still haven't sent it.
example_sentences.furigana: 恋[こい]人[びと]に手[て]紙[がみ]を書[か]いたのに、まだ送[おく]っていません。

example_sentences.japanese: 姉の恋人は料理がとても上手です。
example_sentences.english: My older sister's partner is a really good cook.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]の恋[こい]人[びと]は料[りょう]理[り]がとても上手[じょうず]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 恋人と湖の近くを散歩したいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to take a walk by the lake with my partner.
example_sentences.furigana: 恋[こい]人[びと]と湖[みずうみ]の近[ちか]くを散[さん]歩[ぽ]したいです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 友（ゆう）＋人（じん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A friend (友) person (人): a friend.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>person</kanji> you would call a <kanji>friend</kanji>, named in the stiff wording you would put on a form, is a <vocabulary>friend (formal)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学の友人が来月結婚します。
example_sentences.english: A friend from university is getting married next month.
example_sentences.furigana: 大[だい]学[がく]の友[ゆう]人[じん]が来[らい]月[げつ]結[けっ]婚[こん]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 友人に紹介してもらった旅館は、静かできれいでした。
example_sentences.english: The inn a friend told me about was quiet and clean.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[ゆう]人[じん]に紹[しょう]介[かい]してもらった旅[りょ]館[かん]は、静[しず]かできれいでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 困ったとき、友人が一番に電話をくれました。
example_sentences.english: When I was in trouble, a friend was the first to call me.
example_sentences.furigana: 困[こま]ったとき、友[ゆう]人[じん]が一[いち]番[ばん]に電[でん]話[わ]をくれました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 仲（なか）＋間（ま）.
items.mnemonic_text: One who shares your space (間) inside (仲): a comrade.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Shrink the space <kanji>between</kanji> you and the people you share a <kanji>relationship</kanji> with until you all stand shoulder to shoulder, and they are your <vocabulary>companion / comrade</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事の仲間と金曜日の夜に食事しました。
example_sentences.english: I had dinner with my work friends on Friday night.
example_sentences.furigana: 仕[し]事[ごと]の仲[なか]間[ま]と金[きん]曜[よう]日[び]の夜[よる]に食[しょく]事[じ]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 山に登るときは、仲間を待たなければなりません。
example_sentences.english: When you climb a mountain, you have to wait for your companions.
example_sentences.furigana: 山[やま]に登[のぼ]るときは、仲[なか]間[ま]を待[ま]たなければなりません。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬は猫を仲間だと思っているかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: The dog might think the cat is one of the pack.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]は猫[ねこ]を仲[なか]間[ま]だと思[おも]っているかもしれません。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 個（こ）＋人（じん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A single (個) person (人): an individual.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pull one <kanji>person</kanji> out of the crowd and weigh them on their own, and what you are looking at is an <vocabulary>individual</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: これは会社のパソコンで、個人のものではありません。
example_sentences.english: This is the company's computer, not a personal one.
example_sentences.furigana: これは会[かい]社[しゃ]のパソコンで、個[こ]人[じん]のものではありません。

example_sentences.japanese: 個人の電話番号は書かなくてもいいです。
example_sentences.english: You don't have to write your personal phone number.
example_sentences.furigana: 個[こ]人[じん]の電[でん]話[わ]番[ばん]号[ごう]は書[か]かなくてもいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 私個人の意見ですが、この店のパンが一番おいしいと思います。
example_sentences.english: That's just my personal opinion, but I think this shop's bread is the best.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]個[こ]人[じん]の意[い]見[けん]ですが、この店[みせ]のパンが一[いち]番[ばん]おいしいと思[おも]います。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 相（あい）＋手（て）.
items.mnemonic_text: The hand (手) you face (相): your opponent or partner.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>hand</kanji> that reaches back to meet yours from the <kanji>mutual</kanji> side of a deal or a match is <vocabulary>the other party</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 電話の相手は誰でしたか。
example_sentences.english: Who was that on the phone?
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]話[わ]の相[あい]手[て]は誰[だれ]でしたか。

example_sentences.japanese: 相手の名前をすぐ忘れるので、ノートに書きます。
example_sentences.english: I forget people's names right away, so I write them in a notebook.
example_sentences.furigana: 相[あい]手[て]の名[な]前[まえ]をすぐ忘[わす]れるので、ノートに書[か]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 次の相手は強そうですね。
example_sentences.english: Our next opponent looks strong, doesn't he?
example_sentences.furigana: 次[つぎ]の相[あい]手[て]は強[つよ]そうですね。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 客（きゃく）.
items.mnemonic_text: A visitor sheltered under a roof: a guest.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Anyone who comes through your door expecting to be seated, served and fussed over before they leave again is a <vocabulary>guest / customer</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の日は、喫茶店に客があまり来ません。
example_sentences.english: On rainy days, not many customers come to the coffee shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]は、喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]に客[きゃく]があまり来[き]ません。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は客が泊まるので、部屋を準備します。
example_sentences.english: Guests are staying over this weekend, so I'm getting the room ready.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]は客[きゃく]が泊[と]まるので、部屋[へや]を準[じゅん]備[び]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 店員は客に傘を貸しました。
example_sentences.english: The clerk lent the customer an umbrella.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]は客[きゃく]に傘[かさ]を貸[か]しました。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — お＋客（きゃく）＋さん.
items.mnemonic_text: Polite form of guest: a customer.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That same visitor, but bowed to on the way in, thanked on the way out, and spoken of only in the polite words staff keep for people they serve, is a <vocabulary>customer (polite)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: お客さん、財布を忘れていますよ。
example_sentences.english: Excuse me, you're forgetting your wallet!
example_sentences.furigana: お客[きゃく]さん、財[さい]布[ふ]を忘[わす]れていますよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はお客さんが多くて、昼ご飯を食べる時間がありませんでした。
example_sentences.english: We had so many customers today that I had no time to eat lunch.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]はお客[きゃく]さんが多[おお]くて、昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べる時[じ]間[かん]がありませんでした。

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんにお釣りを渡してください。
example_sentences.english: Please hand the customer their change.
example_sentences.furigana: お客[きゃく]さんにお釣[つ]りを渡[わた]してください。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 店（てん）＋員（いん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A shop's (店) staff member (員): a clerk.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A roadside <kanji>shop</kanji> so small it keeps just one <kanji>employee</kanji> behind the counter, and that person is the <vocabulary>shop clerk</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 店員に日本語で話しました。
example_sentences.english: I spoke to the shop clerk in Japanese.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]に日本[にほん]語[ご]で話[はな]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: あの店員はとても親切です。
example_sentences.english: That shop clerk is very kind.
example_sentences.furigana: あの店[てん]員[いん]はとても親[しん]切[せつ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 店員に道を聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I asked the shop clerk for directions.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]に道[みち]を聞[き]きました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 公（こう）＋務（む）＋員（いん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A public (公) duty's (務) staff member (員).
items.meaning_mnemonic: An <kanji>employee</kanji> whose <kanji>duties</kanji> are <kanji>public</kanji> is a <vocabulary>civil servant</vocabulary>. The public purse feeds this one, not a single company's till.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は公務員です。
example_sentences.english: My older brother is a civil servant.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は公[こう]務[む]員[いん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 公務員になりたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to become a civil servant.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]務[む]員[いん]になりたいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 公務員の試験は難しいです。
example_sentences.english: The civil service exam is difficult.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]務[む]員[いん]の試[し]験[けん]は難[むずか]しいです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 主（しゅ）＋婦（ふ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The main (主) woman (婦) of the house.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The household <kanji>lord</kanji> whose word everyone follows, who also happens to be the <kanji>wife</kanji>, is the <vocabulary>housewife</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は主婦です。
example_sentences.english: My mother is a housewife.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は主[しゅ]婦[ふ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 主婦は毎日忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: Housewives are busy every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 主[しゅ]婦[ふ]は毎[まい]日[にち]忙[いそが]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の主婦に野菜をもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I got some vegetables from the housewife next door.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]の主[しゅ]婦[ふ]に野[や]菜[さい]をもらいました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 学（がく）＋者（しゃ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A person (者) of learning (学): a scholar.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>person</kanji> stacked so high with days of <kanji>study</kanji> that they grumble about it has turned into a <vocabulary>scholar</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は有名な学者です。
example_sentences.english: He is a famous scholar.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は有[ゆう]名[めい]な学[がく]者[しゃ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: その学者は歴史を教えています。
example_sentences.english: That scholar teaches history.
example_sentences.furigana: その学[がく]者[しゃ]は歴[れき]史[し]を教[おし]えています。

example_sentences.japanese: 学者になるのは難しいです。
example_sentences.english: Becoming a scholar is difficult.
example_sentences.furigana: 学[がく]者[しゃ]になるのは難[むずか]しいです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 専（せん）＋門（もん）＋家（か）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A house (家) devoted to one gate (専門): an expert.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Build your whole <kanji>house</kanji> up against one <kanji>gate</kanji> and refuse to deal with anything outside that single <kanji>specialty</kanji>, and you are a <vocabulary>specialist</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者は病気の専門家です。
example_sentences.english: A doctor is an expert on illness.
example_sentences.furigana: 医[い]者[しゃ]は病[びょう]気[き]の専[せん]門[もん]家[か]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 専門家の意見を聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I listened to the expert's opinion.
example_sentences.furigana: 専[せん]門[もん]家[か]の意[い]見[けん]を聞[き]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 専門家の話はとても面白かったです。
example_sentences.english: The expert's talk was very interesting.
example_sentences.furigana: 専[せん]門[もん]家[か]の話[はなし]はとても面白[おもしろ]かったです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 成（せい）＋人（じん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: One who has become (成) a person (人): an adult.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>person</kanji> the law finally counts as having <kanji>turned into</kanji> a full-grown one is an <vocabulary>adult</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は今年成人しました。
example_sentences.english: My older sister came of age this year.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]は今年[ことし]成[せい]人[じん]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 娘はまだ成人していません。
example_sentences.english: My daughter is not yet an adult.
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]はまだ成[せい]人[じん]していません。

example_sentences.japanese: 成人したら、一人で旅行できます。
example_sentences.english: Once you become an adult, you can travel alone.
example_sentences.furigana: 成[せい]人[じん]したら、一人[ひとり]で旅[りょ]行[こう]できます。

items.word_type: な adjective, noun, の adjective
items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 偶（ぐう）＋然（ぜん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A paired (偶) natural (然) event: a coincidence.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Two things line up by pure <kanji>accident</kanji>, with nothing behind it but being <kanji>that sort of thing</kanji>, and you call it a <vocabulary>coincidence</vocabulary>. It takes な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅で偶然先生に会いました。
example_sentences.english: I happened to run into my teacher at the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]で偶[ぐう]然[ぜん]先[せん]生[せい]に会[あ]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: それは偶然です。
example_sentences.english: That's a coincidence.
example_sentences.furigana: それは偶[ぐう]然[ぜん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 偶然、財布を見つけました。
example_sentences.english: I happened to find a wallet.
example_sentences.furigana: 偶[ぐう]然[ぜん]、財[さい]布[ふ]を見[み]つけました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 親（おや）.
items.mnemonic_text: Standing by a tree, watching over you: a parent.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>parent</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>parent</vocabulary> word are the same character, so they mean exactly the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: From the highest branch of the tree by Sei's school field, a figure craning to see every kick shouts <reading>oh, ya</reading>, 「<reading>おや</reading>」, at each goal, and only a <vocabulary form="親">parent</vocabulary> would.

example_sentences.japanese: 親に電話しました。
example_sentences.english: I called my parent.
example_sentences.furigana: 親[おや]に電[でん]話[わ]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 親は子供の名前を考えます。
example_sentences.english: Parents think about their child's name.
example_sentences.furigana: 親[おや]は子[こ]供[ども]の名[な]前[まえ]を考[かんが]えます。

example_sentences.japanese: 親と一緒に旅行しました。
example_sentences.english: I traveled together with my parent.
example_sentences.furigana: 親[おや]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に旅[りょ]行[こう]しました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 寂（さび）＋しい.
items.mnemonic_text: A quiet (寂) still heart: lonely.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The kanji here already means <kanji>loneliness</kanji> all by itself, and the い on the end makes it the adjective <vocabulary>lonely</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: All her loneliness comes out in one <reading>sob, she</reading> sound with a thin trailing ee, 「<reading>さびしい</reading>」, and that small cry is how feeling <vocabulary form="寂しい">lonely</vocabulary> sounds.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で寂しいです。
example_sentences.english: I feel lonely being by myself.
example_sentences.furigana: 一人[ひとり]で寂[さび]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい学校で友達がいなくて寂しいです。
example_sentences.english: I'm lonely at my new school without any friends.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい学[がっ]校[こう]で友[とも]達[だち]がいなくて寂[さび]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母に会えなくて寂しいです。
example_sentences.english: I'm lonely because I can't see my grandmother.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]に会[あ]えなくて寂[さび]しいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 恥（は）＋ずかしい.
items.mnemonic_text: A heart (心) that shrinks: embarrassed.
items.meaning_mnemonic: That single kanji carries the plain sense of <kanji>shame</kanji>, and adding the い ending turns it into the adjective <vocabulary>embarrassing</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A customer burns with shame at the till: the man <reading>has a cashier</reading> staring at him, and his whisper of 「<reading>はずかしい</reading>」 trails off into a long ee, because this is so <vocabulary form="恥ずかしい">embarrassing</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 質問に答えられなくて恥ずかしかったです。
example_sentences.english: I was embarrassed that I couldn't answer the question.
example_sentences.furigana: 質[しつ]問[もん]に答[こた]えられなくて恥[は]ずかしかったです。

example_sentences.japanese: 恥ずかしいから、あまり話しません。
example_sentences.english: It's embarrassing, so I don't talk much.
example_sentences.furigana: 恥[は]ずかしいから、あまり話[はな]しません。

example_sentences.japanese: 写真を見せるのは恥ずかしいです。
example_sentences.english: Showing photos is embarrassing.
example_sentences.furigana: 写[しゃ]真[しん]を見[み]せるのは恥[は]ずかしいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 羨（うらや）＋ましい.
items.mnemonic_text: Looking sideways with longing: envious.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your friend shows you her new apartment with the huge balcony and the view of the park, and yours looks at a wall. That hot, sour wish to have her place instead of yours is being <vocabulary form="羨ましい">envious</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: From your friend's huge new balcony you spot her red sports car by the park and groan 「<reading>うらやましい</reading>」, as in <reading>you're a Maserati</reading> owner too. Your window faces a wall, so you are <vocabulary form="羨ましい">envious</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は毎年外国へ旅行できるので、羨ましいです。
example_sentences.english: My older sister gets to travel abroad every year, so I envy her.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]は毎[まい]年[ねん]外[がい]国[こく]へ旅[りょ]行[こう]できるので、羨[うらや]ましいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 君の新しい自転車、本当に羨ましいよ。
example_sentences.english: I really envy you that new bike.
example_sentences.furigana: 君[きみ]の新[あたら]しい自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]、本[ほん]当[とう]に羨[うらや]ましいよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語が上手な隣の人が羨ましかった。
example_sentences.english: I was jealous of the person next to me, whose Japanese was so good.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]語[ご]が上手[じょうず]な隣[となり]の人[ひと]が羨[うらや]ましかった。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — めんどくさい cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 面倒くさい.
items.mnemonic_text: A face (面) that's too much bother: annoying.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You put on a stiff <kanji form="面">mask</kanji> just to answer the door, and the whole prop shelf <kanji form="倒">collapses</kanji> on you as you reach for it. A small job that turns into that much bother is <vocabulary form="面倒くさい">troublesome</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Mendo pulls on a stiff mask to answer the door, the whole prop shelf collapses on him, and <reading>Mendo cusses</reading> 「<reading>めんどくさい</reading>」 from under the pile, a job grown <vocabulary form="面倒くさい">troublesome</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎晩皿を洗うのが面倒くさい。
example_sentences.english: Washing the dishes every night is such a pain.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]晩[ばん]皿[さら]を洗[あら]うのが面[めん]倒[どう]くさい。

example_sentences.japanese: 面倒くさいから、今日は駅までタクシーで行きます。
example_sentences.english: I can't be bothered, so I'm taking a taxi to the station today.
example_sentences.furigana: 面[めん]倒[どう]くさいから、今日[きょう]は駅[えき]までタクシーで行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 面倒くさい書類は、明日書きます。
example_sentences.english: I'll fill out the annoying paperwork tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 面[めん]倒[どう]くさい書[しょ]類[るい]は、明日[あした]書[か]きます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 厳（きび）＋しい.
items.mnemonic_text: A stern cliff of rules: strict.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your piano teacher stops you at the first wrong note, every time, and will not let you move on until the bar is perfect. Being held to a standard that hard, with nothing let slide, is <vocabulary form="厳しい">strict</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Your piano teacher, a bee named <reading>Kibi</reading>, buzzes <reading>きびしい</reading> and stops you at the first wrong note, never letting a single bar slide, because she is that <vocabulary form="厳しい">strict</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: あの数学の先生は宿題にとても厳しい。
example_sentences.english: That math teacher is really strict about homework.
example_sentences.furigana: あの数[すう]学[がく]の先[せん]生[せい]は宿[しゅく]題[だい]にとても厳[きび]しい。

example_sentences.japanese: この会社は時間に厳しいので、遅れないでください。
example_sentences.english: This company is strict about time, so please don't be late.
example_sentences.furigana: この会[かい]社[しゃ]は時[じ]間[かん]に厳[きび]しいので、遅[おく]れないでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は食事のとき厳しかったです。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother was strict at mealtimes.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]は食[しょく]事[じ]のとき厳[きび]しかったです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 優（やさ）＋しい.
items.mnemonic_text: A superior (優) gentle heart: kind.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A person who meets everyone with <kanji form="優">tenderness</kanji>, quick to go easy on you and slow to judge, is what Japanese calls <vocabulary form="優しい">kind / gentle</vocabulary>. The final い is the ending that makes it an adjective.
items.reading_mnemonic: You mumble a wrong order and brace for a scolding, but the person who goes easy on everyone only smiles <reading>yeah, sushi</reading>, no judging. That soft <reading>やさしい</reading> reply is <vocabulary form="優しい">kind</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の奥さんはいつも猫に優しいです。
example_sentences.english: The lady next door is always gentle with cats.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]の奥[おく]さんはいつも猫[ねこ]に優[やさ]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅員さんが優しく道を教えてくれました。
example_sentences.english: The station attendant kindly showed me the way.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]員[いん]さんが優[やさ]しく道[みち]を教[おし]えてくれました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は優しい声で赤ちゃんに歌を歌った。
example_sentences.english: She sang to the baby in a gentle voice.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は優[やさ]しい声[こえ]で赤[あか]ちゃんに歌[うた]を歌[うた]った。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 怖（こわ）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: A heart (忄) gripped by fear: scary.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A thing so <kanji form="怖">dreadful</kanji> that your legs lock and your breath stops before you can even run from it is what <vocabulary form="怖い">scary</vocabulary> means.
items.reading_mnemonic: A <reading>koala</reading> drops from a branch right in front of you, ears flat and hissing, and your legs lock and your breath stops before you can run. You can only gasp <reading>こわい</reading>, because that is <vocabulary form="怖い">scary</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜の公園は暗くて怖いです。
example_sentences.english: The park at night is dark and scary.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]の公[こう]園[えん]は暗[くら]くて怖[こわ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は犬が怖いので、近くに行けません。
example_sentences.english: My little sister is scared of dogs, so she can't go near them.
example_sentences.furigana: 妹[いもうと]は犬[いぬ]が怖[こわ]いので、近[ちか]くに行[い]けません。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、怖い映画を見て、寝られなかった。
example_sentences.english: I watched a scary movie yesterday and couldn't sleep.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、怖[こわ]い映[えい]画[が]を見[み]て、寝[ね]られなかった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 深（ふか）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: Water (氵) reaching far down: deep.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You drop a stone into the well and count five full seconds before you hear it hit water. A gap that long between the top and the bottom is what <vocabulary form="深い">deep</vocabulary> means.
items.reading_mnemonic: Your stone takes five full seconds to splash down the well, and you mutter that <reading>few can</reading> climb out of a hole that <vocabulary form="深い">deep</vocabulary>. The word for it is <reading>ふかい</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: この湖は深いので、子供は入ってはいけません。
example_sentences.english: This lake is deep, so children must not go in.
example_sentences.furigana: この湖[みずうみ]は深[ふか]いので、子[こ]供[ども]は入[はい]ってはいけません。

example_sentences.japanese: 山の中に深い川がありました。
example_sentences.english: There was a deep river up in the mountains.
example_sentences.furigana: 山[やま]の中[なか]に深[ふか]い川[かわ]がありました。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は深い箱に古い写真を入れた。
example_sentences.english: My father put the old photos in a deep box.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は深[ふか]い箱[はこ]に古[ふる]い写[しゃ]真[しん]を入[い]れた。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 浅（あさ）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: Water (氵) barely covering: shallow.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You wade into the lake ready to swim, and fifty steps out the water still only reaches your knees. Water that never gets deep enough to swim in is <vocabulary form="浅い">shallow</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Fifty steps out into the lake the water still only reaches your knees, so you let out <reading>a sigh</reading>, <reading>あさい</reading>, because nobody can swim in water this <vocabulary form="浅い">shallow</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この川は浅いので、歩いて渡れます。
example_sentences.english: This river is shallow, so you can walk across it.
example_sentences.furigana: この川[かわ]は浅[あさ]いので、歩[ある]いて渡[わた]れます。

example_sentences.japanese: 浅い皿に魚を並べました。
example_sentences.english: I laid the fish out on a shallow plate.
example_sentences.furigana: 浅[あさ]い皿[さら]に魚[さかな]を並[なら]べました。

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は海の浅い所で遊んでいます。
example_sentences.english: My son is playing in the shallow part of the sea.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]は海[うみ]の浅[あさ]い所[ところ]で遊[あそ]んでいます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 細（ほそ）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: Thread drawn out fine: thin.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="細">thin</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="細い">thin / slender</vocabulary> word are the same character and carry the same sense. The い on the end is what lets it stand in front of a noun like any adjective.
items.reading_mnemonic: The farmer lays a <reading>hose</reading> along the mud path between the rice fields, and it only fits because each path is no wider than a thread. Anything that narrow is <reading>ほそい</reading>, <vocabulary form="細い">thin</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の後ろに細い道があります。
example_sentences.english: There's a narrow lane behind the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の後[うし]ろに細[ほそ]い道[みち]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母の髪は細くて長いです。
example_sentences.english: My aunt's hair is fine and long.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔母[おば]の髪[かみ]は細[ほそ]くて長[なが]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 細いペンで名前を書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write your name with a thin pen.
example_sentences.furigana: 細[ほそ]いペンで名[な]前[まえ]を書[か]いてください。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 太（ふと）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: A big extra drop of size: thick.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You have already met the kanji <kanji form="太">thick</kanji>, so the word <vocabulary form="太い">thick / fat</vocabulary> is nothing new: it is the same character with the same meaning.
items.reading_mnemonic: That one extra drop of fat lands on a <reading>foot</reading> already stretched as big as it can stand, and now no shoe fits. A foot gone that wide is <reading>ふとい</reading>, <vocabulary form="太い">fat</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 庭に太い木が一本あります。
example_sentences.english: There's one thick tree in the yard.
example_sentences.furigana: 庭[にわ]に太[ふと]い木[き]が一[いっ]本[ぽん]あります。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は首が太くて、力が強いです。
example_sentences.english: My older brother has a thick neck and is really strong.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は首[くび]が太[ふと]くて、力[ちから]が強[つよ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 黒板にチョークで太く書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write in thick strokes on the blackboard with the chalk.
example_sentences.furigana: 黒[こく]板[ばん]にチョークで太[ふと]く書[か]いてください。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Neither hot nor cold: lukewarm.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Louie pours you a coffee that has sat out so long it is neither hot nor cold. A drink stuck at room temperature like that is <vocabulary form="ぬるい">lukewarm</vocabulary>, and hearing <reading>new Louie</reading> pour another one is how you keep hold of 「<reading>ぬるい</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: お茶がぬるくなったので、もう一度入れました。
example_sentences.english: My tea had gone lukewarm, so I made a fresh cup.
example_sentences.furigana: お茶[ちゃ]がぬるくなったので、もう一[いち]度[ど]入[い]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: このビール、ぬるくてまずいよ。
example_sentences.english: This beer is lukewarm and tastes awful.
example_sentences.furigana: このビール、ぬるくてまずいよ。

example_sentences.japanese: ぬるい牛乳は飲みたくない。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to drink lukewarm milk.
example_sentences.furigana: ぬるい牛[ぎゅう]乳[にゅう]は飲[の]みたくない。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: A tight fit that pinches: tight, harsh.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The zip-tie on that parcel is pulled so <vocabulary form="きつい">tight / harsh</vocabulary> it <reading>cuts you</reading> when you lift it. That bite into your fingers is what <reading>きつい</reading> means.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年のシャツを着たら、きつかった。
example_sentences.english: I put on last year's shirt, and it was tight.
example_sentences.furigana: 去[きょ]年[ねん]のシャツを着[き]たら、きつかった。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝六時から働くのはきついね。
example_sentences.english: Working from six every morning is rough, isn't it?
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]六[ろく]時[じ]から働[はたら]くのはきついね。

example_sentences.japanese: 父に「遅い」ときつく言われました。
example_sentences.english: My father told me sharply, "You're late."
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]に「遅[おそ]い」ときつく言[い]われました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 緩（ゆる）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: Thread with slack in it: loose.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The elastic in Sei's gym shorts has lost all its stretch. One jog down the field and the waistband slides past his hips, flapping <vocabulary form="緩い">loose / lax</vocabulary> with every step.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei's gym shorts are hand-me-downs from <reading>Yuri</reading>, and one jog down the field sends the worn waistband sliding past his hips. Yuri just shrugs <reading>ゆるい</reading>, they were always <vocabulary form="緩い">loose</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 帽子が緩くて、風で飛びました。
example_sentences.english: My hat was loose, and the wind blew it off.
example_sentences.furigana: 帽[ぼう]子[し]が緩[ゆる]くて、風[かぜ]で飛[と]びました。

example_sentences.japanese: 眼鏡が緩いので、店で直してもらいました。
example_sentences.english: My glasses were loose, so I had them fixed at the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 眼鏡[めがね]が緩[ゆる]いので、店[みせ]で直[なお]してもらいました。

example_sentences.japanese: この学校は緩いので、生徒は好きな服を着られます。
example_sentences.english: This school is relaxed, so pupils can wear whatever clothes they like.
example_sentences.furigana: この学[がっ]校[こう]は緩[ゆる]いので、生[せい]徒[と]は好[す]きな服[ふく]を着[き]られます。

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 素（す）on'yomi ＋ 晴（ば）kun'yomi ＋ ら ＋ し ＋ い.
items.mnemonic_text: A plain (素) clear (晴) sky: wonderful.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Strip a scene down to its <kanji form="素">elementary</kanji> parts under a sky that has just <kanji form="晴">cleared up</kanji>. A view that bare and that bright is <vocabulary form="素晴らしい">wonderful</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 山の上から見た星は素晴らしかった。
example_sentences.english: The stars I saw from the top of the mountain were wonderful.
example_sentences.furigana: 山[やま]の上[うえ]から見[み]た星[ほし]は素晴[すば]らしかった。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母の料理はいつも素晴らしいです。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother's cooking is always wonderful.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]の料[りょう]理[り]はいつも素[す]晴[ば]らしいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 素晴らしい歌を聞かせてくれて、ありがとう。
example_sentences.english: Thanks for letting me hear such a wonderful song.
example_sentences.furigana: 素[す]晴[ば]らしい歌[うた]を聞[き]かせてくれて、ありがとう。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: So intense it's amazing: sugoi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: In this town you can <reading>sue a guy</reading> for looking at you wrong and still collect a payout. That the courts work that way is both <vocabulary form="すごい">amazing / terrible</vocabulary>, so onlookers just breathe <reading>すごい</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 見て、すごい雪だよ。
example_sentences.english: Look at all that snow!
example_sentences.furigana: 見[み]て、すごい雪[ゆき]だよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 三歳の娘がカタカナを全部書けて、すごいと思いました。
example_sentences.english: My three-year-old daughter can write all the katakana. I thought that was amazing.
example_sentences.furigana: 三[さん]歳[さい]の娘[むすめ]がカタカナを全[ぜん]部[ぶ]書[か]けて、すごいと思[おも]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の前はすごい人でした。
example_sentences.english: There was a huge crowd in front of the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]はすごい人[ひと]でした。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 偉（えら）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: A person (亻) of great deeds: admirable.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At ninety, Grandma Kane still climbs the shrine's mossy steps twice a day to sweep each one clean. The whole town agrees that is <vocabulary form="偉い">great / admirable</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Grandma Kane is up <reading>early</reading> at ninety, sweeping every mossy shrine step before sunrise, and the whole town nods <reading>えらい</reading>, calling her <vocabulary form="偉い">admirable</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日宿題をして、偉いね。
example_sentences.english: You do your homework every day. Good for you.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]宿[しゅく]題[だい]をして、偉[えら]いね。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父は会社で一番偉い人です。
example_sentences.english: My uncle is the most senior person at his company.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔父[おじ]は会[かい]社[しゃ]で一[いち]番[ばん]偉[えら]い人[ひと]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 自分が偉いと思っている人は、あまり好きじゃない。
example_sentences.english: I don't much like people who think they're important.
example_sentences.furigana: 自[じ]分[ぶん]が偉[えら]いと思[おも]っている人[ひと]は、あまり好[す]きじゃない。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Slipping around the rules: sly.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every Sunday a kid runs the same <reading>zoo ruse</reading> and slips through a gap in the fence without paying. Beating the queue that way is <vocabulary form="ずるい">sly / unfair</vocabulary>, and the gate guard just sighs <reading>ずるい</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分だけお菓子を二つ取るのはずるいよ。
example_sentences.english: It's not fair to take two sweets just for yourself.
example_sentences.furigana: 自[じ]分[ぶん]だけお菓[か]子[し]を二[ふた]つ取[と]るのはずるいよ。

example_sentences.japanese: テストで友達の答えを見るのはずるいです。
example_sentences.english: Looking at a friend's answers during a test is cheating.
example_sentences.furigana: テストで友[とも]達[だち]の答[こた]えを見[み]るのはずるいです。

example_sentences.japanese: あの猫はずるいから、よく犬の席に座ります。
example_sentences.english: That cat is sly, so it often sits in the dog's spot.
example_sentences.furigana: あの猫[ねこ]はずるいから、よく犬[いぬ]の席[せき]に座[すわ]ります。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 痒（かゆ）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: A sickness (疒) that wants (羊) scratching: itchy.
items.meaning_mnemonic: One mosquito gets into the tent at the riverbank and finds the strip of skin behind your knee. By dawn that spot is so <vocabulary form="痒い">itchy</vocabulary> you have scratched it raw in your sleep.
items.reading_mnemonic: In the tent by the river you wake with that bite behind your knee burning, and you beg your friend <reading>can you</reading> scratch it. You groan <reading>かゆい</reading>, it is so <vocabulary form="痒い">itchy</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 公園で遊んだら、足が痒くなった。
example_sentences.english: After I played in the park, my legs got itchy.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]で遊[あそ]んだら、足[あし]が痒[かゆ]くなった。

example_sentences.japanese: このコートは首が痒いので、もう着ません。
example_sentences.english: This coat makes my neck itch, so I don't wear it anymore.
example_sentences.furigana: このコートは首[くび]が痒[かゆ]いので、もう着[き]ません。

example_sentences.japanese: 目が痒いときは、この薬を使ってください。
example_sentences.english: When your eyes are itchy, please use this medicine.
example_sentences.furigana: 目[め]が痒[かゆ]いときは、この薬[くすり]を使[つか]ってください。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — まじめ cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 真面目.
items.mnemonic_text: A true (真) face (面) and eye (目): serious.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Hold a <kanji form="真">true</kanji> <kanji form="面">face</kanji>, no act, with your <kanji form="目">eye</kanji> fixed on the work in front of you. That is what <vocabulary form="真面目">serious / diligent</vocabulary> looks like, and it takes な before the noun it describes.
items.reading_mnemonic: Jimmy wears a true face, no act, his eye fixed on the homework in front of him. His sister yells <reading>Ma, Jimmy</reading> is all <reading>まじめ</reading> again, so <vocabulary form="真面目">diligent</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は真面目な学生で、毎晩勉強しています。
example_sentences.english: My son is a diligent student who studies every night.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]は真面目[まじめ]な学[がく]生[せい]で、毎[まい]晩[ばん]勉[べん]強[きょう]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 会議では、みんな真面目な顔をしていました。
example_sentences.english: At the meeting, everyone had a serious look on their face.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]では、みんな真面目[まじめ]な顔[かお]をしていました。

example_sentences.japanese: 真面目に練習すれば、上手になりますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you practice seriously, you'll get good at it.
example_sentences.furigana: 真面目[まじめ]に練[れん]習[しゅう]すれば、上手[じょうず]になりますよ。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 熱（ねっ）＋心（しん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 熱 ねつ → ねっ.
items.mnemonic_text: A hot (熱) heart (心): enthusiasm.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A steady <kanji form="熱">heat</kanji> kept burning in the <kanji form="心">heart</kanji> is what being <vocabulary form="熱心">enthusiastic</vocabulary> about something feels like. It is a な adjective, so な goes before the noun.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は熱心に日本の歴史の本を読んでいます。
example_sentences.english: He is eagerly reading a book on Japanese history.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は熱[ねっ]心[しん]に日本[にほん]の歴[れき]史[し]の本[ほん]を読[よ]んでいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 熱心なお客さんが、朝から店の前で待っていた。
example_sentences.english: Keen customers were waiting in front of the shop from the morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 熱[ねっ]心[しん]なお客[きゃく]さんが、朝[あさ]から店[みせ]の前[まえ]で待[ま]っていた。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は熱心に説明してくれましたが、よく分かりませんでした。
example_sentences.english: The teacher explained it with real enthusiasm, but I didn't really understand.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は熱[ねっ]心[しん]に説[せつ]明[めい]してくれましたが、よく分[わ]かりませんでした。

items.word_type: な adjective, noun, の adjective
items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 完（かん）＋全（ぜん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Fully (完) whole (全): perfect.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Once Koichi has swept the <kanji form="全">whole</kanji> shelf into the basket with not one rice ball left behind, the set is <vocabulary form="完全">perfect / complete</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so な comes before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪はまだ完全に良くなっていません。
example_sentences.english: My cold still hasn't completely gone.
example_sentences.furigana: 風邪[かぜ]はまだ完[かん]全[ぜん]に良[よ]くなっていません。

example_sentences.japanese: この地図は古いので、完全ではありません。
example_sentences.english: This map is old, so it isn't complete.
example_sentences.furigana: この地[ち]図[ず]は古[ふる]いので、完[かん]全[ぜん]ではありません。

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行の準備は完全にできました。
example_sentences.english: The preparations for the trip are completely done.
example_sentences.furigana: 旅[りょ]行[こう]の準[じゅん]備[び]は完[かん]全[ぜん]にできました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 十（じゅう）＋分（ぶん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Ten (十) parts (分) full: enough.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Ten <kanji form="分">part</kanji>s out of <kanji form="十">ten</kanji> make up the whole, and having the whole of something is having <vocabulary form="十分">sufficient / enough</vocabulary> of it. As a な adjective, な comes before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: この弁当は大きいので、一つで十分です。
example_sentences.english: This boxed lunch is big, so one is plenty.
example_sentences.furigana: この弁[べん]当[とう]は大[おお]きいので、一[ひと]つで十[じゅう]分[ぶん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 冬の山に行くなら、このコートでは十分じゃないよ。
example_sentences.english: If you are going up a mountain in winter, this coat won't be enough.
example_sentences.furigana: 冬[ふゆ]の山[やま]に行[い]くなら、このコートでは十[じゅう]分[ぶん]じゃないよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は十分に練習したので、試験は大丈夫でしょう。
example_sentences.english: My little brother practiced plenty, so he should be fine on the exam.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は十[じゅう]分[ぶん]に練[れん]習[しゅう]したので、試[し]験[けん]は大[だい]丈[じょう]夫[ぶ]でしょう。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 不（ふ）＋安（あん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Not (不) at peace (安): anxious.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Set the <kanji form="不">negative</kanji> mark against <kanji form="安">peaceful</kanji> and the calm drains out, and a mind left without calm is <vocabulary form="不安">anxious / uneasy</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so な lands before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で外国へ行くのは、ちょっと不安です。
example_sentences.english: I'm a bit nervous about going abroad on my own.
example_sentences.furigana: 一人[ひとり]で外[がい]国[こく]へ行[い]くのは、ちょっと不[ふ]安[あん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 夜の道が暗くて、娘は不安な顔をしていた。
example_sentences.english: The road was dark at night, and my daughter looked uneasy.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]の道[みち]が暗[くら]くて、娘[むすめ]は不[ふ]安[あん]な顔[かお]をしていた。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が説明してくれたので、不安がなくなりました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher explained it to me, so my worries went away.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]が説[せつ]明[めい]してくれたので、不[ふ]安[あん]がなくなりました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 安（あん）＋全（ぜん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Peaceful (安) and whole (全): safe.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji form="安">Peaceful</kanji> across the <kanji form="全">whole</kanji> of a place, with no corner left unguarded, is what makes it <vocabulary form="安全">safe</vocabulary>. As a な adjective, it wants な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: この橋は古いですが、まだ安全です。
example_sentences.english: This bridge is old, but it's still safe.
example_sentences.furigana: この橋[はし]は古[ふる]いですが、まだ安[あん]全[ぜん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が公園の安全な場所で遊んでいます。
example_sentences.english: The kids are playing in a safe spot in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]が公[こう]園[えん]の安[あん]全[ぜん]な場[ば]所[しょ]で遊[あそ]んでいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 雪の日は、ゆっくり運転したほうが安全ですよ。
example_sentences.english: On snowy days, it's safer to drive slowly.
example_sentences.furigana: 雪[ゆき]の日[ひ]は、ゆっくり運[うん]転[てん]したほうが安[あん]全[ぜん]ですよ。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 危（き）＋険（けん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Danger (危) that's steep (険): risky.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="険">precipitous</kanji> place is all sheer drops and loose footing, so setting foot on one is plainly <vocabulary form="危険">dangerous</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so な goes before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 携帯を見ながら自転車に乗るのは危険です。
example_sentences.english: Riding a bike while looking at your phone is dangerous.
example_sentences.furigana: 携[けい]帯[たい]を見[み]ながら自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]に乗[の]るのは危[き]険[けん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 警官が危険な場所を教えてくれました。
example_sentences.english: A police officer told us which places were dangerous.
example_sentences.furigana: 警[けい]官[かん]が危[き]険[けん]な場[ば]所[しょ]を教[おし]えてくれました。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫にはこの薬は危険かもしれない。
example_sentences.english: This medicine might be dangerous for cats.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]にはこの薬[くすり]は危[き]険[けん]かもしれない。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 適（てき）＋当（とう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Fitting (適) the situation (当): suitable, or careless.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="適">suitable</kanji> pick is the one that <kanji form="当">hit</kanji>s the target dead center, and a pick that lands there is <vocabulary form="適当">appropriate</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so な sits before the noun it describes.
items.description: In careful use 適当 means fitting or suitable. In casual speech it often means the opposite: something done at random, with little thought.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議に適当な部屋を探しています。
example_sentences.english: We're looking for a suitable room for the meeting.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]に適[てき]当[とう]な部屋[へや]を探[さが]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は料理のとき、塩を適当に入れる。
example_sentences.english: When my older brother cooks, he just throws in salt without measuring.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は料[りょう]理[り]のとき、塩[しお]を適[てき]当[とう]に入[い]れる。

example_sentences.japanese: 質問に適当に答えないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don't answer the questions carelessly.
example_sentences.furigana: 質[しつ]問[もん]に適[てき]当[とう]に答[こた]えないでください。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 正（しょう）＋直（じき）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Correct (正) and straight (直): honest.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone who keeps every dealing <kanji form="正">correct</kanji> and answers you <kanji form="直">straightaway</kanji>, with nothing bent or held back, is <vocabulary form="正直">honest</vocabulary>. As a な adjective, it takes な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 正直に言うと、その映画はつまらなかった。
example_sentences.english: To be honest, that movie was boring.
example_sentences.furigana: 正[しょう]直[じき]に言[い]うと、その映[えい]画[が]はつまらなかった。

example_sentences.japanese: 正直な客は、多すぎたお釣りを店に返しました。
example_sentences.english: The honest customer gave the extra change back to the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 正[しょう]直[じき]な客[きゃく]は、多[おお]すぎたお釣[つ]りを店[みせ]に返[かえ]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は正直に理由を話しました。
example_sentences.english: He honestly told us the reason.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は正[しょう]直[じき]に理[り]由[ゆう]を話[はな]しました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: 'My own way' repeated: selfish.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <reading>wagon mama</reading> drags the family cart to whatever shop she fancies and never asks where anyone else wants to go. Putting your own way ahead of everyone else's is <vocabulary form="わがまま">selfish</vocabulary>, and that pushy <reading>わがまま</reading> sound carries the same trait.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子がわがままを言うので、スーパーに行くのは大変です。
example_sentences.english: My son throws fits, so going to the supermarket is a real ordeal.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]がわがままを言[い]うので、スーパーに行[い]くのは大[たい]変[へん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 恋人はわがままで、いつもレストランを自分で選ぶ。
example_sentences.english: My partner is selfish and always picks the restaurant.
example_sentences.furigana: 恋[こい]人[びと]はわがままで、いつもレストランを自[じ]分[ぶん]で選[えら]ぶ。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日だけは私のわがままを聞いてくれませんか。
example_sentences.english: Just for today, could you let me have my way?
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]だけは私[わたし]のわがままを聞[き]いてくれませんか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 立（りっ）＋派（ぱ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 立 りつ → りっ. Handakuon: 派 は → ぱ.
items.mnemonic_text: Standing (立) in a fine faction (派): splendid.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="派">faction</kanji> that can <kanji form="立">stand</kanji> tall on its own, propped up by nothing, is an impressive thing, and impressive is exactly <vocabulary form="立派">splendid / fine</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so な slots in ahead of the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父の家には立派な庭があります。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather's house has a magnificent garden.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]の家[いえ]には立[りっ]派[ぱ]な庭[にわ]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で荷物を全部運んで、立派だったね。
example_sentences.english: You carried all the luggage by yourself. Well done.
example_sentences.furigana: 一人[ひとり]で荷[に]物[もつ]を全[ぜん]部[ぶ]運[はこ]んで、立[りっ]派[ぱ]だったね。

example_sentences.japanese: この魚は大きくて立派ですね。
example_sentences.english: What a big, fine fish this is.
example_sentences.furigana: この魚[さかな]は大[おお]きくて立[りっ]派[ぱ]ですね。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 無（む）＋理（り）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: No (無) logic (理): unreasonable.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A demand with <kanji form="無">nothing</kanji> behind it in the way of <kanji form="理">logic</kanji> cannot be argued for and cannot be met, which makes it <vocabulary form="無理">unreasonable / impossible</vocabulary>. As a な adjective, it needs な before any noun it modifies.

example_sentences.japanese: 一週間で漢字を三百覚えるのは無理だよ。
example_sentences.english: Memorizing three hundred kanji in one week is impossible.
example_sentences.furigana: 一[いっ]週[しゅう]間[かん]で漢[かん]字[じ]を三[さん]百[びゃく]覚[おぼ]えるのは無[む]理[り]だよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪のときは無理して働かないほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: When you have a cold, you shouldn't push yourself to work.
example_sentences.furigana: 風邪[かぜ]のときは無[む]理[り]して働[はたら]かないほうがいい。

example_sentences.japanese: 車が欲しいと言ったら、父に「無理だ」と言われた。
example_sentences.english: When I said I wanted a car, my dad told me, "No way."
example_sentences.furigana: 車[くるま]が欲[ほ]しいと言[い]ったら、父[ちち]に「無[む]理[り]だ」と言[い]われた。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 無（む）＋駄（だ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: No (無) worth left: wasteful.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A mule hauls a <kanji form="駄">burdensome</kanji> load all day and brings back <kanji form="無">nothing</kanji> for it, so every step of that trip was <vocabulary form="無駄">wasteful / useless</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so な belongs before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は食べ物を無駄にするのが嫌いです。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother hates wasting food.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]は食[た]べ物[もの]を無[む]駄[だ]にするのが嫌[きら]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 使わない物を買うのは、お金の無駄です。
example_sentences.english: Buying things you won't use is a waste of money.
example_sentences.furigana: 使[つか]わない物[もの]を買[か]うのは、お金[かね]の無[む]駄[だ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 無駄な話が多くて、授業が終わらない。
example_sentences.english: There's so much pointless chatter that class never ends.
example_sentences.furigana: 無[む]駄[だ]な話[はなし]が多[おお]くて、授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]が終[お]わらない。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 簡（かん）＋単（たん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A bamboo (竹) slip, single (単) point: simple.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A job cut back to pure <kanji form="簡">brevity</kanji>, with nothing left over to explain, is a <vocabulary form="簡単">simple</vocabulary> one. As a な adjective, it takes な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: この料理は簡単なので、子供でも作れます。
example_sentences.english: This dish is simple, so even a child can make it.
example_sentences.furigana: この料[りょう]理[り]は簡[かん]単[たん]なので、子[こ]供[ども]でも作[つく]れます。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅までの道は簡単だから、地図は要りません。
example_sentences.english: The way to the station is easy, so you won't need a map.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]までの道[みち]は簡[かん]単[たん]だから、地[ち]図[ず]は要[い]りません。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は難しい問題を簡単に説明してくれました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher explained the hard problem in a simple way.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は難[むずか]しい問[もん]題[だい]を簡[かん]単[たん]に説[せつ]明[めい]してくれました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 複（ふく）＋雑（ざつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Doubled (複) and mixed (雑): complicated.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A plan built from <kanji form="複">doubled</kanji>, overlapping layers and stuffed with <kanji form="雑">miscellaneous</kanji> odd parts is a <vocabulary form="複雑">complicated</vocabulary> one. As a な adjective, it takes な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい携帯は複雑で、祖父はまだ使えません。
example_sentences.english: The new phone is so complicated that my grandfather still can't use it.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい携[けい]帯[たい]は複[ふく]雑[ざつ]で、祖[そ]父[ふ]はまだ使[つか]えません。

example_sentences.japanese: この駅の地下は複雑だから、出口の番号を覚えてください。
example_sentences.english: The underground part of this station is confusing, so remember your exit number.
example_sentences.furigana: この駅[えき]の地[ち]下[か]は複[ふく]雑[ざつ]だから、出[で]口[ぐち]の番[ばん]号[ごう]を覚[おぼ]えてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 税金の書類は複雑なので、専門家に手伝ってもらいました。
example_sentences.english: The tax forms were complicated, so I had an expert help me.
example_sentences.furigana: 税[ぜい]金[きん]の書[しょ]類[るい]は複[ふく]雑[ざつ]なので、専[せん]門[もん]家[か]に手伝[てつだ]ってもらいました。
