items.word_type: な adjective, noun, の adjective
items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 得（とく）＋意（い）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Gaining (得) meaning (意): one's forte.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji form="得">Getting</kanji> the exact result your <kanji form="意">heart</kanji> aimed at, time after time, is what being <vocabulary form="得意">good at</vocabulary> something feels like. It is a な adjective, so it takes な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫は高い所に登るのが得意だ。
example_sentences.english: Cats are good at climbing up to high places.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]は高[たか]い所[ところ]に登[のぼ]るのが得[とく]意[い]だ。

example_sentences.japanese: 数学が得意な兄に宿題を教えてもらいました。
example_sentences.english: My older brother, who is good at math, helped me with my homework.
example_sentences.furigana: 数[すう]学[がく]が得[とく]意[い]な兄[あに]に宿[しゅく]題[だい]を教[おし]えてもらいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は絵が得意なので、店の看板を作りました。
example_sentences.english: She is good at drawing, so she made the sign for the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は絵[え]が得[とく]意[い]なので、店[みせ]の看[かん]板[ばん]を作[つく]りました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 苦（にが）＋手（て）.
items.mnemonic_text: A bitter (苦) hand (手): a weak point.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A task that brings your <kanji form="手">hand</kanji> nothing but <kanji form="苦">suffering</kanji> every time you try it is one you are <vocabulary form="苦手">bad at</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so it takes な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は朝早く起きるのが苦手です。
example_sentences.english: I'm bad at getting up early in the morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は朝[あさ]早[はや]く起[お]きるのが苦[にが]手[て]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は野菜が苦手だから、母は小さく切ってご飯に入れる。
example_sentences.english: My little brother doesn't like vegetables, so Mom cuts them small and hides them in his rice.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は野[や]菜[さい]が苦[にが]手[て]だから、母[はは]は小[ちい]さく切[き]ってご飯[はん]に入[い]れる。

example_sentences.japanese: 寒い冬が苦手なので、来年は南の町に住みたい。
example_sentences.english: I can't stand cold winters, so next year I want to live in a town down south.
example_sentences.furigana: 寒[さむ]い冬[ふゆ]が苦[にが]手[て]なので、来[らい]年[ねん]は南[みなみ]の町[まち]に住[す]みたい。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 自（じ）＋由（ゆう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: One's own (自) reason (由): free.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When your <kanji form="自">self</kanji> is the only <kanji form="由">reason</kanji> you need for what you do, you have <vocabulary form="自由">freedom</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so it takes な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: この図書館の本は自由に読んでもいいです。
example_sentences.english: You're free to read any of the books in this library.
example_sentences.furigana: この図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]の本[ほん]は自[じ]由[ゆう]に読[よ]んでもいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は予定がないので、自由な時間がたくさんあります。
example_sentences.english: I have no plans this weekend, so I have lots of free time.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]は予[よ]定[てい]がないので、自[じ]由[ゆう]な時[じ]間[かん]がたくさんあります。

example_sentences.japanese: 大学に入ってから、自由に旅行に行けるようになりました。
example_sentences.english: Since starting university, I've been able to travel wherever I like.
example_sentences.furigana: 大[だい]学[がく]に入[はい]ってから、自[じ]由[ゆう]に旅[りょ]行[こう]に行[い]けるようになりました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 平（へい）＋気（き）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Flat (平) energy (気): unbothered.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Let your <kanji form="気">spirit</kanji> lie as <kanji form="平">flat</kanji> and cool as a freshly mown field, and you stay <vocabulary form="平気">calm</vocabulary> no matter what happens. As a な adjective, it takes な before the noun it describes.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は辛い物を平気な顔で食べます。
example_sentences.english: My dad eats spicy food without batting an eye.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は辛[から]い物[もの]を平[へい]気[き]な顔[かお]で食[た]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は暗い道を一人で歩くのが平気です。
example_sentences.english: My little sister doesn't mind walking down dark streets alone.
example_sentences.furigana: 妹[いもうと]は暗[くら]い道[みち]を一人[ひとり]で歩[ある]くのが平[へい]気[き]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 足は少し痛いですが、平気です。
example_sentences.english: My leg hurts a little, but I'm okay.
example_sentences.furigana: 足[あし]は少[すこ]し痛[いた]いですが、平[へい]気[き]です。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 残（ざん）＋念（ねん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A remaining (残) thought (念): a shame.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The one <kanji form="念">wish</kanji> you never acted on is the part that <kanji form="残">remains</kanji> unburied after the chance is gone. That is what <vocabulary form="残念">regrettable</vocabulary> names, and as a な adjective it takes な before its noun.

example_sentences.japanese: 残念ですが、その日は会議があって行けません。
example_sentences.english: Unfortunately, I have a meeting that day, so I can't go.
example_sentences.furigana: 残[ざん]念[ねん]ですが、その日[ひ]は会[かい]議[ぎ]があって行[い]けません。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の前のあの喫茶店が無くなって、本当に残念です。
example_sentences.english: It's a real shame that café in front of the station is gone.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]のあの喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]が無[な]くなって、本[ほん]当[とう]に残[ざん]念[ねん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 残念な結果でしたが、次の試験のためにまた勉強します。
example_sentences.english: The result was disappointing, but I'll study again for the next exam.
example_sentences.furigana: 残[ざん]念[ねん]な結[けっ]果[か]でしたが、次[つぎ]の試[し]験[けん]のためにまた勉[べん]強[きょう]します。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 届（とど）＋く.
items.mnemonic_text: Stretching out to reach: todoku.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="届">reach</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="届く">to reach</vocabulary> word are the same character, so they mean the same thing. With く on the end it is intransitive, so the parcel arrives on its own with no one delivering it.
items.reading_mnemonic: The runner tosses the parcel from the doorway and it skids across the tatami alone, stopping like a boat bumping <reading>to a dock</reading> right beside the body. That is <reading>とどく</reading>, a parcel managing <vocabulary form="届く">to reach</vocabulary> its place by itself.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国の友人から大きい荷物が届きました。
example_sentences.english: A big package arrived from a friend abroad.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]の友[ゆう]人[じん]から大[おお]きい荷[に]物[もつ]が届[とど]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫の上の箱に手が届かない。
example_sentences.english: I can't reach the box on top of the fridge.
example_sentences.furigana: 冷[れい]蔵[ぞう]庫[こ]の上[うえ]の箱[はこ]に手[て]が届[とど]かない。

example_sentences.japanese: 後ろの席まで先生の声が届かなかった。
example_sentences.english: The teacher's voice didn't carry to the back seats.
example_sentences.furigana: 後[うし]ろの席[せき]まで先[せん]生[せい]の声[こえ]が届[とど]かなかった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 届（とど）＋ける.
items.mnemonic_text: Reaching it out to someone: todokeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="届">deliver</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="届ける">to deliver</vocabulary> word are the same character with the same meaning. The ける ending makes it transitive, so now someone is carrying a parcel and handing it to you.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already learned 「とど」 from 届く, this word's intransitive partner, so its transitive form is simply <reading>とどける</reading> for <vocabulary form="届ける">to deliver</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 落とした財布を交番に届けました。
example_sentences.english: I took the wallet someone dropped to the police box.
example_sentences.furigana: 落[お]とした財[さい]布[ふ]を交[こう]番[ばん]に届[とど]けました。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母の家に果物を届けに行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to take some fruit over to my aunt's house.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔母[おば]の家[いえ]に果物[くだもの]を届[とど]けに行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: この店は昼ご飯を会社まで届けてくれます。
example_sentences.english: This shop delivers lunch right to your office.
example_sentences.furigana: この店[みせ]は昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を会[かい]社[しゃ]まで届[とど]けてくれます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 治（なお）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: The body governing itself back to health: naoru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When a fever or a sore throat <kanji form="治">calms down</kanji> and goes quiet on its own, with no one treating it, the body is starting to <vocabulary form="治る">recover</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Nao was stuck in bed a week with fever, then jogs onto the sports field and out-runs the whole class. The cheer of <reading>Nao rules</reading> again is <reading>なおる</reading>, the sound of a body that gets better on its own and <vocabulary form="治る">recovers</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 足が治ったら、また公園を走りたいです。
example_sentences.english: Once my leg heals, I want to run in the park again.
example_sentences.furigana: 足[あし]が治[なお]ったら、また公[こう]園[えん]を走[はし]りたいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬の病気が治って、また元気に歩けるようになった。
example_sentences.english: The dog got over its illness and can walk around happily again.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]の病[びょう]気[き]が治[なお]って、また元[げん]気[き]に歩[ある]けるようになった。

example_sentences.japanese: 一週間休んだのに、風邪がまだ治りません。
example_sentences.english: I rested for a whole week, but my cold still hasn't gone away.
example_sentences.furigana: 一[いっ]週[しゅう]間[かん]休[やす]んだのに、風邪[かぜ]がまだ治[なお]りません。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 伝（つた）＋わる.
items.mnemonic_text: The message passing along on its own: tsutawaru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A message that will <kanji form="伝">go along</kanji> by itself, passed from mouth to mouth with no one carrying it, is one that comes <vocabulary form="伝わる">to be conveyed</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 伝 is 「つた」 from 伝える, so for a word <vocabulary form="伝わる">to be conveyed</vocabulary> across a crowd is <reading>つたわる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の気持ちは彼女に伝わったと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think my feelings got through to her.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の気[き]持[も]ちは彼[かの]女[じょ]に伝[つた]わったと思[おも]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 英語で話したのに、意味が全然伝わらなかった。
example_sentences.english: I spoke in English, but the meaning didn't come across at all.
example_sentences.furigana: 英[えい]語[ご]で話[はな]したのに、意[い]味[み]が全[ぜん]然[ぜん]伝[つた]わらなかった。

example_sentences.japanese: この町の伝統は親から子供に伝わります。
example_sentences.english: In this town, traditions are passed down from parents to children.
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]の伝[でん]統[とう]は親[おや]から子[こ]供[ども]に伝[つた]わります。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 迎（むか）＋える.
items.mnemonic_text: Going out on the road to meet someone: mukaeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You throw the front door open, step out onto the path, and draw your visitor inside by both hands: doing that to a guest is how you <vocabulary form="迎える">welcome / greet</vocabulary> them.
items.reading_mnemonic: A cow pulls up in a taxi with one long <reading>moo-car</reading> honk. You throw the front door open, step onto the path and draw her in by both hooves, <reading>むかえる</reading>, to <vocabulary form="迎える">welcome</vocabulary> her.

example_sentences.japanese: 父が駅まで弟を迎えに行きました。
example_sentences.english: Dad went to the station to pick up my little brother.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]が駅[えき]まで弟[おとうと]を迎[むか]えに行[い]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 旅館の人たちが笑って客を迎えました。
example_sentences.english: The staff at the inn greeted the guests with a smile.
example_sentences.furigana: 旅[りょ]館[かん]の人[ひと]たちが笑[わら]って客[きゃく]を迎[むか]えました。

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の春、うちは新しい猫を家族に迎えました。
example_sentences.english: This spring, we welcomed a new cat into the family.
example_sentences.furigana: 今年[ことし]の春[はる]、うちは新[あたら]しい猫[ねこ]を家[か]族[ぞく]に迎[むか]えました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 見（み）＋つかる.
items.mnemonic_text: Something turns up to the eye: mitsukaru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A missing sock drifts out into the open until a wandering eye on legs happens to <kanji form="見">see</kanji> it, and with no one searching for it that sock has come <vocabulary form="見つかる">to be found</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 見 is 「み」 from 見る, so for a lost thing <vocabulary form="見つかる">to be found</vocabulary> at last is <reading>みつかる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 無くした財布が交番で見つかりました。
example_sentences.english: The wallet I lost turned up at the police box.
example_sentences.furigana: 無[な]くした財[さい]布[ふ]が交[こう]番[ばん]で見[み]つかりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末に泊まる安いホテルが見つからなくて困っています。
example_sentences.english: I can't find a cheap hotel for the weekend, and I'm stuck.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]に泊[と]まる安[やす]いホテルが見[み]つからなくて困[こま]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄にいい仕事が見つかったらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard my older brother found a good job.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]にいい仕[し]事[ごと]が見[み]つかったらしい。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 決（き）＋まる.
items.mnemonic_text: The levee breaks on its own: kimaru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="決">decide</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="決まる">to be decided</vocabulary> word are the same word. This form just means the matter settles on its own, with nobody there to make the call.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Kiki</reading> the tree spirit watches the water drop leave the brush and the hooked stroke swing. Once neither can be pulled back, she sighs <reading>きまる</reading>, for the matter has come <vocabulary form="決まる">to be decided</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月の旅行の場所がまだ決まらない。
example_sentences.english: We still haven't settled where next month's trip is going.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]月[げつ]の旅[りょ]行[こう]の場[ば]所[しょ]がまだ決[き]まらない。

example_sentences.japanese: 会議は金曜日の午後に決まりました。
example_sentences.english: The meeting has been set for Friday afternoon.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]は金[きん]曜[よう]日[び]の午[ご]後[ご]に決[き]まりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 試験の結果で、入る大学が決まる。
example_sentences.english: Your exam results decide which university you get into.
example_sentences.furigana: 試[し]験[けん]の結[けっ]果[か]で、入[はい]る大[だい]学[がく]が決[き]まる。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 決（き）＋める.
items.mnemonic_text: Breaking through to a decision: kimeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="決">decide</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="決める">to decide</vocabulary> word are the same word. This form adds a person to the scene: you are the one who makes the call and fixes the outcome.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 決 is 「き」 from 決まる, so for you <vocabulary form="決める">to decide</vocabulary> the outcome yourself is <reading>きめる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 晩ご飯に何を作るか、まだ決めていません。
example_sentences.english: I haven't decided what to make for dinner yet.
example_sentences.furigana: 晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]に何[なに]を作[つく]るか、まだ決[き]めていません。

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は長い時間考えて、黒い靴に決めました。
example_sentences.english: After thinking for ages, my little sister went with the black shoes.
example_sentences.furigana: 妹[いもうと]は長[なが]い時[じ]間[かん]考[かんが]えて、黒[くろ]い靴[くつ]に決[き]めました。

example_sentences.japanese: 夫と話して、息子の名前を決めました。
example_sentences.english: My husband and I talked it over and chose our son's name.
example_sentences.furigana: 夫[おっと]と話[はな]して、息子[むすこ]の名[な]前[まえ]を決[き]めました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 続（つづ）＋く.
items.mnemonic_text: Thread sold onward without a break: tsuzuku.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="続">continue</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="続く">to continue</vocabulary> word are the same word. This is the form that runs on by itself, the thread unrolling off the spool with no one feeding it.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 続 is 「つづ」 from 続き, so for a spell of good weather <vocabulary form="続く">to continue</vocabulary> on its own is <reading>つづく</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 電話の話が二時間も続いて、耳が痛くなった。
example_sentences.english: The phone call went on for two whole hours, and my ear started to hurt.
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]話[わ]の話[はなし]が二[に]時[じ]間[かん]も続[つづ]いて、耳[みみ]が痛[いた]くなった。

example_sentences.japanese: この道は海まで続きます。
example_sentences.english: This road runs all the way to the sea.
example_sentences.furigana: この道[みち]は海[うみ]まで続[つづ]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 暑い日が続くので、冷たいお茶をたくさん飲んでいます。
example_sentences.english: The hot days keep coming, so I'm drinking lots of cold tea.
example_sentences.furigana: 暑[あつ]い日[ひ]が続[つづ]くので、冷[つめ]たいお茶[ちゃ]をたくさん飲[の]んでいます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 続（つづ）＋ける.
items.mnemonic_text: Keeping the thread going: tsuzukeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="続">continue</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="続ける">to continue</vocabulary> word are the same word. This is the form with a hand on the spool, someone pulling more thread off on purpose.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 続 is 「つづ」 from 続き, so for a worker <vocabulary form="続ける">to continue</vocabulary> a task without a break is <reading>つづける</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は八十歳ですが、今も仕事を続けています。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother is eighty, but she's still working.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]は八[はち]十[じゅう]歳[さい]ですが、今[いま]も仕[し]事[ごと]を続[つづ]けています。

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の勉強は毎日続けたほうがいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: You should keep up your Japanese study every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]語[ご]の勉[べん]強[きょう]は毎[まい]日[にち]続[つづ]けたほうがいいですよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんが朝まで泣き続けて、誰も寝られなかった。
example_sentences.english: The baby kept crying until morning, and nobody got any sleep.
example_sentences.furigana: 赤[あか]ちゃんが朝[あさ]まで泣[な]き続[つづ]けて、誰[だれ]も寝[ね]られなかった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 増（ふ）＋える.
items.mnemonic_text: Earth piling ever higher: fueru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="増">increase</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="増える">to increase</vocabulary> word are the same word. This is the form that climbs on its own, the mound rising past the signpost with no one piling it up.
items.reading_mnemonic: The mound beside the signpost began as only a <reading>few</reading> loads of earth, yet each dawn it stands taller with no one piling it on. Watching it <vocabulary form="増える">increase</vocabulary> by itself, you whisper <reading>ふえる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏になると、公園に来る人が増えます。
example_sentences.english: When summer comes, more people visit the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 夏[なつ]になると、公[こう]園[えん]に来[く]る人[ひと]が増[ふ]えます。

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に住む外国人は去年より増えました。
example_sentences.english: More foreigners live in Japan than last year.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]に住[す]む外[がい]国[こく]人[じん]は去[きょ]年[ねん]より増[ふ]えました。

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字を覚えたので、読める本が増えました。
example_sentences.english: I've learned kanji, so there are more books I can read now.
example_sentences.furigana: 漢[かん]字[じ]を覚[おぼ]えたので、読[よ]める本[ほん]が増[ふ]えました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 増（ふ）＋やす.
items.mnemonic_text: Piling more earth up: fuyasu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="増">increase</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="増やす">to increase</vocabulary> word are the same word. This is the form with a worker in it, someone shovelling load after load of earth on to raise the mound.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 増 is 「ふ」 from 増える, so for someone <vocabulary form="増やす">to increase</vocabulary> the pile on purpose is <reading>ふやす</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 客を増やすために、店の前に大きい看板を置きました。
example_sentences.english: To bring in more customers, they put a big sign in front of the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 客[きゃく]を増[ふ]やすために、店[みせ]の前[まえ]に大[おお]きい看[かん]板[ばん]を置[お]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: お弁当の野菜を少し増やしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please put a few more vegetables in the boxed lunch.
example_sentences.furigana: お弁[べん]当[とう]の野[や]菜[さい]を少[すこ]し増[ふ]やしてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 趣味の仲間をもっと増やしたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to make more friends who share my hobby.
example_sentences.furigana: 趣[しゅ]味[み]の仲[なか]間[ま]をもっと増[ふ]やしたいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 減（へ）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: Water cut down to less: heru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="減">decrease</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="減る">to decrease</vocabulary> word are the same word. This is the form that falls on its own, the water level dropping once the plug is gone with no one draining it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Pull the bathhouse plug and a clump of <reading>hair</reading> spins at the drain as all the water races out. Watching the level <vocabulary form="減る">decrease</vocabulary> on its own, you murmur <reading>へる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫の牛乳が、朝より減っている。
example_sentences.english: There's less milk in the fridge than there was this morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 冷[れい]蔵[ぞう]庫[こ]の牛[ぎゅう]乳[にゅう]が、朝[あさ]より減[へ]っている。

example_sentences.japanese: この学校の生徒は十年で半分に減りました。
example_sentences.english: This school's student numbers have halved in ten years.
example_sentences.furigana: この学[がっ]校[こう]の生[せい]徒[と]は十[じゅう]年[ねん]で半[はん]分[ぶん]に減[へ]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 忙しくなって、友達と遊ぶ時間が減りました。
example_sentences.english: I got busy, so I have less time to hang out with friends.
example_sentences.furigana: 忙[いそが]しくなって、友[とも]達[だち]と遊[あそ]ぶ時[じ]間[かん]が減[へ]りました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 減（へ）＋らす.
items.mnemonic_text: Cutting the water level down: herasu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="減">decrease</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="減らす">decrease</vocabulary> word are the same thing. The trailing kana make it transitive, so you are the one cutting an amount down, not the amount falling on its own.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know this sound from 減る, so the transitive twin, the one where you <vocabulary form="減らす">decrease</vocabulary> something else, is <reading>へらす</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は医者に言われて、お酒を減らしました。
example_sentences.english: My father cut back on drinking after the doctor told him to.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は医[い]者[しゃ]に言[い]われて、お酒[さけ]を減[へ]らしました。

example_sentences.japanese: 砂糖を少し減らしたら、もっとおいしくなりました。
example_sentences.english: When I cut back the sugar a little, it tasted even better.
example_sentences.furigana: 砂[さ]糖[とう]を少[すこ]し減[へ]らしたら、もっとおいしくなりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 会社は来月から会議を減らすらしいです。
example_sentences.english: I hear the company is cutting down on meetings starting next month.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]社[しゃ]は来[らい]月[げつ]から会[かい]議[ぎ]を減[へ]らすらしいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 壊（こわ）＋す.
items.mnemonic_text: A soil clump crumbling in the hand: kowasu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take something that works fine, swing a hammer at it, and leave it in pieces on the floor. Doing that to an object on purpose is what it is to <vocabulary form="壊す">break</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: A <reading>cow</reading> grips your hammer in her teeth, swings it at the perfectly good radio and leaves it in pieces on the floor. She moos <reading>こわす</reading>, proud of how hard she can <vocabulary form="壊す">break</vocabulary> things.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟がまた私のカメラを壊しました。
example_sentences.english: My little brother broke my camera again.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]がまた私[わたし]のカメラを壊[こわ]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の古い家は来週壊されるそうです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently the old house next door is getting torn down next week.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]の古[ふる]い家[いえ]は来[らい]週[しゅう]壊[こわ]されるそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 箱を開けるとき、中の皿を壊さないでください。
example_sentences.english: When you open the box, please don't break the plates inside.
example_sentences.furigana: 箱[はこ]を開[あ]けるとき、中[なか]の皿[さら]を壊[こわ]さないでください。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 壊（こわ）＋れる.
items.mnemonic_text: The clump crumbling apart on its own: kowareru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: One morning the old radio just goes silent, and no switch brings it back. A thing that stops working with nobody laying a hand on it has come to <vocabulary form="壊れる">break</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know this sound from 壊す, so the twin where a thing <vocabulary form="壊れる">breaks</vocabulary> on its own, with no one touching it, is <reading>こわれる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 暑い日に冷蔵庫が壊れて、本当に困りました。
example_sentences.english: The fridge broke on a hot day, and I was really stuck.
example_sentences.furigana: 暑[あつ]い日[ひ]に冷[れい]蔵[ぞう]庫[こ]が壊[こわ]れて、本[ほん]当[とう]に困[こま]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: このドアは壊れているので、あちらから入ってください。
example_sentences.english: This door is broken, so please go in over there.
example_sentences.furigana: このドアは壊[こわ]れているので、あちらから入[はい]ってください。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母のラジオは古いのに、まだ壊れません。
example_sentences.english: Grandma's radio is old, but it still hasn't broken.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]のラジオは古[ふる]いのに、まだ壊[こわ]れません。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 育（そだ）＋てる.
items.mnemonic_text: Nurturing flesh (月) to grow: sodateru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="育">bring up</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="育てる">raise</vocabulary> word are the same. The trailing kana make it transitive, so you are the one bringing a child or an animal up.
items.reading_mnemonic: You keep the cocoon under its warm lid for a whole month, dripping in a little <reading>soda</reading> each day, until something alive crawls out. That patient feeding is how you <vocabulary form="育てる">raise</vocabulary> it, <reading>そだてる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母は庭で野菜を育てています。
example_sentences.english: My aunt grows vegetables in her garden.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔母[おば]は庭[にわ]で野[や]菜[さい]を育[そだ]てています。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は一人で三人の子供を育てました。
example_sentences.english: He raised three children on his own.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は一人[ひとり]で三[さん]人[にん]の子[こ]供[ども]を育[そだ]てました。

example_sentences.japanese: この猫は赤ちゃんのときから私たちが育てました。
example_sentences.english: We've raised this cat since it was a baby.
example_sentences.furigana: この猫[ねこ]は赤[あか]ちゃんのときから私[わたし]たちが育[そだ]てました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 育（そだ）＋つ.
items.mnemonic_text: Growing on its own: sodatsu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="育">bring up</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="育つ">grow up</vocabulary> word are the same. The trailing kana make it intransitive, so the child comes up on its own and no one is raising it.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already met this sound in 育てる, so the twin where someone simply <vocabulary form="育つ">grows up</vocabulary> on their own is <reading>そだつ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は海の近くの小さい町で育ちました。
example_sentences.english: My mother grew up in a small town near the sea.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は海[うみ]の近[ちか]くの小[ちい]さい町[まち]で育[そだ]ちました。

example_sentences.japanese: 寒い所では、この木はあまり育ちません。
example_sentences.english: This tree doesn't grow well in cold places.
example_sentences.furigana: 寒[さむ]い所[ところ]では、この木[き]はあまり育[そだ]ちません。

example_sentences.japanese: 息子はよく食べて、大きく育ちました。
example_sentences.english: My son ate well and grew up big.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]はよく食[た]べて、大[おお]きく育[そだ]ちました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 乾（かわ）＋かす.
items.mnemonic_text: Drying a dry (乾) stalk further: kawakasu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You hold a soaked towel flat in front of the heater and keep it there until not one drop is left. Forcing all the water out of a wet thing like that is what it is to <vocabulary form="乾かす">dry</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: You hold the soaked towel in front of the heater, and it roars like the blower at a <reading>car wash</reading> until not one drop is left. That is how you <vocabulary form="乾かす">dry</vocabulary> it, <reading>かわかす</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 寝る前に髪を乾かしたほうがいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: You'd better dry your hair before you go to bed.
example_sentences.furigana: 寝[ね]る前[まえ]に髪[かみ]を乾[かわ]かしたほうがいいですよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の日は、部屋の中で服を乾かします。
example_sentences.english: On rainy days, I dry my clothes indoors.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]は、部屋[へや]の中[なか]で服[ふく]を乾[かわ]かします。

example_sentences.japanese: 洗った靴を外に出して乾かしました。
example_sentences.english: I put my washed shoes outside to dry.
example_sentences.furigana: 洗[あら]った靴[くつ]を外[そと]に出[だ]して乾[かわ]かしました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 乾（かわ）＋く.
items.mnemonic_text: Becoming dry on its own: kawaku.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You peg the washing out in the midday sun and come back to sheets that are stiff, warm, and holding no water at all. A thing losing every drop on its own is what it is to <vocabulary form="乾く">dry</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know this sound from 乾かす, so the twin where something goes <vocabulary form="乾く">dry</vocabulary> on its own, with no heater on it, is <reading>かわく</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 風が強い日は、タオルが早く乾きます。
example_sentences.english: On windy days, towels dry quickly.
example_sentences.furigana: 風[かぜ]が強[つよ]い日[ひ]は、タオルが早[はや]く乾[かわ]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 絵がまだ乾いていないので、上に本を置かないでください。
example_sentences.english: The painting isn't dry yet, so please don't put books on it.
example_sentences.furigana: 絵[え]がまだ乾[かわ]いていないので、上[うえ]に本[ほん]を置[お]かないでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 午後に洗濯したので、シャツは夕方までに乾くはずです。
example_sentences.english: I did the laundry in the afternoon, so the shirts should be dry by evening.
example_sentences.furigana: 午[ご]後[ご]に洗[せん]濯[たく]したので、シャツは夕[ゆう]方[がた]までに乾[かわ]くはずです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 濡（ぬ）＋らす.
items.mnemonic_text: Making something wet on purpose: nurasu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You tip a full watering can straight over the folded picnic blanket until it is soaked through and heavy. Pouring water onto a thing until it is soaked is what it is to <vocabulary form="濡らす">wet</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: A <reading>gnu</reading> grabs the full watering can in its teeth and tips it over your folded picnic blanket until it sags heavy. Soaking it on purpose like that is to <vocabulary form="濡らす">wet</vocabulary> it, <reading>ぬらす</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 書類を濡らさないように、かばんに入れてください。
example_sentences.english: Put the documents in your bag so they don't get wet.
example_sentences.furigana: 書[しょ]類[るい]を濡[ぬ]らさないように、かばんに入[い]れてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 歯ブラシを水で濡らしてから使います。
example_sentences.english: I wet my toothbrush with water before using it.
example_sentences.furigana: 歯[は]ブラシを水[みず]で濡[ぬ]らしてから使[つか]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬を洗うときは、耳を濡らさないでください。
example_sentences.english: When you wash the dog, please don't get its ears wet.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]を洗[あら]うときは、耳[みみ]を濡[ぬ]らさないでください。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 濡（ぬ）＋れる.
items.mnemonic_text: Getting wet by chance: nureru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The sky opens while you are still ten minutes from home with no umbrella, and by the corner your shirt is stuck to your back. Rain landing on you until you are soaked is what it is to <vocabulary form="濡れる">get wet</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know this sound from 濡らす, so the twin where you end up <vocabulary form="濡れる">wet</vocabulary> with no say in it is <reading>ぬれる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 傘を忘れたので、駅から家まで歩いて濡れました。
example_sentences.english: I forgot my umbrella, so I got wet walking home from the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 傘[かさ]を忘[わす]れたので、駅[えき]から家[いえ]まで歩[ある]いて濡[ぬ]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: 雨で地図が濡れて、読めなくなりました。
example_sentences.english: The rain got the map wet, and I couldn't read it anymore.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]で地[ち]図[ず]が濡[ぬ]れて、読[よ]めなくなりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 濡れた手で電気をつけてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You must not turn on the lights with wet hands.
example_sentences.furigana: 濡[ぬ]れた手[て]で電[でん]気[き]をつけてはいけません。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 沸（わ）＋く.
items.mnemonic_text: Water bubbling up on its own: waku.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You set the kettle on a high flame and wait until the surface is rolling over and throwing off steam. Water climbing to that churn on its own is what it is to <vocabulary form="沸く">boil</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Your kettle on the high flame starts rolling and throwing off steam, rattling its lid like a <reading>wok</reading> in a busy kitchen. Water churning like that by itself has begun to <vocabulary form="沸く">boil</vocabulary>, <reading>わく</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 牛乳が沸いたら、砂糖を入れてください。
example_sentences.english: When the milk comes to a boil, add the sugar.
example_sentences.furigana: 牛[ぎゅう]乳[にゅう]が沸[わ]いたら、砂[さ]糖[とう]を入[い]れてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は水が沸くまで、台所で新聞を読んでいました。
example_sentences.english: Grandpa read the newspaper in the kitchen until the water boiled.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は水[みず]が沸[わ]くまで、台[だい]所[どころ]で新[しん]聞[ぶん]を読[よ]んでいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 寒い朝は、水が沸くまで時間がかかります。
example_sentences.english: On cold mornings, it takes a while for the water to boil.
example_sentences.furigana: 寒[さむ]い朝[あさ]は、水[みず]が沸[わ]くまで時[じ]間[かん]がかかります。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 沸（わ）＋かす.
items.mnemonic_text: Heating water until it boils: wakasu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You stand over the pot with the gas turned up full, holding the water on the heat until it roars. Driving water up to a rolling churn yourself is what it is to <vocabulary form="沸かす">boil</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know this sound from 沸く, so the twin where you are the one heating the water up to a churn is <reading>わかす</reading>, to <vocabulary form="沸かす">boil</vocabulary> it.

example_sentences.japanese: 客が来るから、急いでお茶を沸かしましょう。
example_sentences.english: A guest is coming, so let's hurry and boil some tea.
example_sentences.furigana: 客[きゃく]が来[く]るから、急[いそ]いでお茶[ちゃ]を沸[わ]かしましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 山の上で、湖の水を沸かして飲みました。
example_sentences.english: Up on the mountain, we boiled lake water and drank it.
example_sentences.furigana: 山[やま]の上[うえ]で、湖[みずうみ]の水[みず]を沸[わ]かして飲[の]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は水を沸かすのを忘れて、冷たいコーヒーを飲んだ。
example_sentences.english: My little brother forgot to boil the water and drank cold coffee.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は水[みず]を沸[わ]かすのを忘[わす]れて、冷[つめ]たいコーヒーを飲[の]んだ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 燃（も）＋える.
items.mnemonic_text: Fire catching on its own: moeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A dropped match catches the dry grass at the field's edge, and the whole slope is orange before anyone can stand up. Something going up in flame on its own is what it is to <vocabulary form="燃える">burn</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The <reading>mower</reading> on Sei's school field throws a spark into the heap of dry cuttings, and the pile is alight in seconds. Stuff catching and climbing into flame is what it means to <vocabulary form="燃える">burn</vocabulary>, 「<reading>もえる</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の夜、町の古い工場が燃えていました。
example_sentences.english: Last night, an old factory in town was on fire.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]の夜[よる]、町[まち]の古[ふる]い工[こう]場[じょう]が燃[も]えていました。

example_sentences.japanese: この木は濡れているから、全然燃えません。
example_sentences.english: This wood is wet, so it won't burn at all.
example_sentences.furigana: この木[き]は濡[ぬ]れているから、全[ぜん]然[ぜん]燃[も]えません。

example_sentences.japanese: 父が作った晩ご飯が燃えて、家族でパンを食べました。
example_sentences.english: The dinner Dad made went up in flames, so the family ate bread.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]が作[つく]った晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]が燃[も]えて、家[か]族[ぞく]でパンを食[た]べました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 燃（も）＋やす.
items.mnemonic_text: Setting fire to something: moyasu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You rake the fallen leaves into a heap in the yard, hold a lighter to one edge, and step back as it takes. Setting a thing alight on purpose is what it is to <vocabulary form="燃やす">burn</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know this sound from 燃える, so the twin where you are the one lighting the fire is <reading>もやす</reading>, to <vocabulary form="燃やす">burn</vocabulary> something.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は前の恋人からの手紙を全部燃やした。
example_sentences.english: She burned every letter from her ex.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は前[まえ]の恋[こい]人[びと]からの手[て]紙[がみ]を全[ぜん]部[ぶ]燃[も]やした。

example_sentences.japanese: 庭で箱を燃やしてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You're not allowed to burn boxes in the yard.
example_sentences.furigana: 庭[にわ]で箱[はこ]を燃[も]やしてはいけません。

example_sentences.japanese: 寒い夜は、木を燃やして部屋を暖かくします。
example_sentences.english: On cold nights, we burn wood to keep the room warm.
example_sentences.furigana: 寒[さむ]い夜[よる]は、木[き]を燃[も]やして部屋[へや]を暖[あたた]かくします。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 沈（しず）＋む.
items.mnemonic_text: Water swallowing something down: shizumu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A slow leak fills the rowboat until it tips its nose down and slides under the lake, and the water closes flat over the top. A heavy thing dropping below the surface and staying there is what it is to <vocabulary form="沈む">sink</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The free diver breathes out, whispers 「<reading>she zooms</reading>」, and drops straight down to the dark lake bed. Going under the water and staying down there is what it means to <vocabulary form="沈む">sink</vocabulary>, 「<reading>しずむ</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏は夜の八時ごろに日が沈みます。
example_sentences.english: In summer, the sun sets around eight at night.
example_sentences.furigana: 夏[なつ]は夜[よる]の八[はち]時[じ]ごろに日[ひ]が沈[しず]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が作った紙の船は、すぐ湖に沈んだ。
example_sentences.english: The paper boat the kid made sank into the lake right away.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]が作[つく]った紙[かみ]の船[ふね]は、すぐ湖[みずうみ]に沈[しず]んだ。

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の日は、いつも気分が沈むんです。
example_sentences.english: Rainy days always get me down.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]は、いつも気[き]分[ぶん]が沈[しず]むんです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 浮（う）＋かぶ.
items.mnemonic_text: Bobbing lightly on the water: ukabu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You let go of the beach ball under the pool water and it shoots straight back up to sit on the surface. A thing riding on top of the water instead of going under is what it is to <vocabulary form="浮かぶ">float</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You <reading>hook a boot</reading> out of the canal, and it will not stay under no matter how you shove it. It keeps riding back up to the top, and sitting on the surface like that is what it means to <vocabulary form="浮かぶ">float</vocabulary>, 「<reading>うかぶ</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 見て、川に大きい魚が浮かんでいるよ。
example_sentences.english: Look, there's a big fish floating in the river.
example_sentences.furigana: 見[み]て、川[かわ]に大[おお]きい魚[さかな]が浮[う]かんでいるよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 海では体が軽いから、簡単に浮かぶことができます。
example_sentences.english: Your body is light in the sea, so you can float easily.
example_sentences.furigana: 海[うみ]では体[からだ]が軽[かる]いから、簡[かん]単[たん]に浮[う]かぶことができます。

example_sentences.japanese: 試験のとき、答えが全然浮かびませんでした。
example_sentences.english: During the exam, the answers just wouldn't come to me.
example_sentences.furigana: 試[し]験[けん]のとき、答[こた]えが全[ぜん]然[ぜん]浮[う]かびませんでした。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 流（なが）＋れる.
items.mnemonic_text: Water running its course: nagareru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="流">current</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="流れる">flow</vocabulary> word are the same. The trailing kana just make it a verb, water carrying itself along with nobody pushing it.
items.reading_mnemonic: The river guide never stops talking, keeping up one long <reading>nagging rule</reading> about life jackets while the raft is swept on with no paddling. Water carrying things along on its own is what it means to <vocabulary form="流れる">flow</vocabulary>, 「<reading>ながれる</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の中で、好きな歌が流れていた。
example_sentences.english: My favorite song was playing inside the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の中[なか]で、好[す]きな歌[うた]が流[なが]れていた。

example_sentences.japanese: 雨がたくさん降って、道に水が流れています。
example_sentences.english: It rained a lot, and water is running down the street.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]がたくさん降[ふ]って、道[みち]に水[みず]が流[なが]れています。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父の家では、時間がゆっくり流れるようだ。
example_sentences.english: At Grandpa's house, time seems to flow slowly.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]の家[いえ]では、時[じ]間[かん]がゆっくり流[なが]れるようだ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 流（なが）＋す.
items.mnemonic_text: Letting the water run: nagasu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="流">current</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="流す">let flow</vocabulary> word are the same. The trailing kana make it the one you do to something, so you send the water on its way yourself.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know this sound from 流れる, so the twin where you set the water moving yourself is <reading>ながす</reading>, to <vocabulary form="流す">let flow</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 野菜を水で流してから切ります。
example_sentences.english: I rinse the vegetables under water before I cut them.
example_sentences.furigana: 野[や]菜[さい]を水[みず]で流[なが]してから切[き]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 店員は店で古い音楽を流しています。
example_sentences.english: The clerk is playing old music in the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]は店[みせ]で古[ふる]い音[おん]楽[がく]を流[なが]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: 息子が夫の時計をトイレに流しました。
example_sentences.english: My son flushed my husband's watch down the toilet.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]が夫[おっと]の時計[とけい]をトイレに流[なが]しました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 回（まわ）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: Spinning around a loop: mawaru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A wheel jolts loose from the cart and rolls off on its own, going <kanji form="回">round</kanji> and round all the way down the hill. Something spinning in circles by itself is what it is to <vocabulary form="回る">turn</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The loose cart wheel rolls down the hill going round and round, and a <reading>marble</reading> stuck in its hub whirls along with it. Spinning in circles like that is what it means to <vocabulary form="回る">turn</vocabulary>, <reading>まわる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行で、三日で町の店を全部回りました。
example_sentences.english: On the trip, we went around every shop in town in three days.
example_sentences.furigana: 旅[りょ]行[こう]で、三[みっ]日[か]で町[まち]の店[みせ]を全[ぜん]部[ぶ]回[まわ]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: お酒を飲みすぎて、部屋が回っているようだ。
example_sentences.english: I drank too much, and the room seems to be spinning.
example_sentences.furigana: お酒[さけ]を飲[の]みすぎて、部屋[へや]が回[まわ]っているようだ。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬はベッドの上で三回回ってから寝ました。
example_sentences.english: The dog turned around three times on the bed before it went to sleep.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]はベッドの上[うえ]で三[さん]回[かい]回[まわ]ってから寝[ね]ました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 回（まわ）＋す.
items.mnemonic_text: Turning something by hand: mawasu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You grab the stiff crank on the well and force it <kanji form="回">round</kanji>, one hard shove after another, until the bucket starts to rise. Driving a thing in a circle with your own hand is what it is to <vocabulary form="回す">turn</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know this sound from 回る, so the twin where your hand is the thing spinning it is <reading>まわす</reading>, to <vocabulary form="回す">turn</vocabulary> it.

example_sentences.japanese: 鍵を右に回してから、ドアを開けてください。
example_sentences.english: Turn the key to the right, then open the door.
example_sentences.furigana: 鍵[かぎ]を右[みぎ]に回[まわ]してから、ドアを開[あ]けてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 長い授業の後で、先生は首を回した。
example_sentences.english: After the long class, the teacher rolled his neck.
example_sentences.furigana: 長[なが]い授[じゅ]業[ぎょう]の後[あと]で、先[せん]生[せい]は首[くび]を回[まわ]した。

example_sentences.japanese: 面白い写真を、みんなで回して見ました。
example_sentences.english: We passed the funny photo around so everyone could see it.
example_sentences.furigana: 面[おも]白[しろ]い写[しゃ]真[しん]を、みんなで回[まわ]して見[み]ました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 引（ひ）＋っ＋越（こ）＋す.
items.mnemonic_text: Pulling your life over a hill: hikkosu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="引">pull</kanji> every box, every stick of furniture, and your whole life out of one apartment and cart it across town to the next. Dragging your entire household to a new address is what it is to <vocabulary form="引っ越す">move</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫と一緒に、海の近くに引っ越しました。
example_sentences.english: I moved near the sea with my cat.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に、海[うみ]の近[ちか]くに引[ひ]っ越[こ]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 会社が遠くて不便なので、引っ越すつもりです。
example_sentences.english: My office is far and inconvenient, so I plan to move.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]社[しゃ]が遠[とお]くて不[ふ]便[べん]なので、引[ひ]っ越[こ]すつもりです。

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の人が引っ越して、とても静かになった。
example_sentences.english: The neighbors moved out, and it got really quiet.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]の人[ひと]が引[ひ]っ越[こ]して、とても静[しず]かになった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 通（かよ）＋う.
items.mnemonic_text: Passing the same road daily: kayou.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Slip into the <kanji form="通">traffic</kanji> that pours down one road every morning and back every night. Making that same trip over and over, day after day, is what it means <vocabulary form="通う">to commute</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Every morning the same man slips into the traffic pouring down the one road, and the crossing guard sighs <reading>Kai, you</reading> again. Kai making that trip daily is <reading>かよう</reading>, what it means <vocabulary form="通う">to commute</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は毎日バスで大学に通っています。
example_sentences.english: My older brother takes the bus to university every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]は毎[まい]日[にち]バスで大[だい]学[がく]に通[かよ]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は毎週、近くの病院に通っています。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother goes to the hospital nearby every week.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]は毎[まい]週[しゅう]、近[ちか]くの病[びょう]院[いん]に通[かよ]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 引っ越して会社が遠くなったので、今は電車で通っています。
example_sentences.english: I moved and the office got farther away, so now I commute by train.
example_sentences.furigana: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]して会[かい]社[しゃ]が遠[とお]くなったので、今[いま]は電[でん]車[しゃ]で通[かよ]っています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 通（とお）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: Going straight through a road: tooru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="通">traffic</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="通る">to pass through</vocabulary> word are the same word. With this ending it just means something moves along the road and out the far side on its own, with nobody pushing it.
items.reading_mnemonic: The <reading>toll</reading>-gate guard lifts the barrier for one more truck and it rolls straight past him into the dark. A thing that goes in one side of a gap and out the far side on its own is 「<reading>とおる</reading>」, <vocabulary form="通る">to pass through</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この道は車がたくさん通るので、危ないです。
example_sentences.english: Lots of cars go down this road, so it's dangerous.
example_sentences.furigana: この道[みち]は車[くるま]がたくさん通[とお]るので、危[あぶ]ないです。

example_sentences.japanese: 家へ帰るとき、いつも公園の中を通ります。
example_sentences.english: On my way home, I always cut through the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 家[いえ]へ帰[かえ]るとき、いつも公[こう]園[えん]の中[なか]を通[とお]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 窓の外を犬が通るのが見えました。
example_sentences.english: I could see a dog going past outside the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]の外[そと]を犬[いぬ]が通[とお]るのが見[み]えました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 通（とお）＋す.
items.mnemonic_text: Letting something pass through: toosu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="通">traffic</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="通す">to let pass</vocabulary> word are the same. This ending adds a hand on the gate, so someone now moves the traffic through instead of it flowing past on its own.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 通 sounds like とお from 通る, so the hands-on version, <vocabulary form="通す">to let pass</vocabulary>, is just <reading>とおす</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: すみません、ちょっと通してください。
example_sentences.english: Excuse me, could you let me through?
example_sentences.furigana: すみません、ちょっと通[とお]してください。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅員は切符を見てから、客を通しました。
example_sentences.english: The station attendant checked the ticket, then let the passenger through.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]員[いん]は切[きっ]符[ぷ]を見[み]てから、客[きゃく]を通[とお]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 窓を開けて、部屋に風を通しましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's open the window and air out the room.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]を開[あ]けて、部屋[へや]に風[かぜ]を通[とお]しましょう。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 凍（こお）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: Ice locking the water still: kooru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Leave water still in the cold long enough and it turns hard and <kanji form="凍">frozen</kanji> all by itself. Water going solid like that, with nobody freezing it, is <vocabulary form="凍る">to freeze</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Cora</reading> leaves a bucket of water sitting still in the cold overnight, and by dawn it has turned hard all by itself. She taps the ice and says <reading>こおる</reading>, having watched water <vocabulary form="凍る">freeze</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 外に置いておいた水が、朝には凍っていました。
example_sentences.english: The water I'd left outside was frozen by morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[そと]に置[お]いておいた水[みず]が、朝[あさ]には凍[こお]っていました。

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫の中で牛乳が凍っていたので、飲めませんでした。
example_sentences.english: The milk had frozen in the fridge, so I couldn't drink it.
example_sentences.furigana: 冷[れい]蔵[ぞう]庫[こ]の中[なか]で牛[ぎゅう]乳[にゅう]が凍[こお]っていたので、飲[の]めませんでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 冬は道が凍るので、ゆっくり歩いてください。
example_sentences.english: The roads freeze in winter, so please walk slowly.
example_sentences.furigana: 冬[ふゆ]は道[みち]が凍[こお]るので、ゆっくり歩[ある]いてください。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 溶（と）＋ける.
items.mnemonic_text: A shape softening away in water: tokeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Drop a sugar cube into hot tea and stir once. It loses its edges, goes cloudy, and spreads through the water until it is gone, and that is what <vocabulary form="溶ける">to melt / dissolve</vocabulary> looks like.
items.reading_mnemonic: You drop a sugar cube shaped like a little <reading>token</reading> into hot tea and stir once, and its edges blur until it is gone. That vanishing is <reading>とける</reading>, to <vocabulary form="溶ける">dissolve</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 暑かったので、かばんの中のお菓子が溶けていました。
example_sentences.english: It was so hot that the sweets in my bag had melted.
example_sentences.furigana: 暑[あつ]かったので、かばんの中[なか]のお菓[か]子[し]が溶[と]けていました。

example_sentences.japanese: 春になったら、山の雪が溶けて川に流れます。
example_sentences.english: When spring comes, the snow on the mountains melts and flows into the river.
example_sentences.furigana: 春[はる]になったら、山[やま]の雪[ゆき]が溶[と]けて川[かわ]に流[なが]れます。

example_sentences.japanese: 冷たいお茶に砂糖を入れたら、全然溶けませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I put sugar in cold tea, and it didn't dissolve at all.
example_sentences.furigana: 冷[つめ]たいお茶[ちゃ]に砂[さ]糖[とう]を入[い]れたら、全[ぜん]然[ぜん]溶[と]けませんでした。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 腐（くさ）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: Flesh (肉) crumbling under a roof: kusaru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Shove a tub of rice to the back of the fridge and forget it for three weeks. The smell hits before you see the domed, slimy lid, and food left to turn that far is what <vocabulary form="腐る">to rot / spoil</vocabulary> means.
items.reading_mnemonic: Three weeks on, you pry the slimy domed lid off the forgotten rice tub and find it grey and lumpy as old <reading>couscous</reading>. You gag <reading>くさる</reading>: the rice has begun to <vocabulary form="腐る">rot</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行の間に、台所の果物が全部腐ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: While we were away on the trip, all the fruit in the kitchen went bad.
example_sentences.furigana: 旅[りょ]行[こう]の間[あいだ]に、台[だい]所[どころ]の果物[くだもの]が全[ぜん]部[ぶ]腐[くさ]ってしまった。

example_sentences.japanese: この卵は腐っているかもしれないから、食べないでください。
example_sentences.english: This egg might be rotten, so please don't eat it.
example_sentences.furigana: この卵[たまご]は腐[くさ]っているかもしれないから、食[た]べないでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 古い橋は木が腐っているので、渡らないでください。
example_sentences.english: The wood on the old bridge has rotted, so please don't cross it.
example_sentences.furigana: 古[ふる]い橋[はし]は木[き]が腐[くさ]っているので、渡[わた]らないでください。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 逃（に）＋げる.
items.mnemonic_text: Slipping off the road: nigeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The side door is propped open a crack, and by the time the guard turns back the cell is empty. Getting clear through a gap before anyone can stop you is what it means <vocabulary form="逃げる">to escape / run away</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Nigel</reading> the gerbil works a bar of his cage loose every night and is halfway down the hall before the lights come on. A small thing bolting for the gap the moment it opens is 「<reading>にげる</reading>」, <vocabulary form="逃げる">to escape / run away</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: ドアを開けたら、犬が外へ逃げてしまった。
example_sentences.english: When I opened the door, the dog ran off outside.
example_sentences.furigana: ドアを開[あ]けたら、犬[いぬ]が外[そと]へ逃[に]げてしまった。

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が強かったので、みんな駅の中に逃げました。
example_sentences.english: The rain was so heavy that everyone fled into the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]が強[つよ]かったので、みんな駅[えき]の中[なか]に逃[に]げました。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟はいつも宿題から逃げて、テレビを見ています。
example_sentences.english: My little brother always runs away from his homework and watches TV.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]はいつも宿[しゅく]題[だい]から逃[に]げて、テレビを見[み]ています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 追（お）＋いかける.
items.mnemonic_text: Following closely on the road: oikakeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A bun rolls off the bakery shelf and a boy runs after it down three aisles, hands out, never quite closing the gap. Staying right behind a thing that will not stop, trying to catch it, is what it means <vocabulary form="追いかける">to chase</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The baker bellows <reading>oi, cack-a-roo</reading> at the boy hopping down three aisles after the runaway bun, never quite closing the gap: <reading>おいかける</reading>, to <vocabulary form="追いかける">chase</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 庭で、うちの猫が鳥を追いかけていました。
example_sentences.english: Our cat was chasing a bird in the yard.
example_sentences.furigana: 庭[にわ]で、うちの猫[ねこ]が鳥[とり]を追[お]いかけていました。

example_sentences.japanese: 風で飛んだ帽子を、走って追いかけました。
example_sentences.english: I ran after my hat when the wind blew it away.
example_sentences.furigana: 風[かぜ]で飛[と]んだ帽[ぼう]子[し]を、走[はし]って追[お]いかけました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は今も自分の夢を追いかけています。
example_sentences.english: He is still chasing his dream.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は今[いま]も自[じ]分[ぶん]の夢[ゆめ]を追[お]いかけています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 断（ことわ）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: Cutting off a request: kotowaru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The host holds out the good sweets and you put a flat hand over your cup and say no until she takes the plate back. Turning down what someone offers, out loud and on purpose, is what it means <vocabulary form="断る">to refuse / decline</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Even when the host offers sweets as soft as <reading>cotton wool</reading>, your flat hand stays over the cup until she takes the plate back: <reading>ことわる</reading>, to <vocabulary form="断る">refuse</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事が忙しいので、週末の旅行を断りました。
example_sentences.english: I'm busy with work, so I turned down the weekend trip.
example_sentences.furigana: 仕[し]事[ごと]が忙[いそが]しいので、週[しゅう]末[まつ]の旅[りょ]行[こう]を断[ことわ]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父にお金を貸してくださいと言われたが、断った。
example_sentences.english: My uncle asked me to lend him money, but I said no.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔父[おじ]にお金[かね]を貸[か]してくださいと言[い]われたが、断[ことわ]った。

example_sentences.japanese: レストランでお酒を出されましたが、運転するので断りました。
example_sentences.english: They offered me a drink at the restaurant, but I declined because I was driving.
example_sentences.furigana: レストランでお酒[さけ]を出[だ]されましたが、運[うん]転[てん]するので断[ことわ]りました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 頼（たの）＋む.
items.mnemonic_text: Trusting your weight to a bundle: tanomu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You catch your neighbour at the gate, hold out your spare key, and ask her to feed the cat while you are gone. Putting a task in someone else's hands and counting on them to do it is what it means <vocabulary form="頼む">to request / rely on</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the gate you press your spare key into the neighbour's palm with a quick <reading>ta</reading>, and the cat she will feed gives <reading>no mew</reading> of protest: <reading>たのむ</reading>, to <vocabulary form="頼む">rely on</vocabulary> her.

example_sentences.japanese: 母に駅まで迎えに来てくれるように頼みました。
example_sentences.english: I asked my mother to come pick me up at the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]に駅[えき]まで迎[むか]えに来[き]てくれるように頼[たの]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 喫茶店で、コーヒーを二つ頼みました。
example_sentences.english: I ordered two coffees at the café.
example_sentences.furigana: 喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]で、コーヒーを二[ふた]つ頼[たの]みました。

example_sentences.japanese: 引っ越すとき、友達に荷物を運ぶのを頼みました。
example_sentences.english: When I moved, I asked my friends to help carry my things.
example_sentences.furigana: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]すとき、友[とも]達[だち]に荷[に]物[もつ]を運[はこ]ぶのを頼[たの]みました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 助（たす）＋かる.
items.mnemonic_text: Getting rescued on your own: tasukaru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="助">help</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="助かる">to be saved / helped</vocabulary> word are the same. This ending flips it around so the help lands on you, and you are the one pulled clear, not the one doing the pulling.
items.reading_mnemonic: Stuck in the mud, you get one more pair of hands when a walrus hooks its <reading>tusks</reading> under your arms and heaves with all its power: <reading>たすかる</reading>, to be <vocabulary form="助かる">saved</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 手伝ってくれたら、助かります。
example_sentences.english: If you help me, I'd really appreciate it.
example_sentences.furigana: 手伝[てつだ]ってくれたら、助[たす]かります。

example_sentences.japanese: 道を教えてくれて、助かりました。
example_sentences.english: You showed me the way, and it really helped.
example_sentences.furigana: 道[みち]を教[おし]えてくれて、助[たす]かりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 傘があったので、助かりました。
example_sentences.english: I had an umbrella with me, so it really saved me.
example_sentences.furigana: 傘[かさ]があったので、助[たす]かりました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 助（たす）＋ける.
items.mnemonic_text: Lending strength (力) to someone: tasukeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="助">help</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="助ける">to help / rescue</vocabulary> word are the same. This ending points it outward, so you are the one reaching in and pulling someone else clear.
items.reading_mnemonic: You met this sound as たす in 助かる, so the outward version, <vocabulary form="助ける">to help / rescue</vocabulary>, is simply <reading>たすける</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫が川に落ちて、私が助けました。
example_sentences.english: The cat fell into the river, and I saved it.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]が川[かわ]に落[お]ちて、私[わたし]が助[たす]けました。

example_sentences.japanese: この犬を助けてください。
example_sentences.english: Please help this dog.
example_sentences.furigana: この犬[いぬ]を助[たす]けてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちなら彼を助けられます。
example_sentences.english: If it's us, we can help him.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]たちなら彼[かれ]を助[たす]けられます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 叱（しか）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: A mouth (口) baring teeth (七): to scold.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A kid tips a full tray of paint across the floor, and the teacher kneels down and tells him in a hard, flat voice that this was not okay. Speaking to someone that sharply about what they did wrong is what it means <vocabulary form="叱る">to scold</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Each wrong answer earns one more tap of <reading>chalk</reading> on the desk while the teacher lists your mistakes in a rising voice. That steady, sharp correction for a fault is 「<reading>しかる</reading>」, <vocabulary form="叱る">to scold</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は僕を叱りました。
example_sentences.english: My mother scolded me.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は僕[ぼく]を叱[しか]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が生徒を叱っています。
example_sentences.english: The teacher is scolding the student.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]が生[せい]徒[と]を叱[しか]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟が皿を壊したので、父は弟を叱りました。
example_sentences.english: Since my little brother broke a plate, my father scolded him.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]が皿[さら]を壊[こわ]したので、父[ちち]は弟[おとうと]を叱[しか]りました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 褒（ほ）＋める.
items.mnemonic_text: Clothing (衤) draped in honor: homeru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your kid brings home a drawing, and you pin it on the fridge, point to the careful shading, and tell her it is genuinely good. Saying plainly to someone that what they made is good is how you <vocabulary form="褒める">praise</vocabulary> them.
items.reading_mnemonic: You pin your daughter's drawing on the fridge, point at the careful shading and cheer as if she hit a <reading>home run</reading>: <reading>ほめる</reading>, which is how you <vocabulary form="褒める">praise</vocabulary> her.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は私を褒めました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher praised me.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は私[わたし]を褒[ほ]めました。

example_sentences.japanese: 母はいつも私を褒めたり叱ったりします。
example_sentences.english: My mother is always either praising or scolding me.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]はいつも私[わたし]を褒[ほ]めたり叱[しか]ったりします。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は私の絵を褒めました。
example_sentences.english: He praised my picture.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は私[わたし]の絵[え]を褒[ほ]めました。

items.word_type: godan verb, transitive verb, intransitive verb
items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 謝（あやま）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: Words (言) offered like thanks: ayamaru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You back your bike into a parked car, wince at the fresh scratch, and go knock on the owner's door to say sorry and offer to pay. Owning that you did wrong and saying so to the person is what it means <vocabulary form="謝る">to apologize</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You knock on the door to confess the scratch your bike left on the parked car, and <reading>a llama</reading> answers, so you bow, offer to pay and <vocabulary form="謝る">apologize</vocabulary> anyway: <reading>あやまる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は友達に謝りました。
example_sentences.english: I apologized to my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は友[とも]達[だち]に謝[あやま]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: あなたは彼に謝ったほうがいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: You'd better apologize to him.
example_sentences.furigana: あなたは彼[かれ]に謝[あやま]ったほうがいいですよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は先生に謝っています。
example_sentences.english: He is apologizing to his teacher.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は先[せん]生[せい]に謝[あやま]っています。

items.word_type: godan verb, transitive verb, intransitive verb
items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 喜（よろこ）＋ぶ.
items.mnemonic_text: A mouth (口) opening wide in joy: yorokobu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Hand someone the news they have been hoping for and watch them <kanji form="喜">rejoice</kanji>, all grin and thank-yous and a little bounce. That whole warm rush when something goes right for you is being <vocabulary form="喜ぶ">pleased</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Hand your friend the news she has waited for and she bounces so hard she slops <reading>your cocoa</reading> everywhere, all grin and thank-yous: <reading>よろこぶ</reading>, to be <vocabulary form="喜ぶ">pleased</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は花をもらって喜びました。
example_sentences.english: My mother was delighted to receive the flowers.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は花[はな]をもらって喜[よろこ]びました。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供はお菓子を食べて喜びました。
example_sentences.english: The child was happy eating the sweets.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]はお菓[か]子[し]を食[た]べて喜[よろこ]びました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は先生の話を聞いて喜んでいるようだ。
example_sentences.english: He seems pleased to hear the teacher's story.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は先[せん]生[せい]の話[はなし]を聞[き]いて喜[よろこ]んでいるようだ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 怒（おこ）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: A heart (心) enslaved (奴) by rage: okoru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone slides into the parking spot you waited ten minutes for and smirks at you through the glass. Your face goes hot, your voice climbs, and that sudden flare of temper is what it means <vocabulary form="怒る">to get angry</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The driver who slid into your parking spot smirks at you over a tub of <reading>okra</reading>, and your face goes hot as your voice climbs: <reading>おこる</reading>, to <vocabulary form="怒る">get angry</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟はよく怒る。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother gets angry a lot.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]はよく怒[おこ]る。

example_sentences.japanese: 私が遅れたので、先生が怒りました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher got angry because I was late.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]が遅[おく]れたので、先[せん]生[せい]が怒[おこ]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はなぜ怒っているのですか。
example_sentences.english: Why is she angry?
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]はなぜ怒[おこ]っているのですか。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 悩（なや）＋む.
items.mnemonic_text: A heart (忄) tangled in brains (脳): nayamu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You have two job offers and one week to pick, and every night you lie awake running the same lists. Turning a hard choice over and over until it wears a groove in you is <vocabulary form="悩む">to worry / agonize</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Lying awake over the two job offers, you <reading>gnaw a yam</reading> at midnight and run the same lists again until they wear a groove: <reading>なやむ</reading>, to <vocabulary form="悩む">agonize</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: どれを買うか悩んでいます。
example_sentences.english: I can't decide which one to buy.
example_sentences.furigana: どれを買[か]うか悩[なや]んでいます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は仕事のことでいつも悩んでいる。
example_sentences.english: She's always worried about work.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は仕[し]事[ごと]のことでいつも悩[なや]んでいる。

example_sentences.japanese: 悩んでも答えが見つからなかった。
example_sentences.english: Even after agonizing over it, I couldn't find an answer.
example_sentences.furigana: 悩[なや]んでも答[こた]えが見[み]つからなかった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 驚（おどろ）＋く.
items.mnemonic_text: A horse (馬) rearing up: odoroku.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You lift a plant pot to move it and the whole underside is crawling with woodlice spilling out at once. The jump in your chest and the step back you take before you can think is being <vocabulary form="驚く">surprised</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You tip up what looks like an <reading>odd rock</reading> by the step and it opens into a crab and runs across your foot. You are standing before you have decided to move, and that jolt at a thing you did not expect is 「<reading>おどろく</reading>」, <vocabulary form="驚く">to be surprised</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬の声に驚きました。
example_sentences.english: I was startled by the dog's bark.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]の声[こえ]に驚[おどろ]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 値段が安すぎて驚きました。
example_sentences.english: The price was so cheap it surprised me.
example_sentences.furigana: 値[ね]段[だん]が安[やす]すぎて驚[おどろ]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は驚いた顔をしました。
example_sentences.english: She had a surprised look on her face.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は驚[おどろ]いた顔[かお]をしました。

items.word_type: godan verb, transitive verb, intransitive verb
items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 嘆（なげ）＋く.
items.mnemonic_text: A mouth (口) sighing hard: nageku.
items.meaning_mnemonic: After the storm the old farmer stands in the flattened field and says the same low words about the lost year, over and over, to no one. Letting that grief out loud like that is what it means <vocabulary form="嘆く">to lament</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: On a fence post in the flattened field sits <reading>a gecko</reading>, and the old farmer pours his low words about the lost year out to it, over and over: <reading>なげく</reading>, to <vocabulary form="嘆く">lament</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は財布をなくして、嘆いた。
example_sentences.english: He lost his wallet and lamented it.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は財[さい]布[ふ]をなくして、嘆[なげ]いた。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は時計を壊して、嘆いている。
example_sentences.english: She broke her watch and is lamenting it.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は時計[とけい]を壊[こわ]して、嘆[なげ]いている。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は病気になって、嘆いた。
example_sentences.english: My mother fell ill and lamented it.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は病[びょう]気[き]になって、嘆[なげ]いた。

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 頑（がん）on'yomi ＋ 張（ば）kun'yomi ＋ る.
items.mnemonic_text: Stubbornly (頑) stretching (張) onward: ganbaru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: To be <kanji form="頑">stubborn</kanji> about how far you can <kanji form="張">stretch</kanji> yourself, and then hold that stretch when it burns, is to <vocabulary form="頑張る">try hard</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 来週は試験があるので、毎晩頑張っています。
example_sentences.english: I have an exam next week, so I'm working hard every night.
example_sentences.furigana: 来[らい]週[しゅう]は試[し]験[けん]があるので、毎[まい]晩[ばん]頑張[がんば]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字は難しくても、毎日頑張って覚えます。
example_sentences.english: Even if kanji are hard, I work at memorizing them every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 漢[かん]字[じ]は難[むずか]しくても、毎[まい]日[にち]頑張[がんば]って覚[おぼ]えます。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の会議、頑張ってくださいね。
example_sentences.english: Good luck at tomorrow's meeting.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]の会[かい]議[ぎ]、頑張[がんば]ってくださいね。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 慣（な）＋れる.
items.mnemonic_text: A heart (忄) settling into a pattern: nareru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Do the same small thing every day and the odd feeling fades on its own. Once it is completely gone, you have <vocabulary form="慣れる">gotten used to</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: A new <reading>nurse</reading> does the same small thing every day, one blood draw after another, until the odd feeling fades and she has <vocabulary form="慣れる">gotten used to</vocabulary> it: <reading>なれる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい仕事にだんだん慣れてきました。
example_sentences.english: I'm gradually getting used to my new job.
example_sentences.furigana: 新[あたら]しい仕[し]事[ごと]にだんだん慣[な]れてきました。

example_sentences.japanese: 箸にまだ慣れていないので、スプーンを使ってもいいですか。
example_sentences.english: I'm still not used to chopsticks, so is it okay if I use a spoon?
example_sentences.furigana: 箸[はし]にまだ慣[な]れていないので、スプーンを使[つか]ってもいいですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝六時に起きるのに、もう慣れました。
example_sentences.english: I've already gotten used to getting up at six every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]六[ろく]時[じ]に起[お]きるのに、もう慣[な]れました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 経（た）＋つ.
items.mnemonic_text: Time threading through the loom: tatsu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="経">pass through</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="経つ">for time to pass</vocabulary> word are the same; the extra kana on the end just makes it something time does by itself.
items.reading_mnemonic: The old monk <reading>tuts</reading> softly each time his thumb pushes the thread past another prayer bead, all one hundred and eight, as the hours <vocabulary form="経つ">pass</vocabulary>: <reading>たつ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に来てから、もう三年経ちました。
example_sentences.english: It's already been three years since I came to Japan.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]に来[き]てから、もう三[さん]年[ねん]経[た]ちました。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達と話していたら、二時間経っていました。
example_sentences.english: I was talking with a friend, and before I knew it two hours had gone by.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]と話[はな]していたら、二[に]時[じ]間[かん]経[た]っていました。

example_sentences.japanese: 薬を飲んで三十分経っても、頭がまだ痛いです。
example_sentences.english: Even thirty minutes after taking the medicine, my head still hurts.
example_sentences.furigana: 薬[くすり]を飲[の]んで三[さん]十[じゅう]分[ふん]経[た]っても、頭[あたま]がまだ痛[いた]いです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 過（す）＋ぎる.
items.mnemonic_text: A road (辶) going past a fold: sugiru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Anything that slides past the mark it was meant to stop at, and keeps sliding, has <vocabulary form="過ぎる">passed or exceeded</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Flicked down the counter, a <reading>sugar</reading> cube slides past the cup it was meant to stop at and keeps sliding off the edge. It has <vocabulary form="過ぎる">passed</vocabulary> its mark: <reading>すぎる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: バスで寝ていたら、降りる駅を過ぎてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I fell asleep on the bus and went right past my stop.
example_sentences.furigana: バスで寝[ね]ていたら、降[お]りる駅[えき]を過[す]ぎてしまいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に来てから、もう三年が過ぎました。
example_sentences.english: Three years have already passed since I came to Japan.
example_sentences.furigana: 日本[にほん]に来[き]てから、もう三[さん]年[ねん]が過[す]ぎました。

example_sentences.japanese: もう夜の十時を過ぎたから、早く寝てください。
example_sentences.english: It's already past ten at night, so please go to bed soon.
example_sentences.furigana: もう夜[よる]の十[じゅう]時[じ]を過[す]ぎたから、早[はや]く寝[ね]てください。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 過（す）＋ごす.
items.mnemonic_text: Letting time pass by choice: sugosu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: To let a whole afternoon <kanji form="過">go beyond</kanji> you on purpose, filling every hour of it, is to <vocabulary form="過ごす">spend</vocabulary> that time.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already met 過ぎる, so its near-twin <vocabulary form="過ごす">to spend time</vocabulary> is simply <reading>すごす</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は家族と海の近くで過ごしました。
example_sentences.english: I spent the weekend with my family near the sea.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]は家[か]族[ぞく]と海[うみ]の近[ちか]くで過[す]ごしました。

example_sentences.japanese: 冬は祖母の家で過ごしたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to spend the winter at my grandmother's house.
example_sentences.furigana: 冬[ふゆ]は祖[そ]母[ぼ]の家[いえ]で過[す]ごしたいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の日は、部屋で本を読んで過ごしています。
example_sentences.english: On rainy days, I spend my time in my room reading books.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]は、部屋[へや]で本[ほん]を読[よ]んで過[す]ごしています。

items.word_type: する verb, transitive verb, intransitive verb
items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 期（き）＋待（たい）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A period (期) awaited (待): to expect.
items.meaning_mnemonic: To <kanji form="待">wait</kanji> out a fixed <kanji form="期">period</kanji>, sure the thing is coming, is to <vocabulary form="期待する">expect</vocabulary> it.

example_sentences.japanese: 父が私に期待するのは、試験の結果です。
example_sentences.english: What my father expects from me is exam results.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]が私[わたし]に期[き]待[たい]するのは、試[し]験[けん]の結[けっ]果[か]です。

example_sentences.japanese: みんなが期待する旅行だったのに、毎日雨でした。
example_sentences.english: Everyone was looking forward to the trip, but it rained every day.
example_sentences.furigana: みんなが期[き]待[たい]する旅[りょ]行[こう]だったのに、毎[まい]日[にち]雨[あめ]でした。

example_sentences.japanese: あまり期待すると、残念に思いますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you expect too much, you'll end up disappointed.
example_sentences.furigana: あまり期[き]待[たい]すると、残[ざん]念[ねん]に思[おも]いますよ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 願（ねが）＋う.
items.mnemonic_text: A head bowed asking a favor: negau.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Press your palms together and name aloud the one thing you want another person to grant you. That spoken hope is to <vocabulary form="願う">wish</vocabulary> or request something.
items.reading_mnemonic: The polite お願いします already gave you this reading, so plain <vocabulary form="願う">to wish or request</vocabulary> is <reading>ねがう</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は私たちの旅行の安全を願って、駅まで送ってくれました。
example_sentences.english: Wishing us a safe trip, my dad saw us off at the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は私[わたし]たちの旅[りょ]行[こう]の安[あん]全[ぜん]を願[ねが]って、駅[えき]まで送[おく]ってくれました。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は毎朝、子供の病気が早く治るように願っています。
example_sentences.english: Every morning, my mother prays that her child gets better soon.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]、子[こ]供[ども]の病[びょう]気[き]が早[はや]く治[なお]るように願[ねが]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は天気がいいことを願うよ。
example_sentences.english: I hope the weather is nice tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は天[てん]気[き]がいいことを願[ねが]うよ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 祈（いの）＋る.
items.mnemonic_text: An altar (示) plus an axe-shaped vow: inoru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Bow your head, close your eyes, and quietly ask a power you cannot see to keep someone safe. That asking, with nothing but words, is to <vocabulary form="祈る">pray</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At dawn a line of pilgrims kneels in one long <reading>row</reading> on the shrine steps, foreheads to the stone, each asking an unseen power for rain. Kneeling in a <reading>row</reading> and begging like that is to <vocabulary form="祈る">pray</vocabulary>, which is <reading>いのる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は毎晩、寝る前に静かに祈ります。
example_sentences.english: Every night before bed, my grandmother prays quietly.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]は毎[まい]晩[ばん]、寝[ね]る前[まえ]に静[しず]かに祈[いの]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟の試験の前に、家族みんなで祈りました。
example_sentences.english: Before my little brother's exam, the whole family prayed together.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]の試[し]験[けん]の前[まえ]に、家[か]族[ぞく]みんなで祈[いの]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は雨が降らないように祈っています。
example_sentences.english: I'm praying it doesn't rain this weekend.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]は雨[あめ]が降[ふ]らないように祈[いの]っています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 祝（いわ）＋う.
items.mnemonic_text: An altar (示) blessing an event: iwau.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Good news lands, so you deliberately gather people, food and noise around the one it happened to. That staged happiness is to <vocabulary form="祝う">celebrate</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The team wins and Sei's whole class erupts, caps in the air, everyone shouting 'I <reading>wow</reading>' around a cake nobody planned. Making that much noise on purpose for one person is to <vocabulary form="祝う">celebrate</vocabulary>, which is <reading>いわう</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が結婚したので、みんなで祝いました。
example_sentences.english: My friend got married, so we all celebrated.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]が結[けっ]婚[こん]したので、みんなで祝[いわ]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 試験が終わったら、レストランで祝いましょう。
example_sentences.english: Once the exam is over, let's celebrate at a restaurant.
example_sentences.furigana: 試[し]験[けん]が終[お]わったら、レストランで祝[いわ]いましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんが生まれた日、祖父はお酒で祝いました。
example_sentences.english: On the day the baby was born, my grandfather celebrated with sake.
example_sentences.furigana: 赤[あか]ちゃんが生[う]まれた日[ひ]、祖[そ]父[ふ]はお酒[さけ]で祝[いわ]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 祝（しゅく）＋福（ふく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A celebration (祝) of fortune (福): a blessing.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Words that <kanji form="祝">celebrate</kanji> someone while wishing them good fortune are a <vocabulary form="祝福">blessing</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんが生まれて、たくさんの人から祝福の手紙が届きました。
example_sentences.english: When the baby was born, letters of blessing arrived from lots of people.
example_sentences.furigana: 赤[あか]ちゃんが生[う]まれて、たくさんの人[ひと]から祝[しゅく]福[ふく]の手[て]紙[がみ]が届[とど]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は親の祝福がなくても、彼と結婚するそうです。
example_sentences.english: I heard she's going to marry him even without her parents' blessing.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は親[おや]の祝[しゅく]福[ふく]がなくても、彼[かれ]と結[けっ]婚[こん]するそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: みんなに祝福されて、姉はとても嬉しそうでした。
example_sentences.english: With everyone's blessing, my older sister looked really happy.
example_sentences.furigana: みんなに祝[しゅく]福[ふく]されて、姉[あね]はとても嬉[うれ]しそうでした。

items.word_type: する verb, transitive verb, intransitive verb
items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 感（かん）＋謝（しゃ）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Feeling (感) thanks (謝): to appreciate.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="感">feeling</kanji> that wells up and makes you want to <kanji form="謝">thank</kanji> someone to their face is being <vocabulary form="感謝する">grateful</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 手伝ってくれた友達に、感謝する気持ちを伝えました。
example_sentences.english: I told my friend how grateful I was for the help.
example_sentences.furigana: 手伝[てつだ]ってくれた友[とも]達[だち]に、感[かん]謝[しゃ]する気[き]持[も]ちを伝[つた]えました。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は、困ったときに助けてくれた人に感謝することを忘れない。
example_sentences.english: My father never forgets to thank the people who helped him when he was in trouble.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は、困[こま]ったときに助[たす]けてくれた人[ひと]に感[かん]謝[しゃ]することを忘[わす]れない。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はお客さんに感謝する日なので、コーヒーが安いです。
example_sentences.english: Today is customer appreciation day, so coffee is cheap.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]はお客[きゃく]さんに感[かん]謝[しゃ]する日[ひ]なので、コーヒーが安[やす]いです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 間（ま）＋違（ちが）＋える.
