items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone puts a <kanji form="手">hand</kanji> to your job and lets their own plans <kanji form="伝">go along</kanji> with your work instead. Doing that for you is to <vocabulary form="手伝ってくれる">help (me)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 引っ越すとき、仲間がみんな手伝ってくれました。
example_sentences.english: When I moved, all my friends pitched in and helped.
example_sentences.furigana: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]すとき、仲[なか]間[ま]がみんな手伝[てつだ]ってくれました。

example_sentences.japanese: 重い荷物を持っていたら、若い男の人が手伝ってくれた。
example_sentences.english: I was carrying heavy bags, and a young man helped me.
example_sentences.furigana: 重[おも]い荷[に]物[もつ]を持[も]っていたら、若[わか]い男[おとこ]の人[ひと]が手伝[てつだ]ってくれた。

example_sentences.japanese: 会議の準備は、山田さんが手伝ってくれるそうです。
example_sentences.english: I hear Yamada-san is going to help me get ready for the meeting.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]議[ぎ]の準[じゅん]備[び]は、山田[やまだ]さんが手伝[てつだ]ってくれるそうです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 貸（か）＋してもらう.
items.mnemonic_text: Receiving the favor of a loan: kashite morau.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You ask, and the owner agrees to <kanji form="貸">lend</kanji> you the thing you need. Walking off with it on that promise is to <vocabulary form="貸してもらう">have (something) lent</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 貸 is 「か」 from 貸す, the verb to lend, so <vocabulary form="貸してもらう">to have (something) lent</vocabulary> is <reading>かしてもらう</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が降ってきたので、店で傘を貸してもらいました。
example_sentences.english: It started to rain, so the shop lent me an umbrella.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]ってきたので、店[みせ]で傘[かさ]を貸[か]してもらいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 財布を忘れたので、兄にお金を貸してもらった。
example_sentences.english: I forgot my wallet, so I got my older brother to lend me some money.
example_sentences.furigana: 財[さい]布[ふ]を忘[わす]れたので、兄[あに]にお金[かね]を貸[か]してもらった。

example_sentences.japanese: 旅館で自転車を貸してもらって、町を回りました。
example_sentences.english: The inn lent us bicycles, and we rode around town.
example_sentences.furigana: 旅[りょ]館[かん]で自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]を貸[か]してもらって、町[まち]を回[まわ]りました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 送（おく）＋ってあげる.
items.mnemonic_text: Sending something as a favor: okutte ageru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="送">send</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="送ってあげる">to send (for someone)</vocabulary> word are the same character, so they mean the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 送 is 「おく」 from 送る, the verb to send, so <vocabulary form="送ってあげる">to send (for someone)</vocabulary> is <reading>おくってあげる</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: もう遅いから、家まで送ってあげるよ。
example_sentences.english: It's late, so I'll take you home.
example_sentences.furigana: もう遅[おそ]いから、家[いえ]まで送[おく]ってあげるよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母に赤ちゃんの写真をたくさん送ってあげました。
example_sentences.english: I sent my aunt lots of photos of the baby.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔母[おば]に赤[あか]ちゃんの写[しゃ]真[しん]をたくさん送[おく]ってあげました。

example_sentences.japanese: 外国に住んでいる娘に、日本のお菓子を送ってあげたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to send some Japanese snacks to my daughter who lives abroad.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]に住[す]んでいる娘[むすめ]に、日本[にほん]のお菓[か]子[し]を送[おく]ってあげたい。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 虫（むし）.
items.mnemonic_text: A curling little bug: mushi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Tip up the old flowerpot by the back step and the packed soil under it comes alive with tiny legs and feelers that pour away from the daylight. Every scurrying speck down there is an <vocabulary form="虫">insect / bug</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Tip up the old flowerpot and the soil under it is wet and <reading>mushy</reading>, pouring tiny legs and feelers away from the light: each one a <vocabulary form="虫">bug</vocabulary>, a <reading>むし</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 窓を開けたら、部屋に虫が入ってきた。
example_sentences.english: When I opened the window, a bug flew into the room.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]を開[あ]けたら、部屋[へや]に虫[むし]が入[はい]ってきた。

example_sentences.japanese: 夏の夜は、電気の近くに虫が多いです。
example_sentences.english: On summer nights, there are lots of bugs around the lights.
example_sentences.furigana: 夏[なつ]の夜[よる]は、電[でん]気[き]の近[ちか]くに虫[むし]が多[おお]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 母が育てた野菜を、虫が全部食べてしまった。
example_sentences.english: The bugs ate every one of the vegetables my mother grew.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]が育[そだ]てた野[や]菜[さい]を、虫[むし]が全[ぜん]部[ぶ]食[た]べてしまった。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 蝶（ちょう）.
items.mnemonic_text: Insect (虫) with delicate wings: a butterfly.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A scrap of coloured paper lifts off the shrine path and flutters between the mossy steps, folding shut and opening again as it climbs the air. That drifting pair of painted wings is a <vocabulary form="蝶">butterfly</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 女の子が庭で黄色の蝶を追いかけています。
example_sentences.english: A little girl is chasing a yellow butterfly around the garden.
example_sentences.furigana: 女[おんな]の子[こ]が庭[にわ]で黄[き]色[いろ]の蝶[ちょう]を追[お]いかけています。

example_sentences.japanese: 春の山では、たくさんの蝶が見られます。
example_sentences.english: In the mountains in spring, you can see lots of butterflies.
example_sentences.furigana: 春[はる]の山[やま]では、たくさんの蝶[ちょう]が見[み]られます。

example_sentences.japanese: 蝶が猫の鼻の上に止まって、猫がびっくりした。
example_sentences.english: A butterfly landed on the cat's nose, and the cat jumped.
example_sentences.furigana: 蝶[ちょう]が猫[ねこ]の鼻[はな]の上[うえ]に止[と]まって、猫[ねこ]がびっくりした。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 猿（さる）.
items.mnemonic_text: A dog-like beast (犭) still (袁): a monkey.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A grey shape drops onto the trailhead vending machine, pops the flap with quick clever fingers and swings back up a pine with a stolen can. Only a <vocabulary form="猿">monkey</vocabulary> robs a machine like that.
items.reading_mnemonic: Up the pine above the trailhead vending machine, the <vocabulary form="猿">monkey</vocabulary> with the stolen can also waves <reading>a sarong</reading> grabbed from a hiker's pack, and she yells <reading>さる</reading> after it.

example_sentences.japanese: 猿が窓を開けて台所に入ってきた。
example_sentences.english: A monkey opened the window and came into the kitchen.
example_sentences.furigana: 猿[さる]が窓[まど]を開[あ]けて台[だい]所[どころ]に入[はい]ってきた。

example_sentences.japanese: 猿が木の上からこちらを見ています。
example_sentences.english: A monkey is watching us from up in the tree.
example_sentences.furigana: 猿[さる]が木[き]の上[うえ]からこちらを見[み]ています。

example_sentences.japanese: 帽子を猿に取られてしまった。
example_sentences.english: A monkey snatched my hat.
example_sentences.furigana: 帽[ぼう]子[し]を猿[さる]に取[と]られてしまった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 馬（うま）.
items.mnemonic_text: A galloping horse with a flowing mane: uma.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The animal that walks over to the paddock fence stands taller than you at the shoulder, long-faced, with a mane down its neck and a sweeping tail. That shape and size is a <vocabulary form="馬">horse</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A toddler at the paddock fence stares up at the long face and sweeping mane, taller than her dad, and gasps <reading>ooh, ma</reading>: a <vocabulary form="馬">horse</vocabulary>, or <reading>うま</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は若いとき、毎日馬に乗って学校に通っていたそうです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently my grandfather rode a horse to school every day when he was young.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は若[わか]いとき、毎[まい]日[にち]馬[うま]に乗[の]って学[がっ]校[こう]に通[かよ]っていたそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: あの馬は体が大きいのに、とても優しい。
example_sentences.english: That horse is huge, but it is really gentle.
example_sentences.furigana: あの馬[うま]は体[からだ]が大[おお]きいのに、とても優[やさ]しい。

example_sentences.japanese: 馬に野菜をあげてもいいですか。
example_sentences.english: Is it okay to give the horse some vegetables?
example_sentences.furigana: 馬[うま]に野[や]菜[さい]をあげてもいいですか。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 牛（うし）.
items.mnemonic_text: Horns over a body: a cow.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="牛">cow</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="牛">cow</vocabulary> word are exactly the same character, so they mean the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: Seen from the front, with one slanted horn and those two broad bars of shoulder and back, she makes the farmer sigh <reading>ooh, she</reading> is fine: a <vocabulary form="牛">cow</vocabulary>, <reading>うし</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 農家の牛が道の真ん中で寝ていて、車が止まった。
example_sentences.english: A farmer's cow was lying asleep in the middle of the road, so the cars stopped.
example_sentences.furigana: 農[のう]家[か]の牛[うし]が道[みち]の真[ま]ん中[なか]で寝[ね]ていて、車[くるま]が止[と]まった。

example_sentences.japanese: 牛は水をたくさん飲むそうです。
example_sentences.english: I hear cows drink a lot of water.
example_sentences.furigana: 牛[うし]は水[みず]をたくさん飲[の]むそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供のころ、牛が怖くて近くに行けなかった。
example_sentences.english: As a kid, I was so scared of cows that I couldn't go near them.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]のころ、牛[うし]が怖[こわ]くて近[ちか]くに行[い]けなかった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 豚（ぶた）.
items.mnemonic_text: Flesh (月) matched with a boar's (豕) body: a pig.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Behind Koichi's konbini the scraps bin lies tipped over, and a fat pink animal stands in the spill with its snout down, grunting as it eats. Nothing empties a bin like a <vocabulary form="豚">pig</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The farmer fattens the animal every night on a bucket of <reading>butter</reading> and kitchen scraps until it can barely walk. That round, greasy thing is a <vocabulary form="豚">pig</vocabulary>, and he calls it 「<reading>ぶた</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 豚はきれいな動物だと先生が言っていました。
example_sentences.english: Our teacher said that pigs are actually clean animals.
example_sentences.furigana: 豚[ぶた]はきれいな動[どう]物[ぶつ]だと先[せん]生[せい]が言[い]っていました。

example_sentences.japanese: 豚の鼻は丸くて、ちょっとかわいい。
example_sentences.english: A pig's nose is round and kind of cute.
example_sentences.furigana: 豚[ぶた]の鼻[はな]は丸[まる]くて、ちょっとかわいい。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父は家で豚を三匹育てています。
example_sentences.english: My uncle is raising three pigs at his house.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔父[おじ]は家[いえ]で豚[ぶた]を三[さん]匹[ひき]育[そだ]てています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 羊（ひつじ）.
items.mnemonic_text: A woolly head with curling horns: a sheep.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="羊">sheep</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="羊">sheep</vocabulary> word are the same character, so they point at the same animal.
items.reading_mnemonic: The shepherd yells <reading>hit, Suzy</reading> to hurry her, but the animal with two short horns just stands calmly on stiff legs and chews: a <vocabulary form="羊">sheep</vocabulary>, <reading>ひつじ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 羊の赤ちゃんが生まれたので、みんなで見に行った。
example_sentences.english: A lamb was born, so we all went to see it.
example_sentences.furigana: 羊[ひつじ]の赤[あか]ちゃんが生[う]まれたので、みんなで見[み]に行[い]った。

example_sentences.japanese: この羊は人が好きで、呼ぶとすぐ来ます。
example_sentences.english: This sheep loves people and comes right away when you call it.
example_sentences.furigana: この羊[ひつじ]は人[ひと]が好[す]きで、呼[よ]ぶとすぐ来[き]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 雪の中で、羊たちが静かに立っていた。
example_sentences.english: The sheep stood quietly in the snow.
example_sentences.furigana: 雪[ゆき]の中[なか]で、羊[ひつじ]たちが静[しず]かに立[た]っていた。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 狐（きつね）.
items.mnemonic_text: A dog-like beast (犭) melon-shaped (瓜) tail: a fox.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At dusk a low red-brown shape slips along the treeline by the school field, quick and quiet, a white-tipped tail held straight out behind. That build and that tail mean a <vocabulary form="狐">fox</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: By the school field at dusk, a girl watches the white-tipped tail slip along the treeline and whispers <reading>Kit, so neat</reading> to her brother: a <vocabulary form="狐">fox</vocabulary>, <reading>きつね</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜になると、狐が町に来ることがあります。
example_sentences.english: At night, foxes sometimes come into town.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]になると、狐[きつね]が町[まち]に来[く]ることがあります。

example_sentences.japanese: 森の中で狐を見たことがありますか。
example_sentences.english: Have you ever seen a fox in the forest?
example_sentences.furigana: 森[もり]の中[なか]で狐[きつね]を見[み]たことがありますか。

example_sentences.japanese: あの狐、また僕の靴を持って行った。
example_sentences.english: That fox made off with my shoe again.
example_sentences.furigana: あの狐[きつね]、また僕[ぼく]の靴[くつ]を持[も]って行[い]った。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 熊（くま）.
items.mnemonic_text: A powerful beast standing over fire-like paws: a bear.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The beekeeper finds three hives smashed flat, the honey frames licked clean and claw marks gouged deep in the wood. Only a <vocabulary form="熊">bear</vocabulary> robs hives like that.
items.reading_mnemonic: The beekeeper follows the claw marks to a hollow log where the thief lies curled in a furry <reading>comma</reading>, honey on its snout, and hisses <reading>くま</reading> at the <vocabulary form="熊">bear</vocabulary> that licked his frames clean.

example_sentences.japanese: 山で熊に会った場合は、走って逃げてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: If you run into a bear in the mountains, don't turn and run.
example_sentences.furigana: 山[やま]で熊[くま]に会[あ]った場[ば]合[あい]は、走[はし]って逃[に]げてはいけません。

example_sentences.japanese: 熊は冬の間、何も食べないで寝ている。
example_sentences.english: Bears sleep all winter without eating anything.
example_sentences.furigana: 熊[くま]は冬[ふゆ]の間[あいだ]、何[なに]も食[た]べないで寝[ね]ている。

example_sentences.japanese: 川で熊が魚を取っているのが見えた。
example_sentences.english: I could see a bear catching fish in the river.
example_sentences.furigana: 川[かわ]で熊[くま]が魚[さかな]を取[と]っているのが見[み]えた。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 象（ぞう）.
items.mnemonic_text: A long-trunked beast shape: an elephant.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Behind the zoo fence stands a grey animal the size of a truck, its legs like pillars and its nose long enough to pick a bun off the ground. That reaching nose alone means <vocabulary form="象">elephant</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 象の鼻は手のように使えるそうです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently an elephant can use its trunk like a hand.
example_sentences.furigana: 象[ぞう]の鼻[はな]は手[て]のように使[つか]えるそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 象はとても重いので、この橋を渡ることができません。
example_sentences.english: The elephant is far too heavy to cross this bridge.
example_sentences.furigana: 象[ぞう]はとても重[おも]いので、この橋[はし]を渡[わた]ることができません。

example_sentences.japanese: 象が水を飲むところを、息子と一緒に見ました。
example_sentences.english: My son and I watched an elephant drinking water.
example_sentences.furigana: 象[ぞう]が水[みず]を飲[の]むところを、息子[むすこ]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に見[み]ました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 蛇（へび）.
items.mnemonic_text: Insect (虫) shape twisting like an earth-snake (它): a snake.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The hose coiled on the riverbank path lifts one end, flicks a thin forked tongue, and pours itself smoothly off into the long grass. A rope that moves on its own is a <vocabulary form="蛇">snake</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A hiker nudges what looks like a <reading>heavy</reading> length of rope lying across the trail, and it coils back on itself and hisses. Rope that fights back is a <vocabulary form="蛇">snake</vocabulary>, 「<reading>へび</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 階段の下に蛇がいて、父がびっくりしていた。
example_sentences.english: There was a snake under the stairs, and my dad got a real shock.
example_sentences.furigana: 階[かい]段[だん]の下[した]に蛇[へび]がいて、父[ちち]がびっくりしていた。

example_sentences.japanese: 蛇は足がないのに、速く動くことができる。
example_sentences.english: Snakes have no legs, yet they can move fast.
example_sentences.furigana: 蛇[へび]は足[あし]がないのに、速[はや]く動[うご]くことができる。

example_sentences.japanese: 蛇を見るたびに、姉は大きい声を出す。
example_sentences.english: Every time she sees a snake, my big sister shrieks.
example_sentences.furigana: 蛇[へび]を見[み]るたびに、姉[あね]は大[おお]きい声[こえ]を出[だ]す。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — くも cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 蜘蛛.
items.mnemonic_text: Two insect (虫) characters weaving a web: a spider.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You step off the porch at dawn and walk face-first through a wide sticky net strung across the doorway. Sitting dead centre with its legs spread is the <vocabulary form="蜘蛛">spider</vocabulary> that spun it overnight.
items.reading_mnemonic: Mo walks the mountain trail into the same face-height web every dawn and yells <reading>come, Mo</reading> at nobody. The weaver that keeps rebuilding it is a <vocabulary form="蜘蛛">spider</vocabulary>, 「<reading>くも</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝起きたら、窓に黒い蜘蛛がいた。
example_sentences.english: When I got up this morning, there was a black spider on the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 朝[あさ]起[お]きたら、窓[まど]に黒[くろ]い蜘蛛[くも]がいた。

example_sentences.japanese: 蜘蛛は虫を食べるから、殺さないで。
example_sentences.english: Spiders eat bugs, so don't kill it.
example_sentences.furigana: 蜘蛛[くも]は虫[むし]を食[た]べるから、殺[ころ]さないで。

example_sentences.japanese: 蜘蛛が怖いので、夫に外へ出してもらった。
example_sentences.english: I'm scared of spiders, so I had my husband put it outside.
example_sentences.furigana: 蜘蛛[くも]が怖[こわ]いので、夫[おっと]に外[そと]へ出[だ]してもらった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 蚊（か）.
items.mnemonic_text: Insect (虫) that hums like the number ten crossed: a mosquito.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The high thin whine circles your ear in the dark, stops, and a second later a hot itch rises on your arm. The thing that bit you and left that whine is a <vocabulary form="蚊">mosquito</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Kaa</reading> the crow hears the thin whine circling your ear in the dark, puffs one spark at it and caws <reading>か</reading> as the <vocabulary form="蚊">mosquito</vocabulary> drops off your itching arm.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏の夜は窓を開けると、蚊が部屋に入ってきます。
example_sentences.english: On summer nights, the moment you open the window, mosquitoes come into the room.
example_sentences.furigana: 夏[なつ]の夜[よる]は窓[まど]を開[あ]けると、蚊[か]が部屋[へや]に入[はい]ってきます。

example_sentences.japanese: 足が痒いと思ったら、蚊が三匹もいた。
example_sentences.english: I thought my leg felt itchy, and there were three mosquitoes on it.
example_sentences.furigana: 足[あし]が痒[かゆ]いと思[おも]ったら、蚊[か]が三[さん]匹[ひき]もいた。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は蚊を殺すまで寝ないと言っています。
example_sentences.english: My little brother says he isn't going to sleep until he kills the mosquito.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は蚊[か]を殺[ころ]すまで寝[ね]ないと言[い]っています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 蝿（はえ）.
items.mnemonic_text: Insect (虫) buzzing around: a fly.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You set the bowl down for one minute and three of them already crowd the rim, rubbing their legs and testing the food. Nothing finds a meal faster than a <vocabulary form="蝿">fly (insect)</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You set the bowl down on a bale of <reading>hay</reading>, and three of them climb out of the stalks onto its rim, rubbing their legs and buzzing <reading>はえ</reading>: each one a <vocabulary form="蝿">fly</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 台所のテーブルに蝿が止まっている。
example_sentences.english: A fly has landed on the kitchen table.
example_sentences.furigana: 台[だい]所[どころ]のテーブルに蝿[はえ]が止[と]まっている。

example_sentences.japanese: 料理に蝿が入らないように、皿の上に紙を置いておきましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's put some paper over the plates so no flies get into the food.
example_sentences.furigana: 料[りょう]理[り]に蝿[はえ]が入[はい]らないように、皿[さら]の上[うえ]に紙[かみ]を置[お]いておきましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: ドアを開けてあげたのに、蝿は出ていかなかった。
example_sentences.english: I opened the door for it, but the fly still wouldn't leave.
example_sentences.furigana: ドアを開[あ]けてあげたのに、蝿[はえ]は出[で]ていかなかった。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 自（し）＋然（ぜん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: One's own (自) natural state (然): nature.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Anything that is the way it is by its own <kanji form="自">self</kanji>, just that <kanji form="然">sort of thing</kanji> with nobody shaping it, is <vocabulary form="自然">nature</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は自然の多い町に住みたいそうです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently my grandfather wants to live in a town with lots of nature.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は自[し]然[ぜん]の多[おお]い町[まち]に住[す]みたいそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は自然を見に、川へ出かけることにしました。
example_sentences.english: I decided to head out to the river this weekend to enjoy some nature.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]は自[し]然[ぜん]を見[み]に、川[かわ]へ出[で]かけることにしました。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供のうちに、自然の中でたくさん遊んだほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: Kids should play outdoors in nature as much as they can while they are young.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]のうちに、自[し]然[ぜん]の中[なか]でたくさん遊[あそ]んだほうがいい。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 太（たい）＋陽（よう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The great (太) yang (陽): the sun.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The sky's one genuinely <kanji form="太">fat</kanji> light is too bright to look straight at, and every shadow on the ground points away from it. That light is the <vocabulary form="太陽">sun (formal)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 太陽が海に沈むところを、夫婦で静かに見ていた。
example_sentences.english: The couple quietly watched the sun sinking into the sea.
example_sentences.furigana: 太[たい]陽[よう]が海[うみ]に沈[しず]むところを、夫[ふう]婦[ふ]で静[しず]かに見[み]ていた。

example_sentences.japanese: 太陽が出ている間に、シャツを乾かしておきましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's get the shirts dried while the sun is out.
example_sentences.furigana: 太[たい]陽[よう]が出[で]ている間[あいだ]に、シャツを乾[かわ]かしておきましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 太陽を見ると、目が痛くなりますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you look at the sun, your eyes will start to hurt.
example_sentences.furigana: 太[たい]陽[よう]を見[み]ると、目[め]が痛[いた]くなりますよ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 星（ほし）＋空（ぞら）. Rendaku: 空 そら → ぞら.
items.mnemonic_text: Stars (星) filling the sky (空): a starry sky.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Wait until a <kanji form="空">sky</kanji> that looked empty all day fills after dark with thousands of small points of light, and you are looking at a <vocabulary form="星空">starry sky</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 山の上に登ると、星空がとてもきれいでした。
example_sentences.english: When we climbed to the top of the mountain, the starry sky was beautiful.
example_sentences.furigana: 山[やま]の上[うえ]に登[のぼ]ると、星[ほし]空[ぞら]がとてもきれいでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は星空を見ながら寝てしまった。
example_sentences.english: My daughter fell asleep while gazing at the starry sky.
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]は星[ほし]空[ぞら]を見[み]ながら寝[ね]てしまった。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の夜は、雲がなければ星空が見えるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow night we should see a starry sky, as long as there are no clouds.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]の夜[よる]は、雲[くも]がなければ星[ほし]空[ぞら]が見[み]えるだろう。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 波（なみ）.
items.mnemonic_text: Water (氵) taking on skin-like (皮) ripples: a wave.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Out on the open sea the water never settles; it stacks itself into a moving ridge, throws that ridge at the land, then draws back to build the next. Each moving ridge is a <vocabulary form="波">wave</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Out on the open sea, <reading>Nami</reading> the lifeguard rides each moving ridge toward the land, and when it draws back she yells <reading>なみ</reading> for the next <vocabulary form="波">wave</vocabulary> to build.

example_sentences.japanese: 波が高い日は、海に入らないほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: On days when the waves are high, you had better stay out of the sea.
example_sentences.furigana: 波[なみ]が高[たか]い日[ひ]は、海[うみ]に入[はい]らないほうがいい。

example_sentences.japanese: 大きい波が来て、兄の靴を持っていってしまった。
example_sentences.english: A big wave came in and carried off my older brother's shoes.
example_sentences.furigana: 大[おお]きい波[なみ]が来[き]て、兄[あに]の靴[くつ]を持[も]っていってしまった。

example_sentences.japanese: 波の上に、古い箱が浮かんでいる。
example_sentences.english: An old box is floating on the waves.
example_sentences.furigana: 波[なみ]の上[うえ]に、古[ふる]い箱[はこ]が浮[う]かんでいる。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 森（もり）.
items.mnemonic_text: Three trees (木) together: a forest.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The single character <kanji>forest</kanji> is the entire word, nothing added and nothing dropped. What you met as a kanji and what you say out loud as <vocabulary>forest</vocabulary> are the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: Walk into the <vocabulary>forest</vocabulary> and a mole named <reading>Morrie</reading> shoves his head up between two roots. He insists <reading>もり</reading> is his family name, since he dug every tunnel under these trees.

example_sentences.japanese: この森には熊がいるらしいから、一人で入らないで。
example_sentences.english: There are supposed to be bears in this forest, so don't go in alone.
example_sentences.furigana: この森[もり]には熊[くま]がいるらしいから、一人[ひとり]で入[はい]らないで。

example_sentences.japanese: 森で道が分からなくなってしまった。
example_sentences.english: I lost my way in the forest.
example_sentences.furigana: 森[もり]で道[みち]が分[わ]からなくなってしまった。

example_sentences.japanese: 森の中は涼しくて、鳥の声がよく聞こえる。
example_sentences.english: It's cool inside the forest, and you can hear the birds clearly.
example_sentences.furigana: 森[もり]の中[なか]は涼[すず]しくて、鳥[とり]の声[こえ]がよく聞[き]こえる。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 林（はやし）.
items.mnemonic_text: Two trees (木) together: a small wood.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="林">grove</kanji> kanji you have already met and the <vocabulary form="林">woods / grove</vocabulary> word are the same character, so they carry the same meaning.
items.reading_mnemonic: Ranger <reading>Hayashi</reading> plants a second tree so close to the first that their branches tangle, then nods <reading>はやし</reading>: two trees that close already make a <vocabulary form="林">grove</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校の後ろに小さい林があります。
example_sentences.english: There is a small grove of trees behind the school.
example_sentences.furigana: 学[がっ]校[こう]の後[うし]ろに小[ちい]さい林[はやし]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬と散歩するときは、いつも林を通って帰ります。
example_sentences.english: When I walk the dog, I always go home through the woods.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]と散[さん]歩[ぽ]するときは、いつも林[はやし]を通[とお]って帰[かえ]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 秋になると、林の木が赤や黄色に変わります。
example_sentences.english: When autumn comes, the trees in the grove turn red and yellow.
example_sentences.furigana: 秋[あき]になると、林[はやし]の木[き]が赤[あか]や黄[き]色[いろ]に変[か]わります。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 池（いけ）.
items.mnemonic_text: Water (氵) pooling beside a snake-like (也) shape: a pond.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="池">pond</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary form="池">pond</vocabulary> word are the same character, so of course they mean exactly the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: Water that goes nowhere, curling back on itself like a snake's tail, turns green and <reading>icky</reading> by August, and the frogs croak <reading>いけ</reading> from that <vocabulary form="池">pond</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 公園の池で、子供が魚にパンをあげています。
example_sentences.english: At the pond in the park, a child is feeding bread to the fish.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]の池[いけ]で、子[こ]供[ども]が魚[さかな]にパンをあげています。

example_sentences.japanese: 寒い朝、池の水が凍っていた。
example_sentences.english: On a cold morning, the water in the pond had frozen.
example_sentences.furigana: 寒[さむ]い朝[あさ]、池[いけ]の水[みず]が凍[こお]っていた。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は池に携帯を落として、とても困っていた。
example_sentences.english: My dad dropped his phone in the pond and was completely stuck.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は池[いけ]に携[けい]帯[たい]を落[お]として、とても困[こま]っていた。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 岩（いわ）.
items.mnemonic_text: A mountain (山) of stone (石): a boulder.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A single stone in the field is too big to lift, too heavy to roll, and was sitting there before the farm was. A stone that large and that settled is a <vocabulary form="岩">rock / boulder</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The <reading>Iowa</reading> farmer plows around the same stone every spring, too big to lift and older than his farm, and kicks it with a grunt of <reading>いわ</reading>: his field's <vocabulary form="岩">boulder</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 丸い岩の上に座って、弁当を食べました。
example_sentences.english: I sat on a round boulder and ate my boxed lunch.
example_sentences.furigana: 丸[まる]い岩[いわ]の上[うえ]に座[すわ]って、弁[べん]当[とう]を食[た]べました。

example_sentences.japanese: この岩は重すぎて、三人でも動かすことができない。
example_sentences.english: This rock is so heavy that even three of us cannot move it.
example_sentences.furigana: この岩[いわ]は重[おも]すぎて、三[さん]人[にん]でも動[うご]かすことができない。

example_sentences.japanese: 山の道に岩が落ちてきて、バスが止まってしまった。
example_sentences.english: A boulder came down onto the mountain road, and the bus had to stop.
example_sentences.furigana: 山[やま]の道[みち]に岩[いわ]が落[お]ちてきて、バスが止[と]まってしまった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 砂（すな）.
items.mnemonic_text: Stone (石) broken into few (少) grains: sand.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <vocabulary form="砂">Sand</vocabulary> is what a cliff turns into after the sea grinds at it for a few thousand years. What is left is a pile of grains so small they run through your fingers and still will not brush off.
items.reading_mnemonic: A fisher drops a <reading>tuna</reading> at the foot of the cliff the sea is grinding down, and it comes up coated in grains that will not brush off. He sighs <reading>すな</reading> and rinses off the <vocabulary form="砂">sand</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が公園で砂の山を作っています。
example_sentences.english: A child is building a mountain of sand in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]が公[こう]園[えん]で砂[すな]の山[やま]を作[つく]っています。

example_sentences.japanese: 靴の中に砂が入って、歩くのが痛いです。
example_sentences.english: Sand got into my shoes, and it hurts to walk.
example_sentences.furigana: 靴[くつ]の中[なか]に砂[すな]が入[はい]って、歩[ある]くのが痛[いた]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 海の砂は白くて、とても熱かったです。
example_sentences.english: The sand at the beach was white and really hot.
example_sentences.furigana: 海[うみ]の砂[すな]は白[しろ]くて、とても熱[あつ]かったです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 泥（どろ）.
items.mnemonic_text: Water (氵) mixed with soil, given a moon-shape twist: mud.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Mix plain dirt with enough rain and you get <vocabulary form="泥">mud</vocabulary>, a brown paste thick enough to hold a footprint and sticky enough to pull a boot off the foot that made it.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Doro</reading> the farmhand steps into the rain-soaked field, and the brown paste sucks the boot right off his foot. He hops on one leg yelling <reading>どろ</reading> at the <vocabulary form="泥">mud</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が降った後で、犬の足が泥で黒くなりました。
example_sentences.english: After the rain, the dog's paws turned black with mud.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]った後[あと]で、犬[いぬ]の足[あし]が泥[どろ]で黒[くろ]くなりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟の服が泥で汚いから、すぐ洗います。
example_sentences.english: My little brother's clothes are filthy with mud, so I'll wash them right away.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]の服[ふく]が泥[どろ]で汚[きたな]いから、すぐ洗[あら]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 農家の人は毎日泥の中で働いています。
example_sentences.english: Farmers work in the mud every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 農[のう]家[か]の人[ひと]は毎[まい]日[にち]泥[どろ]の中[なか]で働[はたら]いています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 煙（けむり）.
items.mnemonic_text: Fire (火) rising through the west (西) sky: smoke.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When something burns, part of it leaves as a grey cloud that climbs, spreads flat under the ceiling, and stings your eyes. That rising grey cloud off a fire is <vocabulary form="煙">smoke</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The grey cloud off the burnt toast climbs, spreads flat under the ceiling and stings the cook's eyes, so he finds the stove only from <reading>memory</reading>, coughing <reading>けむり</reading> through the <vocabulary form="煙">smoke</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 台所から黒い煙が出ています。
example_sentences.english: Black smoke is coming out of the kitchen.
example_sentences.furigana: 台[だい]所[どころ]から黒[くろ]い煙[けむり]が出[で]ています。

example_sentences.japanese: 窓を開けて、煙を外に出しましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's open the window and let the smoke out.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]を開[あ]けて、煙[けむり]を外[そと]に出[だ]しましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の近くで白い煙が上がっています。
example_sentences.english: White smoke is rising near the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の近[ちか]くで白[しろ]い煙[けむり]が上[あ]がっています。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 炎（ほのお）.
items.mnemonic_text: Two fires (火火) stacked: a flame.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Strike a match and a small pointed shape of light stands up on the tip, orange at the edges and bluish at the base. That upright, leaning tongue of burning light is a <vocabulary form="炎">flame</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A knight strikes a match and swears on his <reading>honor</reading> to keep the small orange point on its tip alive, whispering <reading>ほのお</reading> as he cups his hands around the <vocabulary form="炎">flame</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 炎が急に大きくなって、みんなびっくりしました。
example_sentences.english: The flames suddenly grew big, and everyone jumped.
example_sentences.furigana: 炎[ほのお]が急[きゅう]に大[おお]きくなって、みんなびっくりしました。

example_sentences.japanese: 暗い部屋で、炎だけが明るく光っていました。
example_sentences.english: In the dark room, only the flame was shining brightly.
example_sentences.furigana: 暗[くら]い部屋[へや]で、炎[ほのお]だけが明[あか]るく光[ひか]っていました。

example_sentences.japanese: 青い炎は赤い炎より熱いそうです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently a blue flame is hotter than a red one.
example_sentences.furigana: 青[あお]い炎[ほのお]は赤[あか]い炎[ほのお]より熱[あつ]いそうです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 氷（こおり）.
items.mnemonic_text: Water (水) with a frozen edge: ice.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Water held cold enough for long enough stops behaving like a liquid and turns hard, clear and slippery. Water in that solid state is <vocabulary form="氷">ice</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The lake held cold all winter has turned hard, clear and slippery, so the crew saws it out in blocks like a <reading>quarry</reading>, shouting <reading>こおり</reading> over each slab of <vocabulary form="氷">ice</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 冷たいお茶に氷を三つ入れました。
example_sentences.english: I put three ice cubes in the cold tea.
example_sentences.furigana: 冷[つめ]たいお茶[ちゃ]に氷[こおり]を三[みっ]つ入[い]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: 冬になると、池の上に氷ができます。
example_sentences.english: When winter comes, ice forms on the pond.
example_sentences.furigana: 冬[ふゆ]になると、池[いけ]の上[うえ]に氷[こおり]ができます。

example_sentences.japanese: 暑い日だったので、氷がもう溶けてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: It was a hot day, so the ice has already melted.
example_sentences.furigana: 暑[あつ]い日[ひ]だったので、氷[こおり]がもう溶[と]けてしまいました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 嵐（あらし）.
items.mnemonic_text: A mountain (山) wind (風): a storm.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Sometimes the wind, the rain, the black cloud and the noise all arrive together and stay for a whole day. A whole sky misbehaving at once is a <vocabulary form="嵐">storm</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Wind, rain, black cloud and thunder all arrive in <reading>a rush</reading>, and the dock hand shouts <reading>あらし</reading> as the whole sky misbehaves at once: a <vocabulary form="嵐">storm</vocabulary> that will last all day.

example_sentences.japanese: 嵐の夜は怖くて、全然寝られませんでした。
example_sentences.english: The stormy night was so scary that I couldn't sleep at all.
example_sentences.furigana: 嵐[あらし]の夜[よる]は怖[こわ]くて、全[ぜん]然[ぜん]寝[ね]られませんでした。

example_sentences.japanese: 嵐が来る前に、庭の椅子を家の中に入れました。
example_sentences.english: Before the storm came, I brought the garden chairs inside.
example_sentences.furigana: 嵐[あらし]が来[く]る前[まえ]に、庭[にわ]の椅[い]子[す]を家[いえ]の中[なか]に入[い]れました。

example_sentences.japanese: 嵐で電車が止まったので、会社を休みました。
example_sentences.english: The trains stopped because of the storm, so I took the day off work.
example_sentences.furigana: 嵐[あらし]で電[でん]車[しゃ]が止[と]まったので、会[かい]社[しゃ]を休[やす]みました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 台（たい）＋風（ふう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A platform (台) wind (風): a typhoon.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Give one <kanji form="風">wind</kanji> a name, a number, and its own <kanji form="台">pedestal</kanji> on every weather map, and that single most-watched storm is a <vocabulary form="台風">typhoon</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 台風の日は、外に出ないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don't go outside on typhoon days.
example_sentences.furigana: 台[たい]風[ふう]の日[ひ]は、外[そと]に出[で]ないでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 台風の風で、傘が壊れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: The typhoon wind broke my umbrella.
example_sentences.furigana: 台[たい]風[ふう]の風[かぜ]で、傘[かさ]が壊[こわ]れてしまいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 台風が来る場合は、飛行機が遅れることがあります。
example_sentences.english: When a typhoon comes, flights are sometimes delayed.
example_sentences.furigana: 台[たい]風[ふう]が来[く]る場[ば]合[あい]は、飛[ひ]行[こう]機[き]が遅[おく]れることがあります。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 地（じ）＋震（しん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The ground (地) trembling (震): an earthquake.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="地">ground</kanji> is the one thing built to stay still, so when it starts to <kanji form="震">shake</kanji> hard enough to knock cups off the shelf, you have an <vocabulary form="地震">earthquake</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 地震が起きたら、ドアを開けてください。
example_sentences.english: If an earthquake hits, please open the door.
example_sentences.furigana: 地[じ]震[しん]が起[お]きたら、ドアを開[あ]けてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 先週、小さい地震がありました。
example_sentences.english: There was a small earthquake last week.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]週[しゅう]、小[ちい]さい地[じ]震[しん]がありました。

example_sentences.japanese: 地震のたびに、猫がベッドの下に逃げます。
example_sentences.english: Every time there's an earthquake, the cat runs under the bed.
example_sentences.furigana: 地[じ]震[しん]のたびに、猫[ねこ]がベッドの下[した]に逃[に]げます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 和（わ）＋風（ふう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Harmony's (和) style (風): Japanese-style.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You already know <kanji form="和">harmony</kanji> also stands for Japan itself, and <kanji form="風">wind</kanji> can mean the air or manner of a thing. So the Japanese manner of doing something is <vocabulary form="和風">Japanese-style</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: このホテルの部屋は和風で、とても静かです。
example_sentences.english: The rooms at this hotel are Japanese-style and very quiet.
example_sentences.furigana: このホテルの部屋[へや]は和[わ]風[ふう]で、とても静[しず]かです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は和風のお菓子をよく作ります。
example_sentences.english: She often makes Japanese-style sweets.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は和[わ]風[ふう]のお菓[か]子[し]をよく作[つく]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 古い和風の家に住むのが夢です。
example_sentences.english: My dream is to live in an old Japanese-style house.
example_sentences.furigana: 古[ふる]い和[わ]風[ふう]の家[いえ]に住[す]むのが夢[ゆめ]です。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 洋（よう）＋食（しょく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Ocean-crossed (洋) food (食): Western cuisine.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="洋">ocean</kanji> here carries its other sense, foreign. So <kanji form="食">food</kanji> that came from across the water, the fried and buttery knife-and-fork kind, is <vocabulary form="洋食">Western food</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は洋食より和食のほうが好きです。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather likes Japanese food better than Western food.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は洋[よう]食[しょく]より和[わ]食[しょく]のほうが好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の前の喫茶店は、洋食もおいしいです。
example_sentences.english: The coffee shop in front of the station does good Western food, too.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]の喫[きっ]茶[さ]店[てん]は、洋[よう]食[しょく]もおいしいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は、家族で洋食を食べに行きます。
example_sentences.english: On weekends, my family goes out for Western food.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]は、家[か]族[ぞく]で洋[よう]食[しょく]を食[た]べに行[い]きます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 和（わ）＋食（しょく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Harmony's (和) food (食): Japanese cuisine.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take that same <kanji form="和">harmony</kanji> that also stands for Japan, set it in front of <kanji form="食">food</kanji>, and you have the home-side cooking of rice, fish and miso that is <vocabulary form="和食">Japanese food</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母の家に泊まると、毎朝和食が出ます。
example_sentences.english: Whenever I stay at my grandmother's, I get Japanese food every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]母[ぼ]の家[いえ]に泊[と]まると、毎[まい]朝[あさ]和[わ]食[しょく]が出[で]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は洋食ではなくて、和食にしましょう。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow, let's have Japanese food, not Western.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]は洋[よう]食[しょく]ではなくて、和[わ]食[しょく]にしましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 外国人の友人を和食の店に連れて行きました。
example_sentences.english: I took a friend from abroad to a Japanese restaurant.
example_sentences.furigana: 外[がい]国[こく]人[じん]の友[ゆう]人[じん]を和[わ]食[しょく]の店[みせ]に連[つ]れて行[い]きました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 中（ちゅう）＋華（か）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Middle (中) flower (華): Chinese style.
items.meaning_mnemonic: China's own name for itself sets the country at the <kanji form="中">middle</kanji> of the world and calls the culture there its <kanji form="華">splendor</kanji>. On a Japanese menu, <vocabulary form="中華">Chinese (cuisine)</vocabulary> is food from that middle kingdom.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅の近くに新しい中華の店ができたそうです。
example_sentences.english: I heard a new Chinese place opened near the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の近[ちか]くに新[あたら]しい中[ちゅう]華[か]の店[みせ]ができたそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 忙しい日は、中華を持ち帰ることにしています。
example_sentences.english: On busy days, I make a point of getting Chinese takeout.
example_sentences.furigana: 忙[いそが]しい日[ひ]は、中[ちゅう]華[か]を持[も]ち帰[かえ]ることにしています。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は中華料理を作るのが得意です。
example_sentences.english: My dad is great at cooking Chinese food.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は中[ちゅう]華[か]料[りょう]理[り]を作[つく]るのが得[とく]意[い]です。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Borrowed word: menyuu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A waiter at a packed diner is asked for the list of dishes by <reading>many ewe</reading> at the same moment, a whole coach tour of sheep. He keeps shouting that the <vocabulary form="メニュー">menu</vocabulary> is printed on the back of the placemat, and the sheep just bleat <reading>メニュー</reading> louder.

example_sentences.japanese: このメニューは写真が多いので、外国人にも便利です。
example_sentences.english: This menu has lots of photos, so it's handy for visitors from abroad too.
example_sentences.furigana: このメニューは写[しゃ]真[しん]が多[おお]いので、外[がい]国[こく]人[じん]にも便[べん]利[り]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 店員さんに英語のメニューがあるか聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I asked the clerk if they had an English menu.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]さんに英[えい]語[ご]のメニューがあるか聞[き]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: メニューを見ながら、娘は二十分も悩んでいます。
example_sentences.english: My daughter has been agonizing over the menu for twenty whole minutes.
example_sentences.furigana: メニューを見[み]ながら、娘[むすめ]は二[に]十[じゅう]分[ふん]も悩[なや]んでいます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 注（ちゅう）＋文（もん）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Pouring (注) a written request (文): to order.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You speak one clean <kanji form="文">sentence</kanji> across the counter, and a few minutes later a cup is <kanji form="注">poured</kanji> for you. Doing that on purpose is <vocabulary form="注文する">to order (food)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 電話でお弁当を三つ注文しました。
example_sentences.english: We ordered three boxed lunches by phone.
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]話[わ]でお弁[べん]当[とう]を三[みっ]つ注[ちゅう]文[もん]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄はいつも一番安いものを注文する。
example_sentences.english: My older brother always orders the cheapest thing.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]はいつも一[いち]番[ばん]安[やす]いものを注[ちゅう]文[もん]する。

example_sentences.japanese: 注文した料理がまだ来ていません。
example_sentences.english: The dish I ordered still hasn't come.
example_sentences.furigana: 注[ちゅう]文[もん]した料[りょう]理[り]がまだ来[き]ていません。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 甘（あま）＋み.
items.mnemonic_text: The quality (み) of sweet (甘): sweetness.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The flavour children chase and dentists warn against, the one that makes you shut your eyes at the first bite of warm cake, is <vocabulary form="甘み">sweetness</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 甘 is 「あま」 from 甘い, so the noun for that flavour, <vocabulary form="甘み">sweetness</vocabulary>, is just <reading>あまみ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬の野菜は甘みが強いです。
example_sentences.english: Winter vegetables have a strong sweetness.
example_sentences.furigana: 冬[ふゆ]の野[や]菜[さい]は甘[あま]みが強[つよ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 砂糖を入れなくても、果物の甘みで十分です。
example_sentences.english: Even without sugar, the sweetness of the fruit is enough.
example_sentences.furigana: 砂[さ]糖[とう]を入[い]れなくても、果物[くだもの]の甘[あま]みで十[じゅう]分[ぶん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんは甘みがある物が好きだそうです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently babies like things with a bit of sweetness.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A small child at the table starts to <reading>whine</reading> the moment the adults uncork the dark red bottle and fill their glasses. That guarded grown-up drink is <reading>ワイン</reading>, the <vocabulary form="ワイン">wine</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は毎晩ワインを少しだけ飲みます。
example_sentences.english: My father drinks just a little wine every night.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は毎[まい]晩[ばん]ワインを少[すこ]しだけ飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 姉が結婚したので、みんなでワインを開けました。
example_sentences.english: My sister got married, so we all opened some wine.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]が結[けっ]婚[こん]したので、みんなでワインを開[あ]けました。

example_sentences.japanese: ホテルの部屋にワインが置いてありました。

example_sentences.furigana: ホテルの部屋[へや]にワインが置[お]いてありました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 服（ふく）＋装（そう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Clothes (服) formation (装): one's outfit.
items.meaning_mnemonic: One piece of <kanji form="服">clothing</kanji> is just that one piece. The whole matching set you put on to be seen in public is your <vocabulary form="服装">attire</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の会議にはどんな服装で行けばいいですか。
example_sentences.english: What should I wear to tomorrow's meeting?
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]の会[かい]議[ぎ]にはどんな服[ふく]装[そう]で行[い]けばいいですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 山に登るときは、動きやすい服装がいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: When you climb a mountain, clothes you can move in easily are best.
example_sentences.furigana: 山[やま]に登[のぼ]るときは、動[うご]きやすい服[ふく]装[そう]がいいですよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は生徒の服装に厳しい。
example_sentences.english: The teacher is strict about how the students dress.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は生[せい]徒[と]の服[ふく]装[そう]に厳[きび]しい。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 制（せい）＋服（ふく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Regulated (制) clothing (服): a uniform.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="制">rule</kanji> book fixes every piece of this <kanji form="服">clothing</kanji>, down to the buttons. The one outfit you never get to choose for yourself is a <vocabulary form="制服">uniform</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は新しい制服を着て、嬉しそうです。
example_sentences.english: My little sister put on her new uniform and looks happy.
example_sentences.furigana: 妹[いもうと]は新[あたら]しい制[せい]服[ふく]を着[き]て、嬉[うれ]しそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 夏になると、駅員の制服が変わります。
example_sentences.english: When summer comes, the station staff's uniforms change.
example_sentences.furigana: 夏[なつ]になると、駅[えき]員[いん]の制[せい]服[ふく]が変[か]わります。

example_sentences.japanese: 雨で制服が濡れてしまったので、乾かしました。
example_sentences.english: My uniform got soaked in the rain, so I dried it.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]で制[せい]服[ふく]が濡[ぬ]れてしまったので、乾[かわ]かしました。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Every morning you loop a silk strip around your neck and tie it in a snug knot. That plain <reading>neck tie</reading> is a <reading>ネクタイ</reading>, a <vocabulary form="ネクタイ">necktie</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子のネクタイが曲がっていたので、直してあげた。

example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]のネクタイが曲[ま]がっていたので、直[なお]してあげた。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Borrowed word: sukaato.
items.meaning_mnemonic: To <reading>skirt</reading> a puddle you swing wide around its edge. Swing your hips that way as you walk and the loose cloth that flares out from your waist is a <reading>スカート</reading>, a <vocabulary form="スカート">skirt</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: 風[かぜ]が強[つよ]いので、今日[きょう]はスカートじゃなくてズボンにします。

example_sentences.japanese: このスカートは少しきついので、取り替えたいです。
example_sentences.english: This skirt is a little tight, so I'd like to exchange it.
example_sentences.furigana: このスカートは少[すこ]しきついので、取[と]り替[か]えたいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 娘のスカートを洗濯したら、小さくなった。
example_sentences.english: I washed my daughter's skirt and it shrank.
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]のスカートを洗[せん]濯[たく]したら、小[ちい]さくなった。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Borrowed word (from French): zubon.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Sit down, feed one leg in and then the other, and <reading>zip on</reading> the two cloth tubes. Fastened at your waist, that pair of tubes is <reading>ズボン</reading>, your <vocabulary form="ズボン">trousers</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: このズボンは長すぎるので、短くしてもらった。
example_sentences.english: These trousers were too long, so I had them shortened.
example_sentences.furigana: このズボンは長[なが]すぎるので、短[みじか]くしてもらった。

example_sentences.japanese: 自転車に乗るときは、ズボンのほうが便利です。
example_sentences.english: Trousers are more practical when you ride a bike.
example_sentences.furigana: 自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]に乗[の]るときは、ズボンのほうが便[べん]利[り]です。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Pull the thick wool top down over your head and within a minute you start to <reading>sweat</reading>. The heavy knitted layer that does that to you is a <reading>セーター</reading>, a <vocabulary form="セーター">sweater</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は冬[ふゆ]になると、同[おな]じ茶[ちゃ]色[いろ]のセーターを毎[まい]日[にち]着[き]ている。

example_sentences.japanese: 夜は寒いかもしれないから、セーターを持って行って。
example_sentences.english: It might get cold at night, so take a sweater.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]は寒[さむ]いかもしれないから、セーターを持[も]って行[い]って。

example_sentences.furigana: このセーターを着[き]ると、首[くび]が痒[かゆ]くなる。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 靴（くつ）＋下（した）.
items.mnemonic_text: Under (下) the shoes (靴): socks.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Hidden <kanji form="下">below</kanji> your <kanji form="靴">shoes</kanji> all day where nobody sees them, wrapped straight onto the foot, are your <vocabulary form="靴下">socks</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨で靴下が濡れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: My socks got soaked in the rain.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]で靴[くつ]下[した]が濡[ぬ]れてしまいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 洗濯した後で、白い靴下が見つかりません。
example_sentences.english: After doing the laundry, I can't find my white socks.
example_sentences.furigana: 洗[せん]濯[たく]した後[あと]で、白[しろ]い靴[くつ]下[した]が見[み]つかりません。

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は赤い靴下が一番好きです。

example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は赤[あか]い靴[くつ]下[した]が一[いち]番[ばん]好[す]きです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 手（て）＋袋（ぶくろ）. Rendaku: 袋 ふくろ → ぶくろ.
items.mnemonic_text: A bag (袋) for the hand (手): gloves.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A snug <kanji form="袋">sack</kanji> sewn to the shape of a <kanji form="手">hand</kanji>, with a separate slot for each finger, is one of a pair of <vocabulary form="手袋">gloves</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 自転車に乗るときは、手袋をしたほうがいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: When you ride a bike, you should wear gloves.
example_sentences.furigana: 自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]に乗[の]るときは、手[て]袋[ぶくろ]をしたほうがいいですよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 公園で小さい手袋を見つけたので、交番に届けました。
example_sentences.english: I found a small glove in the park, so I took it to the police box.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]で小[ちい]さい手[て]袋[ぶくろ]を見[み]つけたので、交[こう]番[ばん]に届[とど]けました。

example_sentences.japanese: この手袋は古いのに、とても暖かいです。
example_sentences.english: These gloves are old, but they're still really warm.
example_sentences.furigana: この手[て]袋[ぶくろ]は古[ふる]いのに、とても暖[あたた]かいです。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 指（ゆび）＋輪（わ）.
items.mnemonic_text: A ring (輪) for the finger (指): a ring.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A metal band sized to slide onto one <kanji form="指">finger</kanji> and stay there is a <vocabulary form="指輪">ring</vocabulary> you wear as jewelry.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫は結婚した日に、この指輪をくれました。
example_sentences.english: My husband gave me this ring on the day we got married.
example_sentences.furigana: 夫[おっと]は結[けっ]婚[こん]した日[ひ]に、この指[ゆび]輪[わ]をくれました。

example_sentences.japanese: 料理する前に、指輪を取って箱に入れます。
example_sentences.english: Before I cook, I take off my ring and put it in a box.
example_sentences.furigana: 料[りょう]理[り]する前[まえ]に、指[ゆび]輪[わ]を取[と]って箱[はこ]に入[い]れます。

example_sentences.japanese: 砂の中に指輪を落として、みんなで探しました。
example_sentences.english: I dropped my ring in the sand, and we all searched for it.
example_sentences.furigana: 砂[すな]の中[なか]に指[ゆび]輪[わ]を落[お]として、みんなで探[さが]しました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Borrowed word: nekkuresu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Slip the jewelled chain off your collarbones and the bare skin leaves your <reading>neck less</reading> dressed than before. Put the chain back to fix that and you are wearing a <reading>ネックレス</reading>, a <vocabulary form="ネックレス">necklace</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫がネックレスで遊んでいます。

example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]がネックレスで遊[あそ]んでいます。

example_sentences.japanese: このネックレスは高すぎて、買うことができません。
example_sentences.english: This necklace is too expensive for me to buy.
example_sentences.furigana: このネックレスは高[たか]すぎて、買[か]うことができません。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Borrowed word: baggu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Load a leather shoulder <reading>bag</reading> with your purse, phone and keys until its sides go round and firm. Carried as part of an outfit, that piece is a <reading>バッグ</reading>, a <vocabulary form="バッグ">bag</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: 財[さい]布[ふ]と携[けい]帯[たい]と鍵[かぎ]を、小[ちい]さいバッグに入[い]れて出[で]かけました。

example_sentences.japanese: その素敵なバッグは、どこで買いましたか。
example_sentences.english: Where did you buy that lovely bag?
example_sentences.furigana: その素[す]敵[てき]なバッグは、どこで買[か]いましたか。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Borrowed word: saizu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The tailor runs the tape around your chest, reads the number, and <reading>sighs</reading>. That number, how big your clothes have to be, is your <reading>サイズ</reading>, your <vocabulary form="サイズ">size</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.english: I got the box size wrong, and the things wouldn't fit.
example_sentences.furigana: 箱[はこ]のサイズを間[ま]違[ちが]えて、荷[に]物[もつ]が入[はい]りませんでした。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — わりびき cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 割引.
items.mnemonic_text: Splitting (割) and pulling (引) off the price: a discount.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Cut the price into equal <kanji form="割">proportion</kanji>s, then <kanji form="引">pull</kanji> a few of those parts away before you pay. The parts pulled off the total are the <vocabulary form="割引">discount</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Wally Becky</reading> the cashier cuts your bill into equal parts and pulls a few away before you pay, singing <reading>わりびき</reading>: those missing parts are your <vocabulary form="割引">discount</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎週水曜日は、映画館の割引の日です。
example_sentences.english: Every Wednesday is discount day at the cinema.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]週[しゅう]水[すい]曜[よう]日[び]は、映[えい]画[が]館[かん]の割[わり]引[びき]の日[ひ]です。

example_sentences.english: When night comes, the supermarket's boxed lunches get discounted.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]になると、スーパーの弁[べん]当[とう]は割[わり]引[びき]になります。

example_sentences.furigana: この割[わり]引[びき]は、来[らい]月[げつ]まで使[つか]うことができます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 売（う）＋り＋場（ば）.
items.mnemonic_text: A place (場) to sell (売る): a sales counter.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The lit patch of <kanji form="場">place</kanji> on a shop floor where the staff do nothing but <kanji form="売">sell</kanji> one kind of goods is that department's <vocabulary form="売り場">sales floor</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.english: The clerk in the produce section is really kind.
example_sentences.furigana: 野[や]菜[さい]売[う]り場[ば]の店[てん]員[いん]は、とても親[しん]切[せつ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: デパートの地下の食べ物売り場は、いつも賑やかです。
example_sentences.english: The food floor in the department store basement is always busy.
example_sentences.furigana: デパートの地[ち]下[か]の食[た]べ物[もの]売[う]り場[ば]は、いつも賑[にぎ]やかです。

example_sentences.japanese: エスカレーターを降りると、すぐ右にかばん売り場があります。
example_sentences.english: Step off the escalator and the bag counter is right there on your right.
example_sentences.furigana: エスカレーターを降[お]りると、すぐ右[みぎ]にかばん売[う]り場[ば]があります。

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 支（し）on'yomi ＋ 払（はら）kun'yomi ＋ う.
items.mnemonic_text: Supporting (支) and paying (払う): to settle a bill.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Handing a shop the exact money you owe helps <kanji form="支">support</kanji> it for another day. The formal verb for passing that money across the counter is <vocabulary form="支払う">to pay</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 税金は来週までに支払わなければなりません。
example_sentences.english: The tax has to be paid by next week.

example_sentences.japanese: 食事のお金は、父が支払ってくれました。

items.mnemonic_text: Governing (領) collection (収): a formal receipt.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Once the shop has <kanji form="収">reaped</kanji> your payment into its own <kanji form="領">territory</kanji>, it hands you a slip proving the money changed hands. That slip is a <vocabulary form="領収">receipt</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.english: My drawer is full of old receipts.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬が領収書を食べてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: The dog ate my receipt.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]が領[りょう]収[しゅう]書[しょ]を食[た]べてしまいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 領収書の名前は、会社の名前にしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please put the company name on the receipt.
example_sentences.furigana: 領[りょう]収[しゅう]書[しょ]の名[な]前[まえ]は、会[かい]社[しゃ]の名[な]前[まえ]にしてください。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 注（ちゅう）＋文（もん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Pouring (注) a written request (文): an order.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="注">pour</kanji> one clear <kanji form="文">sentence</kanji> across the counter, telling the shop exactly what you want. That sentence is your <vocabulary form="注文">order</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: 店[てん]員[いん]が注[ちゅう]文[もん]を間[ま]違[ちが]えて、カレーが来[き]ました。

example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]の注[ちゅう]文[もん]はいつも同[おな]じラーメンなんです。

example_sentences.japanese: 電話で弁当の注文をしました。
example_sentences.english: I placed an order for boxed lunches over the phone.
example_sentences.furigana: 電[でん]話[わ]で弁[べん]当[とう]の注[ちゅう]文[もん]をしました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 交（こう）＋換（かん）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Crossing (交) a change (換): to exchange.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Two people let their goods <kanji form="交">mingle</kanji> on the table, then <kanji form="換">change</kanji> which one each takes home. What they do is <vocabulary form="交換する">to exchange</vocabulary> them.

example_sentences.japanese: サイズが小さかったので、靴を交換しました。
example_sentences.english: The shoes were too small, so I exchanged them.
example_sentences.furigana: サイズが小[ちい]さかったので、靴[くつ]を交[こう]換[かん]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅で会った人と電話番号を交換した。
example_sentences.english: I swapped phone numbers with someone I met at the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]で会[あ]った人[ひと]と電[でん]話[わ]番[ばん]号[ごう]を交[こう]換[かん]した。

example_sentences.japanese: 時計が壊れているので、新しいのと交換してください。
example_sentences.english: This watch is broken, so please exchange it for a new one.
example_sentences.furigana: 時計[とけい]が壊[こわ]れているので、新[あたら]しいのと交[こう]換[かん]してください。

items.word_type: する verb, transitive verb, intransitive verb
items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 返（へん）＋品（ぴん）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Handakuon: 品 ひん → ぴん.
items.mnemonic_text: Returning (返) the goods (品): to return an item.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You carry the <kanji form="品">goods</kanji> back to the counter that sold them and hand them over for a refund. Doing that is <vocabulary form="返品する">to return an item</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 領収書がないと、返品することができません。
example_sentences.english: Without the receipt, you can't return the item.
example_sentences.furigana: 領[りょう]収[しゅう]書[しょ]がないと、返[へん]品[ぴん]することができません。

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は買ったばかりのバッグを返品しました。
example_sentences.english: My sister returned the bag she had only just bought.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]は買[か]ったばかりのバッグを返[へん]品[ぴん]しました。

example_sentences.japanese: 間違えて注文した本を返品しました。
example_sentences.english: I returned a book I had ordered by mistake.
example_sentences.furigana: 間[ま]違[ちが]えて注[ちゅう]文[もん]した本[ほん]を返[へん]品[ぴん]しました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 健（けん）＋康（こう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Strong (健) and peaceful (康): good health.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When every part of your body has settled into <kanji form="康">ease</kanji> and nothing in it aches or strains, the single word for that whole calm state is <vocabulary form="健康">health</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は健康のために毎日一時間歩いています。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather walks for an hour every day for his health.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は健[けん]康[こう]のために毎[まい]日[にち]一[いち]時[じ]間[かん]歩[ある]いています。

example_sentences.japanese: お酒を飲みすぎるのは健康に悪いですよ。
example_sentences.english: Drinking too much is bad for your health, you know.
example_sentences.furigana: お酒[さけ]を飲[の]みすぎるのは健[けん]康[こう]に悪[わる]いですよ。

example_sentences.japanese: 医者と自分の健康について話しました。
example_sentences.english: I talked with the doctor about my own health.
example_sentences.furigana: 医[い]者[しゃ]と自[じ]分[ぶん]の健[けん]康[こう]について話[はな]しました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 体（たい）＋重（じゅう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The body's (体) heaviness (重): body weight.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Step on a scale and it tells you one thing: how <kanji form="重">heavy</kanji> the <kanji form="体">body</kanji> you carry around all day has become. That one number is your <vocabulary form="体重">body weight</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬の間に体重が増えてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I put on weight over the winter.
example_sentences.furigana: 冬[ふゆ]の間[あいだ]に体[たい]重[じゅう]が増[ふ]えてしまった。

example_sentences.japanese: 医者によると、うちの猫は体重が重すぎるそうです。
example_sentences.english: According to the vet, our cat weighs too much.
example_sentences.furigana: 医[い]者[しゃ]によると、うちの猫[ねこ]は体[たい]重[じゅう]が重[おも]すぎるそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 甘い物を食べなくなったら、体重が減りました。
example_sentences.english: Once I stopped eating sweets, my weight went down.
example_sentences.furigana: 甘[あま]い物[もの]を食[た]べなくなったら、体[たい]重[じゅう]が減[へ]りました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 身（しん）＋長（ちょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The body's (身) length (長): one's height.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Stand a <kanji form="身">person</kanji> against the wall and measure how <kanji form="長">long</kanji> they are from heel to crown. That measurement is their <vocabulary form="身長">height (body)</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は去年より身長が高くなりました。
example_sentences.english: My little brother is taller than he was last year.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は去[きょ]年[ねん]より身[しん]長[ちょう]が高[たか]くなりました。

example_sentences.japanese: この紙に名前と身長を書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write your name and height on this sheet.
example_sentences.furigana: この紙[かみ]に名[な]前[まえ]と身[しん]長[ちょう]を書[か]いてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 友人と身長が同じなので、よく服を借ります。
example_sentences.english: My friend and I are the same height, so I often borrow their clothes.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[ゆう]人[じん]と身[しん]長[ちょう]が同[おな]じなので、よく服[ふく]を借[か]ります。

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 熱（ねつ）.
items.mnemonic_text: A hot (熱) burning inside: a fever.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Lay the back of your hand on a sick child's forehead and it comes away warm, like a pebble left out in full sun. That trapped warmth pouring off the skin is a <vocabulary form="熱">fever / heat</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 熱があるので、今日は早く寝ます。
example_sentences.english: I have a fever, so I'm going to bed early tonight.
example_sentences.furigana: 熱[ねつ]があるので、今日[きょう]は早[はや]く寝[ね]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんの熱が夜になっても下がらない。
example_sentences.english: The baby's fever still hasn't come down, even now that it's night.
example_sentences.furigana: 赤[あか]ちゃんの熱[ねつ]が夜[よる]になっても下[さ]がらない。

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンが熱を持って、動かなくなった。
example_sentences.english: The computer got hot and stopped working.
example_sentences.furigana: パソコンが熱[ねつ]を持[も]って、動[うご]かなくなった。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 咳（せき）.
items.mnemonic_text: A mouth (口) releasing air suddenly: a cough.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A hard bark of air fires up your throat with no warning and rattles the whole quiet room. That sharp, helpless burst is a <vocabulary form="咳">cough</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The quiet room is silent until a hard bark of air fires up the reader's throat and lands like a dropped <reading>sack</reading>, <reading>せき</reading>, rattling every window: a <vocabulary form="咳">cough</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜になると咳が止まらないんです。
example_sentences.english: Once night comes, my cough just won't stop.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]になると咳[せき]が止[と]まらないんです。

example_sentences.japanese: 映画館で隣の人が何回も咳をしていた。
example_sentences.english: The person next to me at the cinema kept coughing.
example_sentences.furigana: 映[えい]画[が]館[かん]で隣[となり]の人[ひと]が何[なん]回[かい]も咳[せき]をしていた。

example_sentences.japanese: 咳が出るときは、熱いお茶を飲むといいですよ。
example_sentences.english: When you have a cough, hot tea helps.
example_sentences.furigana: 咳[せき]が出[で]るときは、熱[あつ]いお茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]むといいですよ。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — かぜをひく cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 風邪をひく.
items.mnemonic_text: Pulling (引く) the cold wind (風邪) in: to catch a cold.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pull a <kanji form="邪">wicked</kanji> <kanji form="風">wind</kanji> deep into your chest and let it settle in as a three-day fever. Drawing bad air right inside you like that is what it means <vocabulary form="風邪をひく">to catch a cold</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A cold gust off the river hooks Kaz like a fish on a line and reels him straight into bed. When chilled air <reading>hooks</reading> into you and holds on, that is <reading>かぜをひく</reading>, <vocabulary form="風邪をひく">to catch a cold</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨に濡れて、風邪をひいてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I got caught in the rain and ended up catching a cold.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]に濡[ぬ]れて、風邪[かぜ]をひいてしまった。

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪をひかないように、コートを着て出かけましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's put our coats on before we go out so we don't catch a cold.
example_sentences.furigana: 風邪[かぜ]をひかないように、コートを着[き]て出[で]かけましょう。

example_sentences.japanese: 娘が風邪をひいたので、会社を休みました。
example_sentences.english: My daughter caught a cold, so I took the day off work.
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]が風邪[かぜ]をひいたので、会[かい]社[しゃ]を休[やす]みました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 治（ち）＋療（りょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Governing (治) and healing (療): treatment.
items.meaning_mnemonic: First you get the disease to <kanji form="治">calm down</kanji>, then you <kanji form="療">heal</kanji> the damage it left behind. Doing both of those, in that order, is <vocabulary form="治療">medical treatment</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この病気の治療には時間がかかります。
example_sentences.english: Treating this illness takes time.
example_sentences.furigana: この病[びょう]気[き]の治[ち]療[りょう]には時[じ]間[かん]がかかります。

example_sentences.japanese: 医者の治療が良かったので、すぐ治りました。
example_sentences.english: The doctor's treatment was good, so I got better quickly.
example_sentences.furigana: 医[い]者[しゃ]の治[ち]療[りょう]が良[よ]かったので、すぐ治[なお]りました。

example_sentences.japanese: 犬の治療に三万円も払いました。
example_sentences.english: I paid a whole thirty thousand yen for the dog's treatment.
example_sentences.furigana: 犬[いぬ]の治[ち]療[りょう]に三[さん]万[まん]円[えん]も払[はら]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 注（ちゅう）＋射（しゃ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Pouring (注) a shot (射): an injection.
items.meaning_mnemonic: An <vocabulary form="注射">injection</vocabulary> is a dose <kanji form="射">shot</kanji> through a thin needle so it <kanji form="注">pours</kanji> straight into your blood instead of going down your throat.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供は注射が嫌いで、病院で泣いてしまった。
example_sentences.english: My kid hates shots and ended up crying at the hospital.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]は注[ちゅう]射[しゃ]が嫌[きら]いで、病[びょう]院[いん]で泣[な]いてしまった。

example_sentences.japanese: 注射は思ったより痛くなかったです。
example_sentences.english: The shot hurt less than I expected.
example_sentences.furigana: 注[ちゅう]射[しゃ]は思[おも]ったより痛[いた]くなかったです。

example_sentences.japanese: 猫に注射をするのは本当に大変です。
example_sentences.english: Giving a cat a shot is a real struggle.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]に注[ちゅう]射[しゃ]をするのは本[ほん]当[とう]に大[たい]変[へん]です。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 手（しゅ）＋術（じゅつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A hand's (手) craft (術): surgery.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <vocabulary form="手術">surgery</vocabulary> is a trained <kanji form="手">hand</kanji> putting every bit of its learned <kanji form="術">technique</kanji> to work inside a body that has been opened up.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は来週、目の手術をすることになった。
example_sentences.english: It's been decided that my grandfather will have eye surgery next week.
example_sentences.furigana: 祖[そ]父[ふ]は来[らい]週[しゅう]、目[め]の手[しゅ]術[じゅつ]をすることになった。

example_sentences.japanese: 手術の前の日は、何も食べてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You can't eat anything the day before surgery.
example_sentences.furigana: 手[しゅ]術[じゅつ]の前[まえ]の日[ひ]は、何[なに]も食[た]べてはいけません。

example_sentences.japanese: 手術が終わるまで、母は静かに待っていました。
example_sentences.english: My mother waited quietly until the surgery was over.
example_sentences.furigana: 手[しゅ]術[じゅつ]が終[お]わるまで、母[はは]は静[しず]かに待[ま]っていました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 入（にゅう）＋院（いん）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Entering (入) the hospital (院): to be admitted.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="入">enter</kanji> the medical <kanji form="院">institution</kanji> as a patient, the doors fall shut, and you are not sleeping at home tonight. Ending up kept inside like that is what it means <vocabulary form="入院する">to be hospitalized</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は自転車から落ちて、一週間入院した。
example_sentences.english: My little brother fell off his bike and spent a week in the hospital.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]は自[じ]転[てん]車[しゃ]から落[お]ちて、一[いっ]週[しゅう]間[かん]入[にゅう]院[いん]した。

example_sentences.japanese: 入院している間、毎日、本を読んでいました。
example_sentences.english: While I was in the hospital, I read books every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 入[にゅう]院[いん]している間[あいだ]、毎[まい]日[にち]、本[ほん]を読[よ]んでいました。

example_sentences.japanese: 入院するなら、何を持って行けばいいですか。
example_sentences.english: If I'm going into the hospital, what should I bring?
example_sentences.furigana: 入[にゅう]院[いん]するなら、何[なに]を持[も]って行[い]けばいいですか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 退（たい）＋院（いん）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Retreating (退) from the hospital (院): to be discharged.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The morning you can finally stand on your own, you <kanji form="退">withdraw</kanji> from the <kanji form="院">institution</kanji> and walk back out to the street. Getting yourself out the doors like that is <vocabulary form="退院する">to leave hospital</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の人は明日退院するそうです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently the person in the next bed is leaving the hospital tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 隣[となり]の人[ひと]は明日[あした]退[たい]院[いん]するそうです。

example_sentences.japanese: 退院した日に、ラーメンを食べに行った。
example_sentences.english: The day I got out of the hospital, I went out for ramen.
example_sentences.furigana: 退[たい]院[いん]した日[ひ]に、ラーメンを食[た]べに行[い]った。

example_sentences.japanese: 夫が退院する前に、部屋を掃除しておきます。
example_sentences.english: I'll clean the room before my husband comes home from the hospital.
example_sentences.furigana: 夫[おっと]が退[たい]院[いん]する前[まえ]に、部屋[へや]を掃[そう]除[じ]しておきます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 健（けん）＋康（こう）＋診（しん）＋断（だん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A health (健康) diagnosis (診断): a checkup.
items.furigana: 健[けん]康[こう]診[しん]断[だん]
items.meaning_mnemonic: Once a year a doctor checks whether every part of you is running at <kanji form="康">ease</kanji>, then draws a firm <kanji form="断">severance</kanji> line between what passed and what a specialist must chase. That whole yearly review is a <vocabulary form="健康診断">health checkup</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社の健康診断は毎年四月にあります。
example_sentences.english: The company health checkup is every April.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]社[しゃ]の健[けん]康[こう]診[しん]断[だん]は毎[まい]年[ねん]四[よん]月[がつ]にあります。

example_sentences.japanese: 健康診断で、体重が増えたのが分かった。
example_sentences.english: My checkup showed that I'd put on weight.
example_sentences.furigana: 健[けん]康[こう]診[しん]断[だん]で、体[たい]重[じゅう]が増[ふ]えたのが分[わ]かった。

example_sentences.japanese: 健康診断の結果が悪くて、兄はお酒を減らした。
example_sentences.english: My older brother's checkup results were bad, so he cut back on drinking.
example_sentences.furigana: 健[けん]康[こう]診[しん]断[だん]の結[けっ]果[か]が悪[わる]くて、兄[あに]はお酒[さけ]を減[へ]らした。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 薬（くすり）＋を＋飲（の）＋む.
items.mnemonic_text: Drinking (飲む) the medicine (薬): to take medicine.
items.meaning_mnemonic: English says you take a pill; Japanese says you <kanji form="飲">drink</kanji> it. So even a dry tablet of <kanji form="薬">medicine</kanji> goes down the same way water does, and that is what it means <vocabulary form="薬を飲む">to take medicine</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 水と一緒に、この薬を飲んでください。
example_sentences.english: Please take this medicine with water.
example_sentences.furigana: 水[みず]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に、この薬[くすり]を飲[の]んでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は咳が止まらないので、毎晩薬を飲んでいる。
example_sentences.english: My older sister can't stop coughing, so she takes medicine every night.
example_sentences.furigana: 姉[あね]は咳[せき]が止[と]まらないので、毎[まい]晩[ばん]薬[くすり]を飲[の]んでいる。

example_sentences.japanese: 苦い薬を飲んだ後で、チョコレートを食べた。
example_sentences.english: After taking the bitter medicine, I ate some chocolate.
example_sentences.furigana: 苦[にが]い薬[くすり]を飲[の]んだ後[あと]で、チョコレートを食[た]べた。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 怪（け）＋我（が）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A mysterious (怪) loss (我): an injury.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="怪">mysterious</kanji> shape swings out of the dark and catches the one <kanji form="我">self</kanji> you were busy minding. Whatever it leaves on you afterward, a gash or a sprain or a spreading bruise, is an <vocabulary form="怪我">injury</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟の怪我は軽いので、明日から学校に行けます。
example_sentences.english: My little brother's injury is minor, so he can go back to school tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 弟[おとうと]の怪[け]我[が]は軽[かる]いので、明日[あした]から学[がっ]校[こう]に行[い]けます。

example_sentences.japanese: 足の怪我が治るまで、走ってはいけないと医者に言われました。
example_sentences.english: The doctor told me not to run until my leg injury heals.
example_sentences.furigana: 足[あし]の怪[け]我[が]が治[なお]るまで、走[はし]ってはいけないと医[い]者[しゃ]に言[い]われました。

example_sentences.japanese: 「怪我はありませんか」と駅員が聞きました。
example_sentences.english: "Are you hurt?" the station attendant asked.
example_sentences.furigana: 「怪[け]我[が]はありませんか」と駅[えき]員[いん]が聞[き]きました。

items.word_type: する verb, transitive verb, intransitive verb
items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 怪（け）＋我（が）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Suffering a mysterious loss: to be injured.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When a <kanji form="怪">suspicious</kanji> force blindsides your own <kanji form="我">self</kanji> and something tears or swells with nobody's hand on it, that event is what it means <vocabulary form="怪我する">to get injured</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: ナイフで野菜を切るときは、怪我しやすいです。

example_sentences.furigana: ナイフで野[や]菜[さい]を切[き]るときは、怪[け]我[が]しやすいです。

example_sentences.english: I found an injured bird in the garden.
example_sentences.furigana: 庭[にわ]で怪[け]我[が]している鳥[とり]を見[み]つけました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 痛（いた）＋む.
items.mnemonic_text: A sickness (疒) piercing through steadily: to ache.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A back tooth starts to throb late at night with nobody near it and nothing pressing on it. When a part of you sends up that steady, unasked-for pain on its own, it has begun <vocabulary form="痛む">to hurt / ache</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already know 痛 is 「いた」 from 痛い, so for a sore knee <vocabulary form="痛む">to hurt / ache</vocabulary> on its own is <reading>いたむ</reading>.

example_sentences.furigana: 冷[つめ]たいジュースを飲[の]みすぎて、お腹[なか]が痛[いた]みます。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 目（め）＋が＋悪（わる）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: The eyes (目) being bad (悪い): poor vision.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When the <kanji form="目">eye</kanji> itself has gone <kanji form="悪">bad</kanji> and anything past your own arm is a blur, that is <vocabulary form="目が悪い">to have poor eyesight</vocabulary>. The final い is the ending that makes it an adjective.

example_sentences.english: My father has poor eyesight, so he doesn't drive at night.

example_sentences.japanese: 暗い所で本を読むと、目が悪くなりますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you read in the dark, your eyesight will get worse.
example_sentences.furigana: 暗[くら]い所[ところ]で本[ほん]を読[よ]むと、目[め]が悪[わる]くなりますよ。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 耳（みみ）＋が＋遠（とお）＋い.
items.mnemonic_text: The ears (耳) being far (遠い): hard of hearing.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your <kanji form="耳">ear</kanji> still works, but every sound now has to cross a long <kanji form="遠">distant</kanji> road to reach it and arrives faint. Sound landing that far off is <vocabulary form="耳が遠い">to be hard of hearing</vocabulary>, and the closing い marks it as an adjective.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父は耳が遠いので、電話より手紙のほうが好きです。
example_sentences.english: My uncle is hard of hearing, so he prefers letters to phone calls.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔父[おじ]は耳[みみ]が遠[とお]いので、電[でん]話[わ]より手[て]紙[がみ]のほうが好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は耳が遠くなってから、声が大きくなりました。
example_sentences.english: Ever since my mother started losing her hearing, her voice has gotten louder.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は耳[みみ]が遠[とお]くなってから、声[こえ]が大[おお]きくなりました。

example_sentences.japanese: 耳が遠いはずの彼が、私たちの話を全部聞いていました。
example_sentences.english: He's supposed to be hard of hearing, but he heard every word we said.
example_sentences.furigana: 耳[みみ]が遠[とお]いはずの彼[かれ]が、私[わたし]たちの話[はなし]を全[ぜん]部[ぶ]聞[き]いていました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 運（うん）＋動（どう）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Carrying (運) motion (動): to exercise.
items.meaning_mnemonic: What it means <vocabulary form="運動する">to exercise</vocabulary> is to <kanji form="運">carry</kanji> your own body through enough hard <kanji form="動">motion</kanji> to leave you breathless.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動しすぎて、次の日は階段を上がるのが大変でした。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 野（や）＋球（きゅう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Field (野) ball (球): baseball.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take the open <kanji form="野">field</kanji> the village never fenced, add one hard <kanji form="球">ball</kanji> and nine leather gloves, and the game they play out there is <vocabulary form="野球">baseball</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 父と兄はテレビで野球を見ながら、晩ご飯を食べています。

example_sentences.english: Baseball is a sport played by nine people.
example_sentences.furigana: 野[や]球[きゅう]は九[きゅう]人[にん]でするスポーツです。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Borrowed word: sakkaa.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Borrowed word: sukii.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Strap two long boards to your boots, point the tips downhill, and let them run over the snow with a <reading>squeaky</reading> hiss all the way to the bottom. That boarded slide is <vocabulary form="スキー">skiing</vocabulary>, <reading>スキー</reading>.
