items.meaning_mnemonic: The raccoon works the alley bins like a <reading>gourmet</reading> picking a buffet, but every fish skeleton, mouldy rice ball, and coffee filter it drags out is just <vocabulary form="ごみ">trash / garbage</vocabulary>. The raccoon's five-star spread is <reading>ごみ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: ごみは朝早く出してください。
example_sentences.english: Please put the trash out early in the morning.
example_sentences.furigana: ごみは朝[あさ]早[はや]く出[だ]してください。

example_sentences.japanese: 燃えるごみは月曜日です。
example_sentences.english: Burnable trash goes out on Mondays.
example_sentences.furigana: 燃[も]えるごみは月[げつ]曜[よう]日[び]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 海岸には、ごみがたくさん落ちていました。
example_sentences.english: There was a lot of trash lying on the beach.
example_sentences.furigana: 海[かい]岸[がん]には、ごみがたくさん落[お]ちていました。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — ごみ＋箱（ばこ）. Rendaku: 箱 はこ → ばこ.
items.mnemonic_text: A box (箱) for trash (ごみ): a trash can.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="箱">box</kanji> whose only job is to hold the trash you throw out all day is a <vocabulary form="ごみ箱">trash can</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: By evening the box that holds everything you threw out all day has gone sticky, a <reading>gummy bucket</reading> of wrappers, <reading>ごみばこ</reading>, so you drag your <vocabulary form="ごみ箱">trash can</vocabulary> to the curb.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫がごみ箱の中で寝ていました。
example_sentences.english: The cat was asleep inside the trash can.
example_sentences.furigana: 猫[ねこ]がごみ箱[ばこ]の中[なか]で寝[ね]ていました。

example_sentences.japanese: ごみ箱に入れる前に、よく洗ってください。
example_sentences.english: Rinse it well before you put it in the bin.
example_sentences.furigana: ごみ箱[ばこ]に入[い]れる前[まえ]に、よく洗[あら]ってください。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅のごみ箱が減って、不便になりました。
example_sentences.english: The station has fewer trash cans now, which is a pain.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]のごみ箱[ばこ]が減[へ]って、不[ふ]便[べん]になりました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Borrowed word: risaikuru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <reading>Lisa cycles</reading> one loop over and over: bottle bank, crusher, shop, back to the bottle bank. Running that same can around the circle until it becomes a brand-new can is <vocabulary form="リサイクル">recycling</vocabulary>, the loop you hear in <reading>リサイクル</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 着なくなった服は、リサイクルに出しています。
example_sentences.english: I send clothes I no longer wear off to be recycled.
example_sentences.furigana: 着[き]なくなった服[ふく]は、リサイクルに出[だ]しています。

example_sentences.japanese: リサイクルで、ごみを減らすことができます。
example_sentences.english: Recycling lets us cut down on trash.
example_sentences.furigana: リサイクルで、ごみを減[へ]らすことができます。

example_sentences.japanese: このノートは、リサイクルの紙で作りました。
example_sentences.english: This notebook is made from recycled paper.
example_sentences.furigana: このノートは、リサイクルの紙[かみ]で作[つく]りました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: そう (so) + いう (say): the kind you just said.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At Koichi's konbini, the cashier eyes your fish-and-banana sandwich and asks, “<reading>So, you</reading> eat <vocabulary form="そういう">that kind of</vocabulary> thing?” His <reading>そういう</reading> points at the odd thing on your side of the till, never at anything on his.
items.description: It always sits right before a noun. It points at things near the listener, and very often back at something the other person just said.

example_sentences.japanese: 私もそういう映画が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like that kind of movie too.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]もそういう映[えい]画[が]が好[す]きです。

example_sentences.japanese: そういう話は先生に聞いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please ask the teacher about that sort of thing.
example_sentences.furigana: そういう話[はなし]は先[せん]生[せい]に聞[き]いてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄はいつもそういう服を着ています。
example_sentences.english: My older brother always wears clothes like that.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[あに]はいつもそういう服[ふく]を着[き]ています。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: こう (like this) + いう (say): this kind.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the riverbank, Sei hugs a wriggling fish to her chest and says, “<reading>Koi, you</reading> see, are <vocabulary form="こういう">this kind of</vocabulary> fish.” Its tail slaps her cheek the whole time, because <reading>こういう</reading> is for things that close to you.
items.description: It always sits right before a noun. It points at things near the speaker, and often ahead at something the speaker is about to show or explain.

example_sentences.japanese: こういう靴はどこで売っていますか。
example_sentences.english: Where do they sell shoes like these?
example_sentences.furigana: こういう靴[くつ]はどこで売[う]っていますか。

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の日は、こういう傘があると便利です。
example_sentences.english: On rainy days, an umbrella like this comes in handy.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]は、こういう傘[かさ]があると便[べん]利[り]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 母はこういう甘いお菓子をよく作ってくれました。
example_sentences.english: My mom often made me sweets like this.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]はこういう甘[あま]いお菓[か]子[し]をよく作[つく]ってくれました。
